name: NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp
doc:
An **Arnoldi decomposition** of `(A, b)` of size `q`: a matrix `Q` whose columns form a graded
orthonormal Krylov basis. The compression `H = Qᵀ A Q` is `ArnoldiDecomp.H`; for symmetric `A`
the same object is a `LanczosDecomp` with `T = H`. Exists iff `q ≤ krylovGrade A b`
(`arnoldiDecomp`, `IsGradedKrylovBasis.le_krylovGrade`); unique up to column signs
(`ArnoldiDecomp.exists_sign`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.3 (Alg. 6.1, Prop. 6.4);
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33.

the last unit vector of `ℝ^q`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.5, eq. (6.7);
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2.

  A * (D.restrict ⋯).Q =

**The Arnoldi relation** (outer-product form): `A Q_q = Q_q H_q + q_{q+1} h̲ᵀ` where
`h̲ = (h_{q+1,1}, …, h_{q+1,q})` is the last row of `H̲_q`. No hypothesis beyond the
decomposition of size `q + 1`; by the Hessenberg structure `h̲ = h_{q+1,q} e_q`
(`mul_restrict_Q_eq_add_smul`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.5, eq. (6.7);
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33, eq. (33.13).

  (hcond : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = ∫ (ω : Ω), cfac ω * Y ω ∂μ) (hYbound : ∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ ≤ B)

  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ cmax * B

doc:
Abstract assembly of Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN` (Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1).
* `X = ‖A − Â‖_F²`, `Y = ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²` (the range-finder error),
  `cfac ω = 1 + q(ω)/(s − q(ω) − 1)` with `q = rank(AΩ)` the (random) number of columns of `Q`.
* `hcond` encodes `lem:completion` after the tower property (conditioning on `Ω`, using
  independence of `Ψ` and `Ω`): `E X = E[(1 + q/(s−q−1)) Y]`.
* `hc` is the deterministic bound `q ≤ t` and monotonicity of `q ↦ q/(s−q−1)`
  (`completion_factor_mono`).
* `hYbound` is the range-finder theorem (`thm:RSVD`).
Atlas `gn-expected-error`.

`t ≥ k+2`, `s ≥ t+2`,
`E‖A − Â‖_F² ≤ (1 + t/(s−t−1)) (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.
Hypotheses: `hc` (`lem:completion`'s factor with `q = rank(AΩ) ≤ t`), `hcond`
(`lem:completion` + tower property), `hstruct` (`prop:hmt-struct` for
`Y = ‖(I−QQᵀ)A‖_F²`), `hZ` (`lem:moments` + `lem:invmom`, as in the proof of `thm:RSVD`).
The hypothesis `hk` is not used by the arithmetic; it is kept for fidelity.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (uses `rsvd-expected-error`).
atlas: gn-expected-error

name: NLAlib.Assembly.integral_le_sqrt_integral_sq
doc:
Jensen's inequality in the form used throughout Chen–Persson: for a nonnegative
square-integrable random variable `Y`, `E Y ≤ √(E Y²)`. Proved from
`0 ≤ Var Y = E Y² − (E Y)²`. Helper for atlas `rsvd-expected-error` (Frobenius-norm,
unsquared form of HMT 2011, Thm 10.5).

Assembly of Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD` (HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case).

signature:
NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.hanson_wright_inequality.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} {X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ} {K C t : ℝ}
  (hK : 0 < K) (hC : 0 < C) (hC_domain : 4 * Real.exp 1 ≤ C) (hC_diag_quad : 8 * Real.exp 1 ^ 3 ≤ C)
  (hC_offdiag_domain : 16 * Real.exp 1 ≤ C ^ 2) (hC_offdiag_quad : 64 * Real.exp 1 ^ 2 ≤ C)
  (hF : 0 < NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicFrobeniusNorm A)
  (hOp : 0 < NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicOperatorNorm A) (h_indep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hX_subG : ∀ (i : Fin n), ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (X i) ⟨K ^ 2, ⋯⟩ μ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  (μ {ω | t ≤ |NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.centeredQuadraticForm μ A X ω|}).toReal ≤
    2 *
      Real.exp
        (-(1 / (4 * C)) *
          min (t ^ 2 / (K ^ 4 * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicFrobeniusNorm A ^ 2))
            (t / (K ^ 2 * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicOperatorNorm A)))
name: NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.hanson_wright_inequality
doc:
Hanson-Wright tail bound with the MGF certificate proved from sub-Gaussian coordinates.

This theorem does not take `HasHansonWrightMGF` as a hypothesis.  Instead it proves
that certificate from independence and coordinate sub-Gaussian MGF bounds, then
optimizes the resulting Chernoff bound.

signature:

  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ}

  (hX_subG : ∀ (i : Fin n), ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (X i) ⟨K ^ 2, ⋯⟩ μ) :
  ∃ c,
    0 < c ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ),
        0 ≤ t →
          (μ {ω | t ≤ |NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.centeredQuadraticForm μ A X ω|}).toReal ≤
            2 *
              Real.exp
                (-c *
                  min (t ^ 2 / (K ^ 4 * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicFrobeniusNorm A ^ 2))
                    (t / (K ^ 2 * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicOperatorNorm A)))

doc:
Existential-form compatibility wrapper for the Hanson-Wright endpoint.
The witness is the public `hansonWrightUniversalConstant`.

NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.hasHansonWrightMGF_of_bounded.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ}
  {X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ} {K C : ℝ} (hK : 0 ≤ K) (hX_meas : ∀ (i : Fin n), AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
  (hX_bound : ∀ (i : Fin n), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, |X i ω| ≤ K)
  (hC_bound :
    2 * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.entrywiseL1Norm A ^ 2 ≤
      C * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicFrobeniusNorm A ^ 2) :
  NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.HasHansonWrightMGF μ A X K C
name: NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.hasHansonWrightMGF_of_bounded
doc:
A proved Hanson-Wright MGF certificate for bounded coordinates.

If each coordinate satisfies `|Xᵢ| ≤ K` almost surely, then the quadratic form lies
in the interval `[-K²‖A‖₁, K²‖A‖₁]`.  The centered quadratic form is therefore
bounded by `2K²‖A‖₁`; the local bounded MGF lemma above gives a quadratic CGF
estimate.  The explicit side condition compares this bounded-coordinate constant
with the Frobenius-scale constant used by the Hanson-Wright tail statement.

  (c : ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev
doc:
A probability measure satisfies the Euclidean logarithmic Sobolev inequality with
constant `c` if `Ent(g²)≤2c∫|∇g|²` for every `C¹` test function whose displayed integrals
are finite. The gradient is the standard coordinate Dirichlet form.
Ledoux 2001, Theorem 5.1; atlas `herbst` (general LSI premise).

signature:
NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev.casesOn.{u, u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure (ι → ℝ)} {c : ℝ} {motive : NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev μ c → Sort u}
  (t : NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev μ c)
  (mk :
    (constant_nonneg : 0 ≤ c) →
      (inequality :
          ∀ (g : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ),
            ContDiff ℝ 1 g →
              MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => g x ^ 2) μ →
                MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => g x ^ 2 * Real.log (g x ^ 2)) μ →
                  MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ∑ i, (fderiv ℝ g x) (Pi.single i 1) ^ 2) μ →
                    ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), g x ^ 2 * Real.log (g x ^ 2) ∂μ -
                        (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), g x ^ 2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), g x ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤
                      2 * c * ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), ∑ i, (fderiv ℝ g x) (Pi.single i 1) ^ 2 ∂μ) →
        motive ⋯) :
  motive t
name: NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev.casesOn

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)) (x : n → ℝ) :
  Prop
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser
doc:
`x` minimises the objective `E` over the affine space `x₀ + S`: `x − x₀ ∈ S` and
`E x ≤ E (x₀ + y)` for every `y ∈ S`. Minimising Krylov methods (CG, GMRES, MINRES, LSQR,
sketched GMRES) are instances with `S` a Krylov space. Non-uniqueness is harmless: theorems
quantify over every minimiser. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §5.1 (optimality of projection
methods); KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.apply_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} {E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ} {x₀ x : n → ℝ} {S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)}
  {x' : n → ℝ} (hx : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser E x₀ S x) (hx' : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser E x₀ S x') : E x = E x'
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.apply_eq
doc:
Two minimisers over the same affine space have the same value.
Source: KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_aeval.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ} {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser E x₀ (NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q) x)
  (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q) (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) :
  E x ≤ E (xs + ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (x₀ - xs))
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_aeval
doc:
**K1, error form.** If `x` minimises any objective `E` over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)` and
`A x⋆ = c`, then `E x ≤ E (x⋆ + p(A)(x₀ − x⋆))` for every residual polynomial `p`
(`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`). No hypothesis on `A` or `E`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`],
Thm 6.29 (proof); Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.3 (proof); KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.
Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (consumer: `cg-convergence`, `minres-bound`).
atlas: affine-krylov-minimiser

name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_aeval_residual
doc:
**K1, residual form.** If `x` minimises an objective of the residual,
`y ↦ F (c − A y)`, over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`, then `F (c − A x) ≤ F (p(A) r₀)` for every
residual polynomial `p`. No solution `x⋆` is needed (GMRES on singular or inconsistent
systems). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.32 (proof); KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.3.
Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (consumer: `gmres-def`).
atlas: affine-krylov-minimiser

name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_of_le
doc:
**Monotonicity.** A minimiser over a larger space is at least as good:
`S ≤ S'` gives `E x' ≤ E x`. With `S = K_q`, `S' = K_{q+1}` this is monotonicity of a
minimising Krylov method in the iteration count. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6
(GMRES residuals are nonincreasing).

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_of_sub_mem.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} {E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ} {x₀ x : n → ℝ} {S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)}
  (hx : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser E x₀ S x) {z : n → ℝ} (hz : z - x₀ ∈ S) : E x ≤ E z
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_of_sub_mem
doc:
A minimiser beats every point of the affine space: `z − x₀ ∈ S → E x ≤ E z`.
Source: KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.

name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_self
doc: A minimiser beats the starting point: `E x ≤ E x₀`. Source: KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ)
  (x : n → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsCGIterate
doc:
`x` is a `q`-th conjugate-gradient iterate for `A x = c` from `x₀`: `x − x₀` lies in
`K_q(A, c − A x₀)` and `x` minimises `cgObjective A c` over `x₀ + K_q(A, c − A x₀)`, i.e.
`IsAffineMinimiser (cgObjective A c) x₀ (krylovSpace A (c − A x₀) q) x`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.2 (variational form). Atlas: `cg-convergence`.
Deviation: a predicate rather than the output of the Hestenes–Stiefel recurrence.
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) (x : n → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate
doc:
`x` is a `q`-th CGLS (equivalently, in exact arithmetic, LSQR) iterate for
`min ‖b − A x‖` from `x₀`: it minimises `‖b − Ay‖²` over `x₀ + K_q(AᵀA, Aᵀ(b − Ax₀))`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3 (CGNR); Paige–Saunders (1982) [`ps82`]. Deviation: a
predicate, not the Golub–Kahan recurrence.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ)
  (x : n → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate
doc:
`x` is a GMRES iterate: `x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` (`r₀ = c − A x₀`) and `x` minimises
`‖c − A y‖²` over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`. MINRES is this predicate for symmetric `A`.
Source: Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §2; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5;
KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.3.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_of_eigenvalues_mem_Icc.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)
  (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤ (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_of_eigenvalues_mem_Icc
doc:
**MINRES, definite case (Chebyshev rate).** If `A` is symmetric with every eigenvalue in
`[a, b]`, `0 < a < b`, then `‖r_q‖ ≤ 2 ((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q ‖r₀‖` (squared form).
Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1; Liesen–Strakoš (2013) [`ls13`], §5.6.
atlas: minres-bound (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} {V W : Matrix n n ℝ} {d : n → ℝ} (hVW : V * W = 1)
  (hAd : A = V * Matrix.diagonal d * W) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ (i : n), |Polynomial.eval (d i) p| ≤ M) :
  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤
    (NLAlib.specNorm V * NLAlib.specNorm W * M) ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul
doc:
**GMRES bound for real diagonalisable `A`.** If `A = V diag(d) W` with `V W = 1` (so
`W = V⁻¹` and the `dᵢ` are the eigenvalues), then for every residual polynomial `p` with
`|p(dᵢ)| ≤ M`, `‖r_q‖ ≤ ‖V‖₂ ‖V⁻¹‖₂ M ‖r₀‖` (squared form).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.32; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 35.2;
Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §3.4.
Deviation: real eigenvalues and a real eigenvector matrix only (the printed statement allows a
complex diagonalisation, which is not available over `ℝ`).
atlas: gmres-diagonalizable (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_sq_mul_of_isHermitian.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q) (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) {M : ℝ}
  (hM : ∀ (i : n), |Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p| ≤ M) :
  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤ M ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_sq_mul_of_isHermitian
doc:
**MINRES spectral bound.** For symmetric `A` and every residual polynomial `p`
(`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`) with `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue, the GMRES (= MINRES) residual
satisfies `‖r_q‖² ≤ M² ‖r₀‖²`. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1; Paige–Saunders
(1975) [`ps75`].
Deviation: no invertibility of `A` and no solution `x⋆` needed (the bound is on residuals).
atlas: minres-bound (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.eq_of_isUnit
doc:
**The GMRES iterate is unique for invertible `A`.** Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.1.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.exists_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval
doc:
**Polynomial form of the residual**: `c − A x = p(A) r₀` for a residual polynomial `p`
(`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6; Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 35.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.isLeast_dotProduct_aeval.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  IsLeast
    {v |
      ∃ p,
        p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧
          Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1 ∧
            v = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)}
    ((c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x))
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.isLeast_dotProduct_aeval
doc:
**`‖r_q‖² = min_{p ∈ 𝒫_q⁰} ‖p(A) r₀‖²`**: the squared GMRES residual is the least value of
`‖p(A) r₀‖²` over residual polynomials. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6;
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35 (GMRES as a polynomial approximation problem).
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.le_aeval.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ}
  {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) :
  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤
    ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.le_aeval
doc:
**GMRES beats every residual polynomial**: `‖r_q‖² ≤ ‖p(A) r₀‖²` for every `p` with
`deg p ≤ q` and `p(0) = 1`. No hypothesis on `A`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.32
(proof); Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 35.2 (proof).
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.le_of_le
doc:
**GMRES residuals are nonincreasing**: for `q ≤ q'`, `‖r_{q'}‖² ≤ ‖r_q‖²`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6; Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §3.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.sub_mulVec_eq
doc:
**The GMRES residual is unique**: two GMRES iterates for the same data have the same
residual `c − A x`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.1 (the residual is the orthogonal
projection of `r₀` onto `(A K_q)^⟂`).
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.sub_mulVec_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : IsUnit A) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x)
  (hq : NLAlib.krylovGrade A (c - A.mulVec x₀) ≤ q) : c - A.mulVec x = 0
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.sub_mulVec_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
**Finite termination.** For invertible `A`, a GMRES iterate with `q` at least the grade
`ν = krylovGrade A r₀` solves the system: `c − A x = 0`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`],
Prop 6.10 (no breakdown before the solution) and §6.5.6; Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §3.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ}
  (Q : Matrix n (Fin q) ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis
doc:
`Q` is a **graded orthonormal Krylov basis** of `(A, b)`: its columns are orthonormal and for
every `i < q` the first `i + 1` columns span `K_{i+1}(A, b)`. Equivalently (`of_mem`), the
columns are orthonormal and `q_i ∈ K_{i+1}(A, b)`. Such a basis exists iff `q ≤ krylovGrade A b`
and is unique up to the signs of its columns (`ArnoldiDecomp.exists_sign`).
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3 and §6.6; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.5.
atlas: graded-krylov-basis-def

signature:
NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis.casesOn.{u, u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ}
  {q : ℕ} {Q : Matrix n (Fin q) ℝ} {motive : NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis A b Q → Sort u}
  (t : NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis A b Q)
  (mk :
    (orth : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) →
      (nested :
          ∀ (i : Fin q),
            Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun j => Q.col (Fin.castLE ⋯ j)) = NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (↑i + 1)) →
        motive ⋯) :
  motive t
name: NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis.casesOn

name: NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis.eq_sum_of_mem

Expansion in a graded basis: every `x ∈ K_q(A, b)` is `∑ᵢ (qᵢ ⬝ x) qᵢ`.
Atlas: `graded-krylov-basis-def`.

signature:

doc:

name: NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis.transpose_mul_mul_apply_eq_zero
doc:
**Hessenberg structure**: for a graded basis, `(Qᵀ A Q)_ij = 0` whenever `i > j + 1`, for
every `A`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.5; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33.
Atlas: `graded-krylov-basis-def`.

**Unreduced Hessenberg**: the subdiagonal of `Qᵀ A Q` has no zero,
`(Qᵀ A Q)_{j+1, j} ≠ 0`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.6 (breakdown at step `j`
iff `K_{j+1}` is invariant). Atlas: `graded-krylov-basis-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ) (V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  Prop
name: NLAlib.IsSVD
doc:
`IsSVD A U V`: `U`, `V` are orthogonal and `A = U Σ Vᵀ` with `Σ = rectDiag (singularValues A)`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3; HMT 2011, §2.1). The `k`-th columns of `U` and `V` are the
left/right singular vectors for `σ_k`. Atlas `svd`.
atlas: svd-def

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.apply
doc:
Thin-SVD / outer-product expansion, entrywise:
`A i j = ∑_{k < min m n} σ_k U_{ik} V_{jk}`, i.e. `A = ∑_k σ_k u_k v_kᵀ`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6; HMT 2011, §2.1). Atlas `svd`.

  (mk :
    (transpose_mul_left : U.transpose * U = 1) →
      (transpose_mul_right : V.transpose * V = 1) →
        (eq : A = U * NLAlib.rectDiag (NLAlib.singularValues A) * V.transpose) → motive ⋯) :
  motive t
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.casesOn

NLAlib.IsSVD.eq_head_add_tail {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.frobSq_sub_truncatedMatrix
doc:
The squared error of the truncated SVD is exactly the singular-value
tail, with no rank/dimension side conditions.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.gram_pow_mul_eq
doc:
An SVD diagonalizes every odd rectangular Gram power.
Source: HMT (2011), §10.4; manuscript `sa:expected-power`.

**Frobenius Eckart–Young minimizer.** Truncating any actual SVD gives a
best rank-at-most-`k` approximation, rather than assuming a best-approximation
predicate. Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.isMoorePenroseInverse
doc:
An SVD produces the Moore–Penrose inverse by reciprocating its nonzero
singular values; scalar `0⁻¹ = 0` handles zero singular values.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.mk
NLAlib.IsSVD.moorePenroseInverse_eq
doc:
Any real SVD computes the same Moore–Penrose inverse, independently of the
choice of singular vectors. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.mulVec_dotProduct_mulVec_eq_sum

The SVD gives the squared length as a weighted sum in right-singular
coordinates. Atlas: `svd`, `norm-lipschitz`.

doc:
**Spectral Eckart–Young, attainment for a given SVD.** The spectral error of truncating an
SVD after `k` terms is the `(k+1)`-st singular value (zero-indexed `σ_k`):
`‖A − U Σ_{<k} Vᵀ‖₂ = σ_k(A)`. All shapes and cutoffs are allowed (`σ_k = 0` for
`k ≥ min m n`). Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.4.9.1 (spectral case); HMT 2011, eq. (2.3);
audit G0 C3; atlas `eckart-young`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3} [Fintype k] [Fintype m]
  [Fintype d] (S : Matrix k m ℝ) (U : Matrix m d ℝ) (ε : ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding
doc:
`S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U`: `(1 - ε)‖Ux‖² ≤ ‖SUx‖² ≤ (1 + ε)‖Ux‖²` for
every `x`. Woodruff 2014 §2.1; Martinsson–Tropp 2020 §8.7. Atlas: `ose-def`.
atlas: ose-def

signature:
NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding.mono.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3} [Fintype k] [Fintype m]
  [Fintype d] {S : Matrix k m ℝ} {U : Matrix m d ℝ} {ε ε' : ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε) (hεε' : ε ≤ ε') :
  NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε'
name: NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding.mono
doc:
Monotonicity in the distortion: an `ε`-embedding is an `ε'`-embedding for `ε ≤ ε'`.

Atlas: `ose-def`.
atlas: ose-def

name: NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding.mul_right
doc:
Basis independence, easy direction: an embedding for `range U` is an embedding for
`range (U C)` for any `C` (since `range (U C) ⊆ range U`).

Atlas: `ose-def`.

name: NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding.of_mul_right
doc:
Basis independence, converse direction: if `C` has a right inverse `D` (`C D = 1`, so
`range (U C) = range U`) then an embedding for `range (U C)` is an embedding for `range U`.

Atlas: `ose-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs : n → ℝ) : (n → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr
doc:
Expected squared error `E‖x_k - xs‖²` after `k` randomized Kaczmarz steps started at `x`,
rows drawn i.i.d. with probabilities `prob A`. Defined by first-step recursion:
`expErr 0 x = ‖x - xs‖²`, `expErr (k+1) x = ∑ i, prob A i * expErr k (step A b x i)`.
See `expErr_eq_sum_paths` for the path-sum form. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.
atlas: kaczmarz-def

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_eq_sum_paths.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k =
    ∑ ω,
      (∏ j, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A (ω j)) * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_eq_sum_paths
doc:
`expErr` is the expectation over i.i.d. row sequences: the sum over all `ω : Fin k → m` of
`(∏ j, prob A (ω j)) * ‖run A b k ω x - xs‖²`. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k ≤ (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz converges linearly in expectation.**
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.
If `A *ᵥ xs = b` and `σ² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖A v‖²` for all `v`, then after `k` steps with rows drawn
i.i.d. with probability `‖A i‖² / ‖A‖_F²`,
`E‖x_k - xs‖² ≤ (1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x₀ - xs‖²`.
Deviations from the printed statement: SV09 take `A` of full column rank and `σ = ‖A⁻¹‖⁻¹`
(rate `1 - κ(A)⁻²`); here `σ` is any constant satisfying `hσ` (the sharp choice is
`σ_min(A)`, atlas `courant-fischer`), and no rank or nonzero-row assumption is needed.
atlas: randomized-kaczmarz

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_add.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xh : n → ℝ) (σ : ℝ) (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xh x k ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xh) ⬝ᵥ (x - xh) +
      (∑ j ∈ Finset.range k, (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ j) *
        ((b - A.mulVec xh) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec xh) / NLAlib.frobSq A)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_add
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz on inconsistent systems.** If `σ²‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖²` for all `v`, then for
any reference point `xh` and `e = b − A xh`, with `ρ = 1 − σ²/‖A‖_F²`,
`E‖x_k − xh‖² ≤ ρ^k ‖x₀ − xh‖² + (∑_{j<k} ρ^j) ‖e‖²/‖A‖_F²`.
Source: Needell (2010) [`needell10`], Thm 2.1 (stated for norms, with `xh` the least-squares
solution); Zouzias–Freris (2013) [`zf13`], eq. (5) (squared form).
Atlas: `kaczmarz-inconsistent`; uses `randomized-kaczmarz`.
Deviation: any reference point `xh` (no least-squares or consistency assumption); the geometric
sum is kept exact.
atlas: kaczmarz-inconsistent

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_add_div_sq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xh : n → ℝ) {σ : ℝ} (hσ0 : 0 < σ) (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v)
  (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xh x k ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xh) ⬝ᵥ (x - xh) + (b - A.mulVec xh) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec xh) / σ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_add_div_sq
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz on inconsistent systems, horizon form.** If `σ > 0` and
`σ²‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖²` for all `v`, then for any `xh`,
`E‖x_k − xh‖² ≤ (1 − σ²/‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x₀ − xh‖² + ‖b − A xh‖²/σ²`.
Source: Needell (2010) [`needell10`], Thm 2.1 (squared form, `R = ‖A‖_F²/σ²`);
Zouzias–Freris (2013) [`zf13`], Thm 2. Atlas: `kaczmarz-inconsistent`.
atlas: kaczmarz-inconsistent

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_add_div_sq_of_sub_mem_range.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xh : n → ℝ) {σ : ℝ} (hσ0 : 0 < σ)

**For symmetric `A`, `T_q` is tridiagonal**: `t_ij = 0` whenever `|i − j| > 1`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36.

For symmetric `A`, `T_q` is the Jacobi matrix of its recurrence coefficients:
`T_q = jacobiMatrix α β q`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.X_mul_poly.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ}
  (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsSymm) {j : ℕ} (hj : j + 1 < q) :
  Polynomial.X * D.poly j =
    Polynomial.C (D.beta j) * D.poly (j - 1) + Polynomial.C (D.alpha j) * D.poly j +
      Polynomial.C (D.beta (j + 1)) * D.poly (j + 1)

doc:
**Three-term recurrence of the Lanczos polynomials**: for symmetric `A` and `j + 1 < q`,
`X p_j = β_j p_{j−1} + α_j p_j + β_{j+1} p_{j+1}`, so the Jacobi matrix `T` holds the recurrence
coefficients of the orthonormal polynomials of `μ_b`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`],
Thm 2.1 and Thm 4.2.
atlas: lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials (partial)

The Lanczos diagonal coefficient `α_j = t_jj = q_jᵀ A q_j` (`0` for `j ≥ q`).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Alg. 4.1. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence`.

The Lanczos off-diagonal coefficient `β_j = t_{j,j−1} = q_jᵀ A q_{j−1}` (`β_0 = 0`, and `0`
for `j ≥ q`). Indexing: `A q_j = β_j q_{j−1} + α_j q_j + β_{j+1} q_{j+1}` (0-based columns).

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.cfc_T_apply_zero_zero
doc:
**Golub–Welsch**: `e₁ᵀ f(T_q) e₁ = ∑ᵢ f(θᵢ) (uᵢ)₁²` with `(θᵢ, uᵢ)` the eigenpairs of
`T_q`: the Gauss rule has the eigenvalues of `T_q` as nodes and the squared first components
of its eigenvectors as weights. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 6 (Golub–Welsch; label to
verify).

NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.charpoly_restrict_T_mul_poly_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsSymm) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < q) :

`χ_j p_0 = β_1 ⋯ β_j p_j` with `χ_j = charpoly T_j` (`p_0 = ±1/‖b‖` is a constant; for
`‖b‖ = 1` and the canonical signs this is `det(x I − T_j) = β_1 ⋯ β_j p_j(x)`).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3 and Thm 4.2 (labels to verify).

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq
doc:
**Gauss–Lanczos quadrature through the Jacobi matrix**: for symmetric `A`, `q ≥ 1` and
`deg p < 2q`, `bᵀ p(A) b = ‖b‖² (p(T_q))₁₁`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 6.6
and §7.1; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021) [`ctu21`], Thm 2.1. Deviation: the degree bound is
`p.degree < 2 * q` (no `natDegree`, no truncated subtraction).
atlas: lanczos-gauss-quadrature

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
**Gauss quadrature through the Jacobi matrix**: for symmetric `A`, `q ≥ 1` and
`deg p < 2q`, `bᵀ p(A) b = ‖b‖² ∑ᵢ p(θᵢ) (uᵢ)₁²` with nodes `θᵢ` the eigenvalues of `T_q` and
weights the squared first eigenvector components. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`],
Thm 6.6; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021) [`ctu21`], Thm 2.1.
atlas: lanczos-gauss-quadrature, jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

signature:

    b ⬝ᵥ b * ∑ i, f (⋯.eigenvalues i) * (⋯.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⟨0, hq⟩ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.dotProduct_cfc_T_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
**The Lanczos quadrature value is a Gauss rule**: `(Q_qᵀ b)ᵀ f(T_q) (Q_qᵀ b) =
‖b‖² ∑ᵢ f(θᵢ) (uᵢ)₁²` for every `f`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 6.6 and §7.1;
Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], §3.
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial), lanczos-gauss-quadrature (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.eigenvalues₀_le_eigenvalues₀_restrict_T.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
**Cauchy interlacing, lower half**: `θ_{i + (q − q')}(T_q) ≤ θ_i(T_{q'})` for `q' ≤ q`;
with `q' = q − 1` and the upper half, the eigenvalues of `T_{q−1}` interlace those of `T_q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3 (label to verify); Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`],
Thm 4.3.17.
Deviation: non-strict.
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.eigenvalues₀_restrict_T_le

**Cauchy interlacing, upper half**: the eigenvalues of `T_{q'}` (`q' ≤ q`, a leading
principal submatrix of `T_q`) satisfy `θ_i(T_{q'}) ≤ θ_i(T_q)` (eigenvalues in non-increasing
order). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3 (interlacing; label to verify);
Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], Thm 4.3.17. Deviation: non-strict.
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.exists_col_eq_aeval
doc:
Each Lanczos vector is a polynomial of exact degree `j` in `A` applied to `b`:
`q_j = p_j(A) b` with `deg p_j = j`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2 (§4.1).
Atlas: `lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials`.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.integral_eval_charpoly_mul_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

  (hr : r.degree < ↑q) :

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.integral_eval_charpoly_mul_eq_zero
doc:
**`det(x I − T_q)` is the monic orthogonal polynomial of degree `q`**: for symmetric `A`,
`χ_q = charpoly T_q` (monic of degree `q`, `charpoly_T_monic`, `natDegree_charpoly_T`) is
orthogonal in `μ_b` to every polynomial of degree `< q`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010)
[`gm10`], Thm 4.2 and §3.1 (`p_q` and `det(λI − J_q)` are proportional).
atlas: lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.integral_poly_mul_poly.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i j : ℕ} (hi : i < q) :
  ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x (D.poly i) * Polynomial.eval x (D.poly j) ∂NLAlib.spectralMeasure hA b =

doc:
**The Lanczos polynomials are orthonormal for the spectral measure**:
`∫ p_i p_j dμ_b = δ_ij` for `i < q` (and any `j`; `p_j = 0` for `j ≥ q`).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2 and §2.1; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.5.
atlas: lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.inv_smul_one_sub_T_apply_zero_zero
doc:
**The resolvent entry is the Jacobi continued fraction**: for symmetric `A`, `q ≥ 1` and
`x` above the spectrum of `A`, `e₁ᵀ (x I − T_q)⁻¹ e₁ = 1/(x − α₀ − β₁²/(x − α₁ − ⋯ −
β_{q−1}²/(x − α_{q−1})))`, the `q`-th convergent of the continued fraction of the Stieltjes
transform `∫ dμ_b(t)/(x − t)` (for `‖b‖ = 1`). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3
(continued fractions; label to verify) and Thm 4.2. Deviation: real `x` above the spectrum
(so every trailing block is nonsingular); complex `x` off the real axis is not covered.
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.mulVec_vec_eq
doc:
**The Lanczos three-term recurrence** (column form): for symmetric `A` and `j + 1 < q`,
`A q_j = β_j q_{j−1} + α_j q_j + β_{j+1} q_{j+1}` (with `β_0 = 0`). Together with
`ArnoldiDecomp.mul_restrict_Q_eq_add_smul` this is `A Q_q = Q_q T_q + β_q q_{q+1} e_qᵀ`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36,
eq. (36.3).
atlas: lanczos-recurrence, arnoldi-relation (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.mul_restrict_Q_eq_add_beta_smul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b (q + 1)) (hq : 0 < q) :
  A * (NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.restrict D ⋯).Q =
    (NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.restrict D ⋯).Q * NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.T (NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.restrict D ⋯) +
      D.beta q • Matrix.vecMulVec (D.vec q) (Pi.single ⟨q - 1, ⋯⟩ 1)

doc:
**The Lanczos relation** `A Q_q = Q_q T_q + β_q q_{q+1} e_qᵀ` (for `q ≥ 1`), with
`β_q = t_{q,q−1}` and `q_{q+1}` the last column of a decomposition of size `q + 1`; together with
`T_apply_eq_zero_of_one_lt_dist` (`T_q` symmetric tridiagonal for symmetric `A`) and
`ArnoldiDecomp.hasOrthonormalCols`, `ArnoldiDecomp.range_Q` this is the Lanczos
tridiagonalisation. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021)
[`ctu21`], §2.
atlas: lanczos-recurrence

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} {J : Type u_4} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype s] [Fintype J] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (p : J → ℝ) (S : J → Matrix m s ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) :
  (n → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr
doc:
Expected squared error after `k` sketch-and-project steps from `x`, sketches `S j` drawn
i.i.d. with probabilities `p j`, by first-step recursion:
`expErr 0 x = ‖x − xs‖²`, `expErr (k+1) x = ∑ⱼ pⱼ expErr k (step A b (S j) x)`.
Atlas: `sketch-and-project`.
atlas: sketch-and-project

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr.eq_def.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} {J : Type u_4}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype s] [Fintype J] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (p : J → ℝ) (S : J → Matrix m s ℝ)
  (xs x✝ : n → ℝ) (x✝¹ : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr A b p S xs x✝ x✝¹ =
    match x✝, x✝¹ with
    | x, 0 => (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
    | x, k.succ => ∑ j, p j * NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr A b p S xs (NLAlib.SketchProject.step A b (S j) x) k
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr.eq_def
NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr_le
doc:
**Sketch-and-project converges linearly in expectation.** Let `A xs = b`, `pⱼ ≥ 0`,
`∑ pⱼ = 1`, and `λ ‖v‖² ≤ vᵀ W v` for all `v`, with `W = ∑ⱼ pⱼ (SⱼᵀA)⁺(SⱼᵀA)`. Then after `k`
steps with i.i.d. sketches, `E‖x_k − xs‖² ≤ (1 − λ)^k ‖x₀ − xs‖²`.
Source: Gower–Richtárik (2015) [`gr15`], Thm 4.6 (`B = I`; the sharp `λ` is
`λ_min⁺(W)`). Atlas: `sketch-and-project`; uses `pseudoinverse`. Deviation: finite sketch
distribution; expectation modelled by first-step recursion.
atlas: sketch-and-project

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr_le_of_sub_mem_range.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3}
  {J : Type u_4} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype s] [Fintype J] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (p : J → ℝ)
  (hp : ∀ (j : J), 0 ≤ p j) (hp1 : ∑ j, p j = 1) (S : J → Matrix m s ℝ) {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) {lam : ℝ}
  (hlam :
    ∀ v ∈ A.transpose.mulVecLin.range, lam * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ v ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.SketchProject.expectedProjector A p S).mulVec v)
  (x : n → ℝ) (hx : x - xs ∈ A.transpose.mulVecLin.range) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr A b p S xs x k ≤ (1 - lam) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr_le_of_sub_mem_range
doc:
**Sketch-and-project contraction on the row space.** For a consistent system,
an initial error in `range Aᵀ`, and a lower bound `λ‖v‖² ≤ vᵀ W v` only on that
row space, the finite iid sketch distribution satisfies
`E‖x_k-xs‖² ≤ (1-λ)^k ‖x₀-xs‖²`. No full-column-rank assumption is required.
Gower–Richtárik 2015, Theorem 4.6, Euclidean case `B = I`;
atlas `sketch-and-project`. Deviation: a finite sketch distribution, with expectation
given by the exact first-step recursion. The initial-error membership is essential.
atlas: sketch-and-project

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.expectedProjector.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} {J : Type u_4}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype s] [Fintype J] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (p : J → ℝ) (S : J → Matrix m s ℝ) : Matrix n n ℝ
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.expectedProjector
doc:
The expected projector `W = ∑ⱼ pⱼ (SⱼᵀA)⁺(SⱼᵀA)`. Source: Gower–Richtárik (2015) [`gr15`],
eq. (4.1) (`E[Z]` with `B = I`). Atlas: `sketch-and-project`.
atlas: sketch-and-project

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.expected_sqErr_step_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3}
  {J : Type u_4} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype s] [Fintype J] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (p : J → ℝ)
  (hp1 : ∑ j, p j = 1) (S : J → Matrix m s ℝ) {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (x : n → ℝ) :
  ∑ j, p j * (NLAlib.SketchProject.step A b (S j) x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.SketchProject.step A b (S j) x - xs) =
    (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) - (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.SketchProject.expectedProjector A p S).mulVec (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.expected_sqErr_step_eq
doc:
One-step expected error identity: for `A xs = b` and `∑ pⱼ = 1`,
`∑ⱼ pⱼ ‖step A b (S j) x − xs‖² = ‖x − xs‖² − (x − xs)ᵀ W (x − xs)`.

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.step.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

name: NLAlib.SketchProject.step
doc:
One sketch-and-project step with sketch `S`: the Euclidean projection of `x` onto
`{y | Sᵀ A y = Sᵀ b}`, written `x − (SᵀA)⁺ Sᵀ (A x − b)`. Source: Gower–Richtárik (2015)
[`gr15`], eq. (2.2)–(2.3) with `B = I`. Atlas: `sketch-and-project`.

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.step_sub_mem_range.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype s] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (S : Matrix m s ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ)

name: NLAlib.SketchProject.step_sub_mem_range
doc:
A sketch-and-project update preserves membership of the error in `range Aᵀ`,
even for an arbitrary reference point and an inconsistent right-hand side.
The correction belongs to the row space because the Moore–Penrose inverse of `SᵀA`
has range contained in `range Aᵀ`. Gower–Richtárik 2015, eq. (2.3);
atlas `sketch-and-project` (invariant-space helper).

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.step_sub_solution.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype s] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (S : Matrix m s ℝ) {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b)

  NLAlib.SketchProject.step A b S x - xs =
    x - xs - (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse (S.transpose * A) * (S.transpose * A)).mulVec (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.step_sub_solution
doc:

Atlas: `sketch-and-project`.

signature:

  (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d) (nu : ℕ) {a c : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hc : 0 ≤ c)
  (hlight :
    ‖((1 / ↑m) • NLAlib.SparseFock.NamedBands.Lminus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseFock.FiniteHilbert.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      a + NLAlib.SparseFock.BandEnvelope.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m)
  (hmixed :
    ‖(1 / ↑m) •
            √(↑b - 1) •
              ((NLAlib.SparseFock.NamedBands.XplusAdj m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) +
                NLAlib.SparseFock.NamedBands.YplusAdj m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseFock.FiniteHilbert.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      NLAlib.SparseFock.BandEnvelope.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + 3 / 2 * c)
  (hheavy :
    ‖((1 / ↑m) • √(↑b - 1) ^ 2 • NLAlib.SparseFock.NamedBands.Hminus m fun i x => (F.u i).ofLp x) *
          NLAlib.SparseFock.FiniteHilbert.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
      c)
  (hbTerm : 0 ≤ NLAlib.SparseFock.BandEnvelope.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m) :
  ‖NLAlib.SparseFock.ConcreteLadder.normalizedBand m F b NLAlib.SparseFock.BandInventory.Shift.minus *
        NLAlib.SparseFock.FiniteHilbert.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
    NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.Cband * (a + NLAlib.SparseFock.BandEnvelope.bTerm ↑d ↑nu ↑m + c)

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.DirectionalConcrete.hprime_wordKernel_apply {m n : ℕ} {r : Fin m} {i j : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j)

  NLAlib.SparseFock.FiniteOperator.wordKernel (r, i) (r, j)
      (NLAlib.SparseFock.BandInventory.Leg.pDown, NLAlib.SparseFock.BandInventory.Leg.pUp) out inp =
    if
        out (r, i) = NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.zero ∧
          out (r, j) = NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.one ∧
            inp =
              NLAlib.SparseFock.DirectionalConcrete.setPair out (r, i) NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.one (r, j)
                NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.zero then
      1
    else 0

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.DirectionalConcrete.orderedHprime_mulVec {d m n : ℕ} (u : Fin n → Fin d → ℝ)
  (x : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseFock.Pattern m n → ℝ) (r : Fin m) {i j : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) (k : Fin d)
  (σ : NLAlib.SparseFock.Pattern m n) :
  Matrix.mulVec
      (NLAlib.SparseFock.ExternalOperator.orderedWordTerm u r i j
        (NLAlib.SparseFock.BandInventory.Leg.pDown, NLAlib.SparseFock.BandInventory.Leg.pUp))
      x (k, σ) =
    if σ (r, i) = NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.zero ∧ σ (r, j) = NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.one then
      ∑ l,
        u i k * u j l *
          x
            (l,
              NLAlib.SparseFock.DirectionalConcrete.setPair σ (r, i) NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.one (r, j)
                NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.zero)
    else 0
name: NLAlib.SparseFock.DirectionalConcrete.orderedHprime_mulVec

One ordered transpose-light-hop word has exactly its marked coefficient.

      ∑ l,
        u i k * u j l *
          x
            (l,
              NLAlib.SparseFock.DirectionalConcrete.setPair σ (r, i) NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.one (r, j)
                NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.zero)
    else 0

NLAlib.SparseFock.DirectionalConcrete.orderedYzero_mulVec {d m n : ℕ} (u : Fin n → Fin d → ℝ)

  (t : NLAlib.SparseFock.FiniteL2.WeightedONBasis Omega I)
  (mk :
    (weight : Omega → ℝ) →
      (weight_nonneg : ∀ (x : Omega), 0 ≤ weight x) →
        (sum_weight : ∑ x, weight x = 1) →

              (orthonormal_ne : ∀ (i j : I), i ≠ j → ∑ x, weight x * basis i x * basis j x = 0) →
                (reconstruction :
                    ∀ (f : Omega → ℝ) (x : Omega), f x = ∑ i, (∑ y, weight y * basis i y * f y) * basis i x) →
                  (vacuum : I) →
                    (vacuum_eq_one : ∀ (x : Omega), basis vacuum x = 1) →
                      motive

NLAlib.SparseFock.GlobalBands.cell_lightLight {d m n : ℕ} (u : Fin n → Fin d → ℝ) (ρ : ℝ)

Fubini plus scalar distributivity for the four finite indices used by a

The heavy annihilation analysis matrix is the sum of its one-site summands.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.HeavyBandsConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

name: NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownMatrix_grade_relation
doc:
Every nonzero heavy annihilation analysis entry lowers the pattern grade by one.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.HeavyBandsConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownMatrix_gram_row {d m n : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d)
  (r : Fin m) :
  (NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownMatrix F r).transpose *
      NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownMatrix F r =
    ∑ i,
        ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
          NLAlib.SparseFock.ExternalOperator.orderedWordTerm (NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.frameRows F) r i j
            (NLAlib.SparseFock.BandInventory.Leg.rUp, NLAlib.SparseFock.BandInventory.Leg.rDown) +
      ∑ i,
        (NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownOne F r i).transpose *
          NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownOne F r i
name: NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownMatrix_gram_row
doc:
A row annihilation Gram matrix splits into distinct-site words and its same-site diagonal correction.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.HeavyBandsConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownMatrix_mulVec {d m n : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d)
  (x : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseFock.Pattern m n → ℝ) (r : Fin m) (σ : NLAlib.SparseFock.Pattern m n) :
  (NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownMatrix F r).mulVec x σ =
    ∑ i ∈ σ.lightInRow r,
      NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.analyze F
        (NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.fiber x
          (NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.setSite σ (r, i) NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.two))
        i
name: NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownMatrix_mulVec

A heavy annihilation analysis matrix acts by summing its admissible marked frame coefficients.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.HeavyBandsConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownOne {d m n : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d) (r : Fin m)
  (i : Fin n) : Matrix (NLAlib.SparseFock.Pattern m n) (Fin d × NLAlib.SparseFock.Pattern m n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownOne
doc:
A one-site heavy annihilation analysis summand is expressed on the concrete finite basis.
Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.HeavyBandsConcrete`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownOne_mulVec {d m n : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d)
  (x : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseFock.Pattern m n → ℝ) (r : Fin m) (i : Fin n) (σ : NLAlib.SparseFock.Pattern m n) :
  (NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.ADownOne F r i).mulVec x σ =
    if σ (r, i) = NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.one then
      NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.analyze F
        (NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.fiber x
          (NLAlib.SparseFock.HeavyBandsConcrete.setSite σ (r, i) NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.two))
        i
    else 0

  (heps1 : eps ≤ 1) (frameLaw : NLAlib.SparseFock.FiniteLaw Omega)
  (frames : Omega → NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d)
  (hband :
    ∀ (omega : Omega) (shift : NLAlib.SparseFock.BandInventory.Shift),
      ∀ nu ≤ 2 * NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta,
        ‖NLAlib.SparseFock.ConcreteLadder.normalizedBand
                (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedM d (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta)
                  eps)
                (frames omega)
                (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedB d (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta)
                  eps)
                shift *
              NLAlib.SparseFock.FiniteHilbert.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
          NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.betaEnvelope d (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta)
            ↑(NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedM d (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta) eps)
            ↑(NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedS (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta)
                eps)) :
  (frameLaw.product
          (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackDistribution.rawSampleLaw
            (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedS (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta) eps)
            (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedB d (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta) eps)
            n ⋯)).prob
      {outcome |
        eps <
          ‖NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.gramError (frames outcome.1)
              (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackDistribution.toSample outcome.2)‖} ≤
    delta

                (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedB d (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta)
                  eps)
                shift *
              NLAlib.SparseFock.FiniteHilbert.gradeProjection nu‖ ≤
          NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.betaEnvelope d (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta)
            ↑(NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedM d (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta) eps)
            ↑(NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedS (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta)
                eps)) :
  1 - delta ≤
    (frameLaw.product
          (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackDistribution.rawSampleLaw
            (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedS (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta) eps)
            (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.roundedB d (NLAlib.SparseFock.PaperParameters.failureOrder d delta) eps)
            n ⋯)).prob
      {outcome |
        NLAlib.SparseFock.MatrixTail.IsSparseStackOSE (frames outcome.1)
          (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackDistribution.toSample outcome.2) eps}

doc:
A precise scalar certificate for the shared-leg block-Gram step.

To instantiate this with operators `V_i`, take `energy i = ‖z_i‖²`,
`diagonal i = ⟪z_i, V_i† V_i z_i⟫`, and let `cross i j` be the ordered
off-diagonal quadratic-form contribution.  The three hypotheses below are
exactly the facts that still have to be supplied by an operator formalization:

* `hquadratic`: expansion of the quadratic form into its blocks;
* `hdiag`: `V_i† V_i ≼ d I`;
* `hcross`: the cross-map contraction `‖V_i† V_j‖ ≤ 1` followed by scalar
  Cauchy--Schwarz.

The conclusion is the `d + ell - 1` light-sector constant.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorAbstract`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorAbstract.compressed_lightSector_bound {d ell hard bosonic energy : ℝ}
  (hcompression : hard ≤ bosonic) (hbosonic : bosonic ≤ (d + ell - 1) * energy) : hard ≤ (d + ell - 1) * energy
name: NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorAbstract.compressed_lightSector_bound
doc:
Compression is norm-decreasing at the scalar quadratic-form level.

This theorem intentionally assumes the compression comparison `hard ≤ bosonic`.
In the sparse-Fock proof that premise is supplied by the positive bosonic dilation;
formalizing the Fock-space isometry and positivity is outside this module.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorAbstract`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorAbstract.offDiagonal_sum_le {ell : ℕ} (hell : 1 ≤ ell) (energy : Fin ell → ℝ)
  (cross : Fin ell → Fin ell → ℝ) (hcross : ∀ (i j : Fin ell), i ≠ j → cross i j ≤ (energy i + energy j) / 2) :
  ∑ i, ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, cross i j ≤ (↑ell - 1) * ∑ i, energy i
name: NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorAbstract.offDiagonal_sum_le
doc:
Pairwise arithmetic behind the block-Gram estimate.

`cross i j` is the scalar contribution of the `(i,j)` block to one fixed
quadratic form, while `energy i` is the squared norm of the `i`th input block.
The premise is exactly the operator Cauchy--Schwarz estimate after
`2ab ≤ a²+b²`; no operator fact is hidden here.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.LightSectorAbstract`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:

  ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, energy j = ∑ j, energy j - energy i
name: NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorAbstract.sum_erase_univ_eq_sub
doc:
The sum over all indices other than `i` is the full sum with the `i`th

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.ghat_apply {d m n : ℕ} (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d)
  (out inp : Fin d × NLAlib.SparseFock.Pattern m n) :
  NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.ghat F out inp =
    ∑ r,
      ∑ i,
        ∑ j,
          (F.u i).ofLp out.1 * (F.u j).ofLp inp.1 *
            (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.pDagAt r i * NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.pAt r j) out.2
              inp.2

      (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.LabelledIndex d m n ell) ℝ)
  (x y : NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.BlockIndex d T ell) :

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.lightMove_legal_of_domain_eq {m n : ℕ} (T : Finset (NLAlib.SparseFock.Site m n))
  (ell : ℕ) (out inp : NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.BlockPattern T ell) (pi sigma : Equiv.Perm (Fin ell))
  (k : Fin ell)
  (hdom :
    NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.domainOfWord k
        (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.permutedLightWord T ell out pi) =
      NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.domainOfWord k
        (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.permutedLightWord T ell inp sigma)) :
  have O := NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.permutedLightWord T ell out pi;
  have I := NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.permutedLightWord T ell inp sigma;
  ↑inp (I k) = NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.one ∧
    (O k = I k ∨ ↑inp (O k) = NLAlib.SparseFock.Level.zero) ∧
      ↑out = NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.lightMove (↑inp) (I k) (O k)

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.orbit_legal_weighted_sum {m n : ℕ} (T : Finset (NLAlib.SparseFock.Site m n))
  (ell : ℕ) (out inp : NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.BlockPattern T ell) (a b : Fin n → ℝ) :
  (∑ k,
      ∑ tau,
        if NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.OrbitCompatible T ell out inp (k, tau) then
          a (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.canonicalLightWord T ell out k).2 *
            b (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.permutedLightWord T ell inp tau k).2
        else 0) =
    ∑ r, ∑ i, ∑ j, if NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.LegalLightMove ↑out ↑inp (r, i, j) then a i * b j else 0

  (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.pDagAt r i * NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.pAt r j) out inp =

NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.sum_sum_labelledG_blockLabel {d m n : ℕ}
  (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d) (T : Finset (NLAlib.SparseFock.Site m n)) (ell : ℕ)
  (x y : NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.BlockIndex d T ell) :
  ∑ pi,
      ∑ sigma,
        NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.labelledG F ell
          (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.blockLabel T ell x pi)
          (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.blockLabel T ell y sigma) =
    ↑(NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.permutationCount ell) *
      ∑ tau,
        NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.labelledG F ell
          (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.blockLabel T ell x (Equiv.refl (Fin ell)))
          (NLAlib.SparseFock.LightSectorConcrete.blockLabel T ell y tau)

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.MomentTransfer.iid_trace_moment_eq_product {s b n d : ℕ} (hs : 0 < s) (hb : 1 < b)
  (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d) (q : ℕ) :
  ((NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseIIDUnconditional.iidArrayLaw ⋯ s n).expect fun y =>
      (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseIIDTransfer.iidVectorError F y ^ (2 * q)).trace) =
    (NLAlib.SparseFock.ProductFock.iidLaw b hb (s * b) n).expect fun ω =>
      (NLAlib.SparseFock.VacuumMoment.iidGramError b F ω ^ (2 * q)).trace
name: NLAlib.SparseFock.MomentTransfer.iid_trace_moment_eq_product
doc:
The unscaled iid-vector trace moment is exactly the product-Fock trace
moment after the proved finite-coordinate flattening.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.MomentTransfer`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.MomentTransfer.raw_trace_moment_le_scaled_product {s b n d : ℕ} (hs : 0 < s) (hb : 1 < b)
  (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d) (q : ℕ) :
  ((NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackDistribution.rawSampleLaw s b n ⋯).expect fun z =>
      (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.gramError F (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackDistribution.toSample z) ^
          (2 * q)).trace) ≤
    NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseIIDCoupling.cB b ^ (4 * q) *
      (NLAlib.SparseFock.ProductFock.iidLaw b hb (s * b) n).expect fun omega =>
        (NLAlib.SparseFock.VacuumMoment.iidGramError b F omega ^ (2 * q)).trace
name: NLAlib.SparseFock.MomentTransfer.raw_trace_moment_le_scaled_product
doc:
Exact distribution-level convex-moment bridge from the literal raw
SparseStack law to the product-Fock iid law.

Source: ported from `SparseFockFormal.MomentTransfer`,
b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.MomentTransfer.scaledIIDVectorError_trace_even {s b n d : ℕ}
  (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d) (y : NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseIIDTransfer.YArray b s n) (q : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseIIDTransfer.scaledIIDVectorError F y ^ (2 * q)).trace =
    NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseIIDCoupling.cB b ^ (4 * q) *
      (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseIIDTransfer.iidVectorError F y ^ (2 * q)).trace
name: NLAlib.SparseFock.MomentTransfer.scaledIIDVectorError_trace_even
doc:
Scaling both iid vectors by `c_b` scales the `2q`-trace moment by
`c_b^(4q)`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.MomentTransfer.scaled_iid_trace_moment_eq_product {s b n d : ℕ} (hs : 0 < s) (hb : 1 < b)
  (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d) (q : ℕ) :
  ((NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseIIDUnconditional.iidArrayLaw ⋯ s n).expect fun y =>
      (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseIIDTransfer.scaledIIDVectorError F y ^ (2 * q)).trace) =
    NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseIIDCoupling.cB b ^ (4 * q) *

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.gramError_eq_block_first {s b n d : ℕ}
  (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d) (Z : NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.Sample s b n) (hs : 0 < s) :
  NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.gramError F Z = fun a c =>
    1 / ↑s *
      ∑ g,
        ∑ i,

            inner ℝ (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.signedBasis Z g i)
                  (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.signedBasis Z g j) *
                (F.u i).ofLp a *
              (F.u j).ofLp c

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.sketchGram {s b n : ℕ} (Z : NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.Sample s b n) :

name: NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.sketchGram
doc:

b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.sketchGram_apply {s b n : ℕ} (Z : NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.Sample s b n)
  (hs : 0 < s) (i j : Fin n) :
  NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.sketchGram Z i j =
    1 / ↑s *
      ∑ g,
        inner ℝ (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.signedBasis Z g i)
          (NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.signedBasis Z g j)

doc:

NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.stackMatrix {s b n : ℕ} (Z : NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.Sample s b n) :

name: NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.stackMatrix
doc:
The stacked sketch matrix, with rows indexed without flattening by
`Fin s × Fin b` and columns by `Fin n`.

b9da2b5d96e5fd70252e9c6551aefc92643e7d0b; supports `sparse-ose`.

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.stackMatrix_apply {s b n : ℕ} (Z : NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.Sample s b n)
  (g : Fin s) (a : Fin b) (i : Fin n) :
  NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.stackMatrix Z (g, a) i =
    NLAlib.SparseFock.SparseStackModel.invSqrt s * if a = Z.hash g i then (Z.sgn g i).val else 0

  (Y Y✝ : NLAlib.SparseFock.UniformExactS.IidColumnSample b s n) (e_Y : Y = Y✝) (a✝ a✝¹ : Fin d) :
  a✝ = a✝¹ →
    ∀ (a a✝² : Fin d),
      a = a✝² →
        NLAlib.SparseFock.UniformExactS.exactScaledIIDError hb F Y a✝ a =
          NLAlib.SparseFock.UniformExactS.exactScaledIIDError hb F✝ Y✝ a✝¹ a✝²

            (F.u j).ofLp c

signature:
NLAlib.SparseFock.VacuumMoment.iidGramError_apply {m n d : ℕ} (b : ℕ) (F : NLAlib.SparseFock.ParsevalFrame.Frame n d)
  (omega : NLAlib.SparseFock.ProductFock.Configuration m n) (a c : Fin d) :
  NLAlib.SparseFock.VacuumMoment.iidGramError b F omega a c =
    1 / ↑m *
      ∑ r,
        ∑ i,
          ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
            NLAlib.SparseFock.ProductFock.etaCoordinate b (r, i) omega *
                  NLAlib.SparseFock.ProductFock.etaCoordinate b (r, j) omega *
                (F.u i).ofLp a *
              (F.u j).ofLp c

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval y p| ≤ M) (hx : |x| < 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p)| ≤ ↑q * M / √(1 - x ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Bernstein's inequality** for algebraic polynomials. If `p` has degree at most `q` and
`|p| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|p'(x)| ≤ q M / √(1 − x²)` for `|x| < 1`.

Source: Bernstein (1912); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7; Cheney,
*Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas: `bernstein-polynomial-inequality`.
Proof (algebraic form of the trigonometric argument): with `a = x = cos θ₀`, `b = √(1 − x²)`, the
odd part of `θ ↦ p(cos(θ₀ + θ))` is `sin θ · r(cos θ)` for a polynomial `r` of degree `< q` (built
from Hasse derivatives of `p`), `√(1 − y²) |r(y)| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, and `r(1) = −b p'(x)`; Schur's
inequality `abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le` at `y = 1` gives
`b |p'(x)| ≤ q M`.
atlas: bernstein-polynomial-inequality

signature:

  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p)| ≤ ↑q ^ 2 * M
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Markov brothers' inequality** (the first Markov inequality, sharp constant). If `p` has
degree at most `q` and `|p| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|p'(x)| ≤ q² M` for all `x ∈ [−1, 1]`.

Source: A. A. Markov (1889); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), Thm 2.24 / §2.7;
Cheney, *Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas: `markov-brothers`.
Proof: Bernstein's inequality `abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le` gives
`√(1 − y²) |p'(y)| ≤ q M` on `[−1, 1]`, and Schur's inequality
`abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le` applied to `p'` (degree `< q`) gives
`|p'(x)| ≤ q · q M`. The equality case (`p = ±M T_q`, `x = ±1`) is not formalised.
atlas: markov-brothers

name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_two_mul_sq_div_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Markov brothers' inequality on an interval.** If `p` has degree at most `q` and `|p| ≤ M` on
`[a, b]` (`a < b`), then `|p'(x)| ≤ 2 q² / (b − a) · M` for all `x ∈ [a, b]`.

Source: A. A. Markov (1889); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7 (affine
rescaling of `abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le`). Atlas: `markov-brothers`.
atlas: markov-brothers

signature:

  |Polynomial.eval x r| ≤ ↑q * M
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Schur's inequality.** If `r` has degree `< q` and `√(1 − y²) |r(y)| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then
`|r(x)| ≤ q M` on `[−1, 1]`.

Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7 (Schur's lemma); Cheney,
*Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Proof: for `|x| ≤ cos(π/(2q))` directly from
`√(1 − x²) ≥ sin(π/(2q)) ≥ 1/q`; for `x ≥ cos(π/(2q))` by Lagrange interpolation at the zeros
`ξ_k` of `T_q`, where all partial nodal products are nonnegative and the weights satisfy
`|r(ξ_k)| / |T_q'(ξ_k)| ≤ M/q`, so `|r(x)| ≤ (M/q) T_q'(x) ≤ q M`; the case `x ≤ −cos(π/(2q))` by
reflection. Atlas: auxiliary for `markov-brothers` and `bernstein-polynomial-inequality`.
atlas: schur-polynomial-inequality

  |NLAlib.slqEstimate A (fun x => 1 / x) Q G - NLAlib.hutchinsonEstimate (cfc (fun x => 1 / x) A) G| ≤

`lanczos-gauss-quadrature`, `inverse-polynomial-approx`.

  |NLAlib.slqEstimate A f Q G - NLAlib.hutchinsonEstimate (cfc f A) G| ≤ 2 * E * NLAlib.hutchinsonEstimate 1 G

`abs_slqEstimate_sub_hutchinsonEstimate_le_of_degree_lt_two_mul` with `natDegree p ≤ 2q − 1`.
If `A` is symmetric with spectrum in `[a, c]`, each `Q_k` has orthonormal columns with
`K_q(A, g_k) ⊆ range Q_k`, and `|f − p| ≤ E` on `[a, c]`, then
`|SLQ − tr_m f(A)| ≤ 2E · tr_m(I)`.

uses `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`.

name: NLAlib.abs_slqEstimate_sub_hutchinsonEstimate_le_of_degree_lt_two_mul
doc:
**SLQ quadrature error, deterministic.** If `A` is symmetric with spectrum in `[a, c]`,
each `Q_k` has orthonormal columns with `K_q(A, g_k) ⊆ range Q_k`, and `|f − p| ≤ E` on `[a, c]`
for a polynomial `p` of degree `< 2q`, then `|SLQ − tr_m f(A)| ≤ 2E · tr_m(I)`, where `tr_m` is
the Hutchinson estimator with the same test vectors and `tr_m(I) = (1/m) ∑ₖ ‖g_k‖²`.
Source: Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], proof of Thm 4.1 (Lemma 4.2). Atlas: `slq-error`;
uses `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_sub_eval_interpolate_chebyshevZero_le {f : ℝ → ℝ} {q : ℕ} {M : ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1))
  (hf' : ∀ k ≤ q, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) (Set.Ioo (-1) 1))
  (hM : ∀ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo (-1) 1, |iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ| ≤ M) (x : ℝ) :
  x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1 →
    |f x -
          Polynomial.eval x
            ((Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ (NLAlib.chebyshevZero (q + 1))) (f ∘ NLAlib.chebyshevZero (q + 1)))| ≤
      M / (2 ^ q * ↑(q + 1).factorial)
name: NLAlib.abs_sub_eval_interpolate_chebyshevZero_le
doc:
**Chebyshev interpolation error.** Let `f` be continuous on `[−1, 1]` with
`f, f', …, f^{(q)}` differentiable on `(−1, 1)` and `|f^{(q+1)}| ≤ M` on `(−1, 1)`. The polynomial
interpolating `f` at the `q + 1` zeros of `T_{q+1}` satisfies
`|f x − L(x)| ≤ M / (2^q (q + 1)!)` for every `x ∈ [−1, 1]`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, Ch. 8 (Chebyshev nodes); Trefethen, *Approximation Theory and
Approximation Practice*, Ch. 11; Cheney, Ch. 3.
Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error`; uses `interpolation-remainder`.
Deviation: the derivative bound is assumed only on the open interval `(−1, 1)` (weaker than
on `[−1, 1]`).
atlas: chebyshev-interpolation-error

signature:
NLAlib.aeval_mulVec_eq_and_charpoly_is_unique_minimiser.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

      p.degree < ↑q →
        Q.mulVec (((Polynomial.aeval (Q.transpose * A * Q)) p).mulVec (Q.transpose.mulVec b)) =
          ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b) ∧
    (∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),
        p.degree ≤ ↑q →
          Q.transpose.mulVec (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b) =
            ((Polynomial.aeval (Q.transpose * A * Q)) p).mulVec (Q.transpose.mulVec b)) ∧
      (Q.mulVecLin.range = NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q →
        q ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade A b →
          (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly.Monic ∧
            (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly.degree = ↑q ∧
              (∀ x ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q,
                  x ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly).mulVec b = 0) ∧
                ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),

                            ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly).mulVec b ≤

                        (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b =
                            ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly).mulVec b ⬝ᵥ

                          p = (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly))

compression. The first two identities need only `K_q ⊆ range Q`; minimality and uniqueness

orthogonal to `K_q`. Source: the manuscript's section `rt:compression`, following
(rt:power-exact); Saad (1992), Lemma 3.1. Deviation: arbitrary
finite column labels, squared dot-product norms, and also `q = 0`; no symmetry assumption.

signature: NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (k : ℕ) (A : Matrix m n ℝ) : ℝ

doc:
The actual rank-constrained optimal squared Frobenius error, as an
infimum over all feasible matrices. Eckart–Young proves it is attained.
Atlas `eckart-young`; intended for relative RSVD/GN error statements.

signature:
NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq_eq_singularValueTailSq {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :

The genuine optimal rank-`k` squared Frobenius error equals the spectral
tail. All ranks, rectangular shapes and zero dimensions are included.

NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq_eq_singularValueTailSq_reindex.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

Frobenius Eckart–Young identifies the genuine optimal error on arbitrary

NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq_eq_zero_of_width_le {m n k : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (hnk : n ≤ k) :

A target rank at least the input width has zero optimal Frobenius error.

NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)

The actual optimal squared Frobenius error is nonnegative.

Equivalent row and column labels preserve the actual rank-constrained
optimal squared Frobenius error. Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

signature:
NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (Ω : Matrix n s ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)
name: NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace
doc:
The block Krylov subspace `K_q(A, Ω) = span {(A^i Ω) e_j : i < q, j ∈ s}`, the range of
`[Ω, AΩ, …, A^(q−1)Ω]`. Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Alg. 2; Saad (2011) [`saad11`],
§6.3.
atlas: block-krylov-subspace

signature:
NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace_eq_iSup.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (Ω : Matrix n s ℝ) (q : ℕ) : NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace A Ω q = ⨆ j, NLAlib.krylovSpace A (Ω.col j) q
name: NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace_eq_iSup
doc:
The block Krylov space is the sum of the single-vector Krylov spaces of the columns:
`K_q(A, Ω) = ∑_j K_q(A, Ω e_j)`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3.
atlas: block-krylov-subspace

signature:
NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace_mono.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (Ω : Matrix n s ℝ) {q q' : ℕ} (h : q ≤ q') : NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace A Ω q ≤ NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace A Ω q'
name: NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace_mono
doc:
Block Krylov spaces are nested: `q ≤ q' → K_q(A, Ω) ⊆ K_{q'}(A, Ω)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3.
atlas: block-krylov-subspace

The actual canonical QR frame, using the coordinate frame on the
rank-deficient set. On full rank its diagonal normalizations are positive.

NLAlib.canonicalQRFrame_mul_canonicalQRUpper {n k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) (A : Fin n → Fin k → ℝ)

  Matrix.of ↑(NLAlib.canonicalQRFrame n k hkn A) * NLAlib.canonicalQRUpper hkn A = Matrix.of A

doc:
The literal canonical factors multiply to the original full-column-rank
input. Together with triangularity and positive diagonal, this is an actual
canonical thin QR decomposition. Source: operator re-derivation `sh:qr-equiv`.

NLAlib.canonicalQRFrame_orthogonal_mul {n k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) (O : ↥(Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))

Canonical positive-diagonal QR frame equivariance on the full-rank set.

signature:
NLAlib.canonicalQRFrame_val_of_linearIndependent {n k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) (A : Fin n → Fin k → ℝ)

  ↑(NLAlib.canonicalQRFrame n k hkn A) = NLAlib.qrNormalizedArray A

doc:
The canonical frame is literal normalized Gram–Schmidt on full rank.
Source: operator re-derivation `sh:gaussian-qr`.

signature: NLAlib.canonicalQRUpper {n k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) (A : Fin n → Fin k → ℝ) : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ
name: NLAlib.canonicalQRUpper
doc:
The upper factor consists of inner products between canonical frame
columns and original columns. Source: operator re-derivation `sh:qr-equiv`.

signature:
NLAlib.canonicalQRUpper.congr_simp {n k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) (A A✝ : Fin n → Fin k → ℝ) (e_A : A = A✝) (a✝ a✝¹ : Fin k) :

name: NLAlib.canonicalQRUpper.congr_simp

signature:
NLAlib.canonicalQRUpper_apply_eq_zero_of_lt {n k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) (A : Fin n → Fin k → ℝ)
  (hA : LinearIndependent ℝ (NLAlib.qrColumnFamily A)) {i j : Fin k} (hij : j < i) :

The canonical upper factor has zero entries strictly below its diagonal
on full-column-rank inputs. Source: operator re-derivation `sh:qr-equiv`.

signature:
NLAlib.canonicalQRUpper_apply_self_pos {n k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) (A : Fin n → Fin k → ℝ)

Every canonical QR diagonal entry is the strictly positive residual norm
on full-column-rank inputs. Source: operator re-derivation `sh:qr-equiv`.

signature:
NLAlib.canonicalQRUpper_orthogonal_mul {n k : ℕ} (hkn : k ≤ n) (O : ↥(Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))

name: NLAlib.canonicalQRUpper_orthogonal_mul

The canonical upper factor is unchanged by orthogonal left multiplication.
Source: operator re-derivation `sh:qr-equiv`.

signature:
NLAlib.card_image_univ_sequence_le.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [DecidableEq α] {k : ℕ} (I : Fin k → α) :
  (Finset.image I Finset.univ).card ≤ k
name: NLAlib.card_image_univ_sequence_le
doc:
A sequence's distinct support has cardinality at most its length.
Source: operator re-derivation `sh:convex-sampling`.

signature:
NLAlib.card_le_card_of_hasOrthonormalCols.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {r : Type u_2} [Fintype r]
  [DecidableEq r] {Q : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) : Fintype.card r ≤ Fintype.card n

doc:
A real matrix with orthonormal columns has at most as many columns as rows (general finite
index types). Helper for interlacing; atlas `orthonormal-completion`.
atlas: orthonormal-completion

name: NLAlib.card_le_finrank_inf_add

signature:
NLAlib.card_le_of_transpose_mul_self_eq_one.{u_4} {k : ℕ} {ι : Type u_4} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (V : Matrix (Fin k) ι ℝ) (hV : V.transpose * V = 1) : Fintype.card ι ≤ k
