doc:
A real matrix with orthonormal columns has at most as many columns as rows.
Ported from the Prove2me workspace (Gaussian Random Matrices series). Atlas
`orthonormal-completion`.

signature:
NLAlib.card_le_succ_of_sawtoothError_eq_zero {n : ℕ} {s : Finset ℝ} (hs : ∀ t ∈ s, t ∈ Set.Icc 0 Real.pi)
  (hz : ∀ t ∈ s, NLAlib.sawtoothError n t = 0) : s.card ≤ n + 1
name: NLAlib.card_le_succ_of_sawtoothError_eq_zero
doc:
Every finite set of half-period sawtooth-error zeros has at most `n+1` points.
Rolle's theorem interleaves those zeros with the already exhausted `n` critical points.
Source: operator rederivations `rt:sawtooth` (`jackson-lipschitz`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.card_sawtoothCriticalAngles (n : ℕ) : (NLAlib.sawtoothCriticalAngles n).card = n
name: NLAlib.card_sawtoothCriticalAngles
doc:
The actual angular critical points have cardinality exactly `n`.
Source: operator rederivations `rt:sawtooth` (`jackson-lipschitz`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.card_sawtoothCriticalCosines (n : ℕ) : (NLAlib.sawtoothCriticalCosines n).card = n
name: NLAlib.card_sawtoothCriticalCosines
doc:
The selected cosine roots are all distinct, hence their cardinality is exactly `n`.
Source: operator rederivations `rt:sawtooth` (`jackson-lipschitz`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.card_sawtoothZeroGrid (n : ℕ) : (NLAlib.sawtoothZeroGrid n).card = n + 1
name: NLAlib.card_sawtoothZeroGrid
doc:
The positive half-period grid has exactly `n+1` distinct error zeros.
Source: operator rederivations `rt:sawtooth` (`jackson-lipschitz`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.card_walshIndex (b : ℕ) : Fintype.card (NLAlib.WalshIndex b) = 2 ^ b
name: NLAlib.card_walshIndex
doc:
The Walsh row and column index set has `2^b` elements.
Source: operator re-derivation `sh:srht`.

signature:
NLAlib.cfc_diagonal_real.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ι → ℝ) :
  cfc f (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(x i)) = Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(f (x i))
name: NLAlib.cfc_diagonal_real
doc:
Real functional calculus acts entrywise on a real diagonal matrix.
Arbitrary real functions are allowed because the diagonal spectrum is finite.
Source: the private `cfc_diag` proof in `JointTensorRepresentation`, via Mathlib's
diagonal algebra homomorphism and Pi CFC; Tropp 2015, §2.1.11;
atlas `golden-thompson`, `operator-monotone-convex` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.cfc_eq_aeval_interpolate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (f : ℝ → ℝ) : cfc f A = (Polynomial.aeval A) ((Lagrange.interpolate (Finset.image hA.eigenvalues Finset.univ) id) f)
name: NLAlib.cfc_eq_aeval_interpolate
doc:
`f(A)` is `p(A)` for the Lagrange interpolant `p` of `f` at the (distinct) eigenvalues of the
symmetric `A`. Standard (Higham 2008 [`higham08`], Def. 1.4). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error`
(helper; belongs in `NLAlib.Matrix.PolynomialCalculus`).

name: NLAlib.cfc_eq_aeval_of_forall_eval_eq
doc:
A matrix function of a symmetric `A` equals the polynomial calculus of any polynomial that
agrees with `f` at the eigenvalues: `f(A) = p(A)` when `p(λᵢ) = f(λᵢ)` for all `i`.
Standard (Higham 2008 [`higham08`], Def. 1.4 and Thm 1.12). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper;
belongs in `NLAlib.Matrix.PolynomialCalculus`).

signature:
NLAlib.cfc_unitary_conj.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (U : ↥(unitary (Matrix ι ι ℂ))) (f : ℝ → ℝ)
  (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) : cfc f (↑U * A * (↑U).conjTranspose) = ↑U * cfc f A * (↑U).conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.cfc_unitary_conj
doc:
Every real function on a Hermitian matrix's finite spectrum commutes with
unitary conjugation. No global continuity premise is needed. Source: Mathlib's
CFC transport and Tropp 2015, Theorem 8.5.2; atlas `golden-thompson`,
`operator-monotone-convex` (helper).

signature: NLAlib.cgObjective.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x : n → ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.cgObjective
doc:
The conjugate-gradient objective `φ(x) = ½ xᵀ A x − cᵀ x`. Its minimiser over `ℝⁿ` (for
positive definite `A`) solves `A x = c`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], eq. (38.6).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (c u d : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c (u + d) = NLAlib.cgObjective A c u + d ⬝ᵥ (A.mulVec u - c) + NLAlib.quadForm A d / 2
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_add
doc:
Expansion of the CG objective along a direction: for symmetric `A`,
`φ(u + d) = φ(u) + dᵀ (A u − c) + ½ dᵀ A d`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], proof of
Thm 38.2. Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (z : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c z = NLAlib.cgObjective A c xs + NLAlib.quadForm A (z - xs) / 2
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub
doc:
The CG objective measures the `A`-norm error: if `A x⋆ = c` then
`φ(z) = φ(x⋆) + ½ ‖z − x⋆‖_A²`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], eq. (38.7).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A W : Matrix n n ℝ) (c y : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c (W.mulVec y) = NLAlib.cgObjective (W.transpose * A * W) (W.transpose.mulVec c) y
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_mulVec
doc:
The CG objective under a change of variables: `φ_{A,c}(Wy) = φ_{WᵀAW, Wᵀc}(y)`.
Helper for `preconditioned-cg`.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex (N k : ℕ) : ℕ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex
doc:
Frequency folding into the degree range of the canonical Chebyshev extrema grid.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 4.1 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex_le {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex N k ≤ N
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAliasIndex_le
doc:
Every folded frequency has degree at most the grid cutoff.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 4.1 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier
doc:
The gap-amplifying polynomial `chebyshevAmplifier α γ q = T_q(X/α) / T_q(1 + γ)`: equal to
`1` at `α(1 + γ)`, increasing beyond it, and exponentially small on `[−α, α]`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Lem. 4–5; Atlas: `chebyshev-amplifier`.
atlas: chebyshev-amplifier

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier_def (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier α γ q =
    Polynomial.C (1 / Polynomial.eval (1 + γ) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)) *
      (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q).comp (Polynomial.C (1 / α) * Polynomial.X)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier_def

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff (F : ℂ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff
doc:
The real Chebyshev coefficients are the real parts of the standard contour coefficients.
For a function real on `[-1,1]` these are the usual real Chebyshev expansion coefficients.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, Theorem 8.1 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant (F : ℂ → ℂ) (N : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant
doc:
The actual Lagrange interpolant on the `(N+1)`-point canonical Chebyshev extrema grid.
Mathlib totalizes the `N=0` grid at the point `1`; this convention is made explicit.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 2 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, definition).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc (F : ℂ → ℂ) (N : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc
doc:
The degree-`N` truncation of the canonical real Chebyshev coefficients.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, definition).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction (F : ℂ → ℂ) (θ : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) : ℂ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction
doc:
Pull back a complex function on the Bernstein ellipse to the additive circle.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_coe_eq_cos (F : ℂ → ℂ) (θ : ℝ) : NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F ↑θ = F ↑(Real.cos θ)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_coe_eq_cos
doc:
The circle pullback evaluated at a real angle is exactly `F(cos θ)`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_neg (F : ℂ → ℂ) (θ : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F (-θ) = NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F θ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction_neg
doc:
The circle pullback is even, by the inversion symmetry of the Joukowski transform.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff (F : ℂ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) : ℂ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff
doc:
Complex Chebyshev coefficients in their Joukowski contour form. The zeroth coefficient
has normalization `1/(2πi)`; positive coefficients have normalization `1/(πi)`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapter 8, Theorem 8.1 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff (F : ℂ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff F k = (if k = 0 then 1 else 2) * fourierCoeff (NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F) ↑k
name: NLAlib.chebyshevComplexCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff
doc:
The contour definition agrees exactly with the standard Fourier definition of the
Chebyshev coefficients, including the distinct zeroth normalization.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-coeff-analytic-decay`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (a b : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate
doc:
The Chebyshev iterate for spectrum in `[a, b]`: the polynomial method whose residual
polynomial is `chebyshevResidual a b q = T_q((b + a − 2X)/(b − a)) / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`,
i.e. iteration polynomial `(1 − chebyshevResidual a b q) /ₘ X`. Source: Saad (2003)
[`saad03`], §12.3; Golub–Varga (1961) [`gv61`]. Deviation: defined by its polynomial; the
three-term recurrence of Saad Alg. 12.1 is not formalised.
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_sub_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
  (hab : a < b) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_sub_mem_krylovSpace
doc:
The Chebyshev iterate lies in `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)` (its iteration polynomial has degree
`< q`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual
doc:
The shifted, scaled Chebyshev polynomial normalised to `1` at `0`:
`chebyshevResidual a b q = T_q((b + a − 2 X)/(b − a)) / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`. For `0 < a < b`
it has the smallest maximum modulus on `[a, b]` among polynomials of degree at most `q` with
value `1` at `0` (the residual polynomial of Chebyshev iteration and the model for CG).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.
atlas: inverse-polynomial-approx

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevResidual_def (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevResidual a b q =
    Polynomial.C (1 / Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)) *
      (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q).comp (Polynomial.C ((b + a) / (b - a)) - Polynomial.C (2 / (b - a)) * Polynomial.X)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual_def

signature:
NLAlib.chernoff_matrix_mgf_cgf_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L)
  (hMeas : Measurable X) (hHerm : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X ω).IsHermitian)
  (hBound : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, 0 ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMin (X ω) ∧ NLAlib.lambdaMax (X ω) ≤ L) (θ : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.LoewnerLE (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ)
      (NLAlib.matrixExp (NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient L θ • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ)) ∧
    NLAlib.LoewnerLE (NLAlib.matrixLog (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ))
      (NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient L θ • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ)
name: NLAlib.chernoff_matrix_mgf_cgf_le
doc:
For a random positive semidefinite `X` with `λmax X ≤ L`, `𝔼 matrixExp (θ • X) ≼ matrixExp (g(θ) •
𝔼 X)` and `matrixLog 𝔼 matrixExp (θ • X) ≼ g(θ) • 𝔼 X`, where `g = chernoffCgfCoefficient L`.

Tropp 2015, Lemma 5.4.1. Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 5*.

Stated for all real `θ`; `L = 0` is handled by the piecewise definition of
`chernoffCgfCoefficient`.

name: NLAlib.completion_reduction
doc:
**Exact Gaussian completion, deterministic reduction** (Chen–Persson, Lemma
`lem:completion`; Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Thm 5.1).

Fixed `Q` (orthonormal columns, `q ≥ 1`), its orthogonal completion `Qp = Q⊥`
(`QQᵀ + Q⊥Q⊥ᵀ = I`), fixed `A`, random `Ψ` with `s ≥ q + 2`; `G₁ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q`,
`G₂ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q⊥`, `E = residual Q A = (I − QQᵀ)A`.
* `hG₁`: `G₁` has full column rank a.s. (so `G₁†G₁ = I`), the "almost surely" of the paper;
* `hG₂`: `E‖G₁†G₂(Q⊥ᵀE)‖_F² = E‖G₁†‖_F² · ‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F²` — `lem:moments` for `G₂` conditionally
  on `G₁` (independence of `G₁`, `G₂`) followed by the tower property;
* `hG₁m`: `E‖G₁†‖_F² = q/(s−q−1)` — `lem:invmom` (needs `s ≥ q+2`, `q ≥ 1`);
* `hGi`: integrability of the noise term.
Everything else in the paper's proof (`ΨᵀA = G₁QᵀA + G₂Q⊥ᵀE`, `X̂ = QᵀA + G₁†G₂Q⊥ᵀE`,
Pythagoras, `‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F = ‖E‖_F`) is proved in `SketchedRegression.lean` and used here.
Conclusion: `eq:completion`,
`E‖A − Q(ΨᵀQ)†ΨᵀA‖_F² = (1 + q/(s−q−1)) ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²`.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (helper; uses `sketched-regression`, `orthonormal-completion`).
atlas: gn-expected-error

NLAlib.coreNoise.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_5} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3} {s : Type u_5} [Fintype m]

name: NLAlib.coreNoise
doc:
The core noise `E_core = (ΨᵀQ)† Ψᵀ A⊥` with `A⊥ = (I - QQᵀ)A` (Chen–Persson,
`eq:tGN-fitted-core`, `lem:tGN-core`). Not in the LRA source, which writes the expression
out. Atlas `sketched-regression`.
atlas: sketched-regression

signature:
NLAlib.coreNoise_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3} {r : Type u_4} {s : Type u_5}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype q] [Fintype r] [Fintype s] [DecidableEq q] [DecidableEq m] (Q : Matrix m q ℝ) (Qp : Matrix m r ℝ)
  (Ψ : Matrix m s ℝ) (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hcomp : Q * Q.transpose + Qp * Qp.transpose = 1) :
  NLAlib.coreNoise Q Ψ A = NLAlib.pinvL (Ψ.transpose * Q) * (Ψ.transpose * Qp) * (Qp.transpose * NLAlib.residual Q A)
name: NLAlib.coreNoise_eq
doc:
Deterministic core of `lem:tGN-core` and `eq:tGN-fitted-core` (Chen–Persson): the noise
term `E_core = (ΨᵀQ)† Ψᵀ A⊥` equals `G₁† G₂ B` with `G₁ = ΨᵀQ`, `G₂ = ΨᵀQ⊥`, `B = Q⊥ᵀ A⊥`, where
`A⊥ = (I - QQᵀ)A = residual Q A` (LRA `core_noise_eq`, there with the noise written out).
Atlas `sketched-regression`.

NLAlib.covariance_rotation_eq.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} (X Y : ι → Ω → ℝ)
  (hXY : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω => (fun t => X t ω, fun t => Y t ω)) P)
  (hX0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ∂P = 0) (hY0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), Y t ω ∂P = 0)
  (hcross : ∀ (s t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X s ω * Y t ω ∂P = 0) (θ : ℝ) (i j : ι) :
  ProbabilityTheory.covariance (fun ω => -Real.sin θ * X i ω + Real.cos θ * Y i ω)
      (fun ω => Real.cos θ * X j ω + Real.sin θ * Y j ω) P =
    Real.sin θ * Real.cos θ * (∫ (ω : Ω), Y i ω * Y j ω ∂P - ∫ (ω : Ω), X i ω * X j ω ∂P)

process `Z(θ) = cos θ X + sin θ Y`, for jointly Gaussian centred `X, Y` with vanishing cross

interpolation proofs (Vershynin 2018, proof of Thm 7.2.1). Atlas: helper of `slepian`,
`sudakov-fernique`, `gordon-minimax`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.slepian_tail_comparison` (helper `sl_cov_DZ`).

signature:
NLAlib.degree_le_and_abs_sub_chebyshev_approximations_le_of_open_ellipse {f : ℝ → ℝ} {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ)) (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
  (hmatch : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, F ↑x = ↑(f x)) (N : ℕ) :
  (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc F N).degree ≤ ↑N ∧
    (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant F N).degree ≤ ↑N ∧
      ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1,
        |f x - Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticTrunc F N)| ≤ 2 * M / ρ ^ N / (ρ - 1) ∧
          |f x - Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant F N)| ≤ 4 * M / ρ ^ N / (ρ - 1)
name: NLAlib.degree_le_and_abs_sub_chebyshev_approximations_le_of_open_ellipse
doc:
Both canonical analytic Chebyshev approximations satisfy their exact source constants:
the coefficient truncation has error `2Mρ⁻ᴺ/(ρ-1)`, and the actual `(N+1)`-point grid
interpolant has error `4Mρ⁻ᴺ/(ρ-1)`. Both polynomials have degree at most `N`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 8.2; original open-ellipse assumptions, with the `N=0`
grid convention inherited explicitly from Mathlib's `node`.
atlas: chebyshev-approx-analytic

signature:

doc:
**Residual polynomials of degree `≤ q`** are exactly the `1 − X s` with `deg s < q`:

(atlas `residual-polynomial`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.det_gram_fromCols_eq_mul_frobSq_sub_projector.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype k]

doc:
Appending one column multiplies the Gram determinant by its squared distance

Deshpande--Rademacher--Vempala--Wang (2006), determinant-weighted projection identity.

signature:
NLAlib.det_gram_fromCols_eq_mul_frobenius_norm_sq_sub_complexColumnProjector.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {k : Type u_2}

Appending a genuine complex column multiplies its Gram determinant by

signature:
NLAlib.det_smul_one_sub_jacobiMatrix (a β : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
  (x • 1 - NLAlib.jacobiMatrix a β (m + 2)).det =
    (x - a 0) * (x • 1 - NLAlib.jacobiMatrix (fun i => a (i + 1)) (fun i => β (i + 1)) (m + 1)).det -
      β 1 ^ 2 * (x • 1 - NLAlib.jacobiMatrix (fun i => a (i + 2)) (fun i => β (i + 2)) m).det
name: NLAlib.det_smul_one_sub_jacobiMatrix
doc:
Determinant recurrence of a Jacobi matrix along its first row:
`det(x − J) = (x − a₀) det(x − J') − β₁² det(x − J'')` with `J'`, `J''` the trailing blocks
(shifted coefficients). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3.

signature:
NLAlib.diag_eq_ofReal_re_of_complex_posSemidef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} {R : Matrix n n ℂ} (hR : R.PosSemidef) (i : n) :

The Hermitian dilation as a real-linear map. Tropp 2015, Def. 2.1.5. Atlas:

signature:
NLAlib.dilation_identities {m n : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero n] (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ) :
  (NLAlib.dilation A).IsHermitian ∧
    NLAlib.dilation A ^ 2 = Matrix.fromBlocks (A * A.conjTranspose) 0 0 (A.conjTranspose * A) ∧
      NLAlib.lambdaMax (NLAlib.dilation A) = NLAlib.spectralNorm (NLAlib.dilation A) ∧
        NLAlib.spectralNorm (NLAlib.dilation A) = NLAlib.spectralNorm A
name: NLAlib.dilation_identities
doc:
The Hermitian dilation of `A` is Hermitian, squares to `fromBlocks (A Aᴴ) 0 0 (Aᴴ A)`, and has
`λmax = ‖dilation A‖ = ‖A‖`.

Tropp 2015, Def. 2.1.5 and eqs (2.1.27–28). Atlas: `hermitian-dilation`. Ported from the Prove2me
mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.
atlas: hermitian-dilation

signature:
NLAlib.dilation_sq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
  (X : Matrix m n ℂ) : NLAlib.dilation X ^ 2 = Matrix.fromBlocks (X * X.conjTranspose) 0 0 (X.conjTranspose * X)
name: NLAlib.dilation_sq
doc:
The square of the Hermitian dilation is block diagonal: `(dilation X)² =
fromBlocks (X Xᴴ) 0 0 (Xᴴ X)`. Tropp 2015, eq. (2.1.28). Atlas: `hermitian-dilation`.

signature:
NLAlib.div_pow_sub_one_le_of_log_steps {D η ρ : ℝ} (hD : 0 < D) (hη : 0 < η) (hρ : 1 < ρ) {q : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q)
  (hsteps : (1 + Real.log (D / (η * (ρ - 1))) / Real.log ρ) / 2 ≤ ↑q) : D / ρ ^ (2 * q - 1) / (ρ - 1) ≤ η
name: NLAlib.div_pow_sub_one_le_of_log_steps
doc:
The explicit step condition `q ≥ (1+log(D/(η(ρ-1)))/logρ)/2` pays a geometric error
`D/(ρ^(2q-1)(ρ-1)) ≤ η`, for `D,η>0`, `ρ>1`, and integer `q≥1`.
Source: solving the geometric rate in Trefethen, ATAP, Theorem 8.2;
operator rederivations `rt:slq` (analytic SLQ step budget).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_charpoly_mulVec_eq_zero_of_mem_range.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (b : n → ℝ) (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (Fintype.card k) ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {x : n → ℝ}
  (hx : x ∈ Q.mulVecLin.range) : x ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly).mulVec b = 0
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_charpoly_mulVec_eq_zero_of_mem_range
doc:
The compression's characteristic residual is orthogonal to its range, hence to the
Krylov space it contains. Source: the manuscript's monic least-residual argument following
(rt:power-exact). No symmetry assumption is used.
atlas: krylov-polynomial-exactness (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_charpoly_mulVec_self_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2}
  [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ)
  (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (Fintype.card k) ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.Monic)
  (hpdeg : p.degree = ↑(Fintype.card k)) :
  ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly).mulVec b ⬝ᵥ
      ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly).mulVec b ≤
    ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_charpoly_mulVec_self_le
doc:
The characteristic polynomial of a Krylov compression minimises `‖p(A)b‖²` among monic
polynomials of its degree. Source: the manuscript's monic least-residual argument following
(rt:power-exact). The containing-space hypothesis suffices for minimality; `A` is arbitrary.
atlas: krylov-polynomial-exactness (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_degree_lt_two_mul.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsSymm) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < 2 * ↑q) :
  b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b =
    Q.transpose.mulVec b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval (Q.transpose * A * Q)) p).mulVec (Q.transpose.mulVec b)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_degree_lt_two_mul
doc:
**Gauss (Lanczos) quadrature is exact for degree `< 2q`.** If `A` is symmetric, `Q` has
orthonormal columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, then for every polynomial `p` with
`deg p < 2q`, `bᵀ p(A) b = (Qᵀb)ᵀ p(QᵀAQ) (Qᵀb)`. Valid for every `q` (at `q = 0`, `p = 0`).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 6.6 and §7.1; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021) [`ctu21`],
Thm 2.1.
Deviation: any orthonormal `Q` whose range contains `K_q(A,b)`; with the Lanczos basis,
`Qᵀb = ‖b‖e₁` and the right side is `‖b‖² (p(T_q))₁₁`.
atlas: lanczos-gauss-quadrature

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_krylovSpace_le
doc:
**Gauss (Lanczos) quadrature is exact for degree `≤ 2q − 1`** (`natDegree` form, `q ≥ 1`).
The form of `dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_degree_lt_two_mul` with the truncated bound
`natDegree p ≤ 2q − 1`, kept for existing callers.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 6.6 and §7.1; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021) [`ctu21`],
Thm 2.1.
Deviation: any orthonormal `Q` whose range contains `K_q(A,b)`. The hypothesis `0 < q` is
needed here (at `q = 0` the bound `≤ 0` in ℕ admits constants and the claim fails unless
`b ∈ range Q`); the degree form needs no such hypothesis.
atlas: lanczos-gauss-quadrature

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  v ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v =
    ∑ i, Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p * ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
**Spectral-measure identity.** `vᵀ p(A) v = ∑ᵢ p(λᵢ) ⟨uᵢ, v⟩²` for real symmetric `A`.
Standard (Golub–Meurant 2010, §7.1); audit G3 C1/C2; atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`,
`spectral-measure`.
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_self_eq_charpoly_add.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2}
  [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ)
  (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (Fintype.card k) ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.Monic)
  (hpdeg : p.degree = ↑(Fintype.card k)) :
  ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b =
    ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly).mulVec b ⬝ᵥ
        ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly).mulVec b +
      ((Polynomial.aeval A) (p - (Q.transpose * A * Q).charpoly)).mulVec b ⬝ᵥ

A monic competitor of degree `card k` splits orthogonally into the characteristic residual
and a residual of smaller degree. Source: the manuscript's monic least-residual argument
following (rt:power-exact). Squared norms are explicit dot products; `A` is arbitrary real.

the grade. Equality of squared residual norms forces equality of polynomials.

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
Eigen-expansion of a quadratic form of a matrix function: for symmetric `A`,
`vᵀ f(A) v = ∑ᵢ f(λᵢ) (uᵢ ⬝ v)²` with `(λᵢ, uᵢ)` the eigenpairs of `A`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 7, eq. (7.1). Atlas: `spectral-measure` (helper;
belongs with the polynomial calculus in `NLAlib.Matrix`).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_self_le
doc:
**Spectral bound, `cfc` form.** If every eigenvalue of the symmetric `A` lies in `S` and
`|g| ≤ M` on `S`, then `‖g(A) v‖² ≤ M² ‖v‖²`. The `cfc` form of
`dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_self_le` (Saad 2003, §6.11). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper; the
`cfc` form of `polynomial-spectral-bound`).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < ↑q) {a c E : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c)
  (hfp : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a c, |f x - Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ E) :
  ((cfc f A).mulVec b - NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q A f b) ⬝ᵥ ((cfc f A).mulVec b - NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q A f b) ≤
    (2 * E) ^ 2 * b ⬝ᵥ b
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le
doc:
**Lanczos-FA error bound.** Let `A` be symmetric with every eigenvalue in `[a, c]`, `Q` with
orthonormal columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, and `p` a polynomial with `deg p < q` and
`|f − p| ≤ E` on `[a, c]`. Then `‖f(A) b − Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b‖² ≤ (2E)² ‖b‖²`, i.e.
`‖f(A) b − Q f(T) Qᵀ b‖ ≤ 2E ‖b‖`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.4 (with Lemma 3.1);
Druskin–Knizhnerman (1989) [`dk89`]; Higham (2008) [`higham08`], §13.2.
Deviation: an arbitrary approximant `p` in place of the best one (minimise over `p` to get the
printed form); squared Euclidean norms as dot products; no `q ≥ 1` (at `q = 0`, `p = 0`).
atlas: lanczos-fa-error

NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le_of_open_bernsteinEllipse.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1}

operator rederivations `rt:fa-bound` and `rt:analytic-approx`.

doc:
Upper Rayleigh bound from an eigenvalue enclosure: `xᵀ A x ≤ c ‖x‖²` if every eigenvalue is
at most `c`. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Thm 4.2.2. Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_of_mem_range.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]

  (hy : y ∈ Q.mulVecLin.range) : y ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec y ≤ θ * y ⬝ᵥ y

doc:
Rayleigh quotients over `range Q` are bounded by any upper bound `θ` on the eigenvalues of
`QᵀAQ` (the Ritz values), for `Q` with orthonormal columns: `yᵀAy ≤ θ ‖y‖²` for `y ∈ range Q`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_pow_le_dotProduct_pow_mulVec.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m]
  {M : Matrix m m ℝ} (hM : M.PosSemidef) {y : m → ℝ} (hy : y ⬝ᵥ y ≤ 1) {s : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) :

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_pow_le_dotProduct_pow_mulVec
doc:
**Jensen for a positive semidefinite quadratic form.** For `M ⪰ 0`, a vector `y` with
`y ⬝ y ≤ 1` and `s ≥ 1`, `(yᵀMy)^s ≤ yᵀM^s y`. With `y = Σᵢ cᵢuᵢ` in an eigenbasis this is
`(Σᵢ cᵢ²λᵢ)^s ≤ Σᵢ cᵢ²λᵢ^s`, convexity of `t ↦ t^s` on `t ≥ 0` with total weight `Σᵢ cᵢ² ≤ 1`.
HMT 2011, proof of Prop 8.6. Atlas `power-iteration-deterministic` (helper; belongs in
`Matrix/PolynomialCalculus.lean`).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_sub_le_of_isCGLSIterate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : Type u_2}
  [Fintype m] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {σlo σhi : ℝ} (hlo : 0 < σlo) (hlohi : σlo ≤ σhi)

  (hup : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v ≤ σhi ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v) {b : m → ℝ} {x₀ xs x : n → ℝ}
  (hxs : A.transpose.mulVec (A.mulVec xs) = A.transpose.mulVec b) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate A b x₀ q x) :
  A.mulVec (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x - xs) ≤
    (2 * ((σhi - σlo) / (σhi + σlo)) ^ q) ^ 2 * A.mulVec (x₀ - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x₀ - xs)

doc:
**CGLS/LSQR convergence, `κ(A)` rate.** Let `A : ℝ^{m×n}` have all singular values in
`[σ_lo, σ_hi]`, `0 < σ_lo ≤ σ_hi`, stated as `σ_lo² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖² ≤ σ_hi² ‖v‖²` for all `v` (so `A`

CGLS iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖A(x − x⋆)‖² ≤ (2((σ_hi − σ_lo)/(σ_hi + σ_lo))^q)² ‖A(x₀ − x⋆)‖²`.

Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3; Paige–Saunders (1982) [`ps82`].
Deviation: squared norms; the singular-value hypothesis in Rayleigh form.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound

  {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {b : m → ℝ} {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.transpose.mulVec (A.mulVec xs) = A.transpose.mulVec b)
  (x : n → ℝ) :
  (b - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec x) = (b - A.mulVec xs) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec xs) + A.mulVec (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_self_eq_add
doc:
**Residual splitting for least squares.** If `x⋆` solves the normal equations
`AᵀA x⋆ = Aᵀb`, then `‖b − Ax‖² = ‖b − Ax⋆‖² + ‖A(x − x⋆)‖²` for every `x`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 11.1.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound (partial)

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_eq_dotProduct_mulVec
doc:
An eigenvalue is the Rayleigh quotient of its unit eigenvector: `λᵢ = uᵢᵀ A uᵢ`.
Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature` (helper).

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_le_mul_tanSqAngle
doc:
**Rayleigh–Ritz step of Kaniel–Paige–Saad.** Let `A` be real symmetric with every
eigenvalue `≥ a`, `Q` with orthonormal columns, `θ₁ = θ_{j₁}` the largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`,
and `x ∈ range Q` with `u₁ ⬝ x ≠ 0` (`u₁ = u_{i₁}`). Then
`λ₁ − θ₁ ≤ (λ₁ − a) tan² ∠(u₁, x)` (from `λ₁ − xᵀAx/xᵀx ≤ (λ₁ − a) sin² ∠(u₁, x)`).
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], proof of Thm 6.4. Helper for `kaniel-paige-saad`.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₁ : n} {a c : ℝ} (hac : a < c)
  (hc : c < hA.eigenvalues i₁) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), i ≠ i₁ → hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c) (b : n → ℝ)
  (hb : (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0) (q : ℕ) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (q + 1) ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) (hT : (Q.transpose * A * Q).IsHermitian) {j₁ : k}
  (hj₁ : ∀ (j : k), hT.eigenvalues j ≤ hT.eigenvalues j₁) :
  hA.eigenvalues i₁ - hT.eigenvalues j₁ ≤
    (hA.eigenvalues i₁ - a) *
      (NLAlib.tanSqAngle (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp b /
        Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((hA.eigenvalues i₁ - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le
doc:
**Kaniel–Paige–Saad bound for the largest Ritz value.** Let `A` be real symmetric,
`λ₁ = λ_{i₁}`, every other eigenvalue in `[a, c]` with `a < c < λ₁` (e.g. `a = λₙ`, `c = λ₂`),
`u₁ ⬝ b ≠ 0`, `Q` with orthonormal columns and `K_{q+1}(A, b) ⊆ range Q` (e.g. a Lanczos basis),
and `θ₁` the largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`. Then
`λ₁ − θ₁ ≤ (λ₁ − a) tan² ∠(u₁, b) / T_q(1 + 2γ)²`, `γ = (λ₁ − c)/(c − a)`; the lower bound
`0 ≤ λ₁ − θ₁` is `eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 6.4 (`i = 1`); Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4.
Deviation: Krylov dimension `q + 1` (Saad's `m`, so `T_{m−1} = T_q`); `[a, c]` any enclosure
of the other eigenvalues (Saad: `a = λₙ`, `c = λ₂`, factor `λ₁ − λₙ`); any orthonormal `Q`
whose range contains the Krylov space.
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le_of_poly
doc:
**Kaniel–Paige–Saad, polynomial form.** Let `A` be real symmetric with every eigenvalue
`≥ a`, `u₁ ⬝ b ≠ 0`, `Q` with orthonormal columns and `K_q(A, b) ⊆ range Q`, and `θ₁` the
largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`. For every polynomial `p` with `deg p < q`, `p(λ₁) ≠ 0` and
`|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` for `i ≠ i₁`: `λ₁ − θ₁ ≤ (λ₁ − a) (M/p(λ₁))² tan² ∠(u₁, b)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], proof of Thm 6.4 (`i = 1`).
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₁ : n}
  (htop : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ≤ hA.eigenvalues i₁) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hT : (Q.transpose * A * Q).IsHermitian) (j : k) : hT.eigenvalues j ≤ hA.eigenvalues i₁
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le
doc:
The Ritz values are at most the top eigenvalue: `θⱼ ≤ λ_{i₁}` for every eigenvalue `θⱼ` of
`Qᵀ A Q`, `Q` with orthonormal columns. This is the lower half `0 ≤ λ₁ − θ₁` of the
Kaniel–Paige–Saad bound. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 6.4 (left inequality; Cauchy
interlacing).
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad (partial)

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_mem_Icc
doc:
The eigenvalues of the projected matrix `Qᵀ A Q` (`Q` with orthonormal columns) lie in any
interval `[a, c]` containing the eigenvalues of `A` (Ritz values interlace inside the spectral
interval). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4; Parlett (1998), Thm 10.1.1 (weak form).
Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_add_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (hB : B.IsHermitian) (hAB : (A + B).IsHermitian) (i j : Fin (Fintype.card n)) (hij : ↑i + ↑j < Fintype.card n) :
  hAB.eigenvalues₀ ⟨↑i + ↑j, hij⟩ ≤ hA.eigenvalues₀ i + hB.eigenvalues₀ j
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_add_le
doc:
**Weyl's inequality for eigenvalues.** For real symmetric `A`, `B`,
`λ_{i+j}(A + B) ≤ λ_i(A) + λ_j(B)` whenever `i + j < card n`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 4.3.1
(stated there increasingly; this is the decreasing, zero-indexed form). Audit G0 B7;
atlas `courant-fischer`, `weyl-mirsky`.
atlas: weyl-mirsky

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_compression_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {r : Type u_2} [Fintype r]
  [DecidableEq r] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hB : (Q.transpose * A * Q).IsHermitian) (i : Fin (Fintype.card r)) :
  hB.eigenvalues₀ i ≤ hA.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.castLE ⋯ i)
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_compression_le
doc:
**Cauchy interlacing / Poincaré separation, upper bound.** For real symmetric `A` and `Q`
with orthonormal columns, the eigenvalues of the compression `B = QᵀAQ` satisfy
`λ_i(B) ≤ λ_i(A)`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Cor 4.3.37 (Poincaré separation theorem, label to verify; the
bordered / principal-submatrix case is Thm 4.3.17). Audit G0 B8; atlas `cauchy-interlacing`.
Deviation from the audit statement: the index of `λ(A)` is `Fin.castLE` of `i`, so no side
condition `i < card n` is needed (`card r ≤ card n` is `card_le_card_of_hasOrthonormalCols`).
atlas: cauchy-interlacing

signature:

  {μ : Fin n → ℝ} (hμ : Antitone μ) (hW : W.transpose * W = 1) (hSW : S = W * Matrix.diagonal μ * W.transpose)

doc:
For a real symmetric `S = W diag(μ) Wᵀ` with `W` orthogonal and `μ` non-increasing, `μ` is
Mathlib's sorted eigenvalue list `eigenvalues₀` of `S` (uniqueness of the sorted spectrum, via
the characteristic polynomial). Atlas `svd` (helper; belongs with the spectral API).

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_eigenvalues₀_compression
doc:
**Cauchy interlacing / Poincaré separation, lower bound.** For real symmetric `A` and
`Q : n × r` with orthonormal columns, `λ_{i + (card n − card r)}(A) ≤ λ_i(QᵀAQ)`.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Cor 4.3.37 (label to verify). Audit G0 B8; atlas `cauchy-interlacing`.
The index bound is discharged inside the statement from `card r ≤ card n`.
atlas: cauchy-interlacing

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_eigenvalues₀_of_posSemidef_sub.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (h : (B - A).PosSemidef) (k : Fin (Fintype.card n)) :
  hA.eigenvalues₀ k ≤ hB.eigenvalues₀ k
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_eigenvalues₀_of_posSemidef_sub
doc:
**Loewner monotonicity of eigenvalues.** If `B − A` is positive semidefinite then
`λ_k(A) ≤ λ_k(B)` for every `k`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Cor 4.3.12. Audit G0 B7;
atlas `courant-fischer`.
atlas: weyl-mirsky

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_of_forall_mem.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (k : Fin (Fintype.card n)) (W : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ))
  (hW : Fintype.card n ≤ Module.finrank ℝ ↥W + ↑k) {c : ℝ} (hAW : ∀ x ∈ W, x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x ≤ c * x ⬝ᵥ x) :
  hA.eigenvalues₀ k ≤ c
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_of_forall_mem
doc:
**Courant–Fischer, min-max half.** For real symmetric `A`, if the Rayleigh quotient is at
most `c` on a subspace `W` of codimension at most `k` (`card n ≤ dim W + k`), then the `k`-th
largest eigenvalue satisfies `λ_k ≤ c`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 4.2.6 (HJ order eigenvalues
increasingly and from `1`; here `eigenvalues₀` is decreasing and zero-indexed). Audit G0 A1;
atlas `courant-fischer`. No sign condition on `c` is needed.
atlas: courant-fischer

Sorted eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite matrix are nonnegative.
Source: Mathlib's spectral theorem; manuscript `sa:rp-recursion`.

signature:
NLAlib.entropy_exp_mul_le_gaussian_of_lipschitz.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) (L : ℝ)
  (hLip : ∀ (x y : ι → ℝ), |f x - f y| ≤ L * √(∑ i, (x i - y i) ^ 2)) (s : ℝ) :
  (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), s * f x * Real.exp (s * f x) ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) -
      (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), Real.exp (s * f x) ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) *
        Real.log
          (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), Real.exp (s * f x) ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) ≤
    s ^ 2 * L ^ 2 / 2 *
      ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), Real.exp (s * f x) ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1
name: NLAlib.entropy_exp_mul_le_gaussian_of_lipschitz
doc:
**Entropy bound for Lipschitz functions** under the standard Gaussian: for `f`
`L`-Lipschitz (Euclidean) and every real `s`,
`∫ s f e^{s f} dγₙ - (∫ e^{s f} dγₙ) log ∫ e^{s f} dγₙ ≤ (s² L² / 2) ∫ e^{s f} dγₙ`.
Source: Ledoux, *The Concentration of Measure Phenomenon*, (5.5) and proof of Thm 5.3;
Boucheron–Lugosi–Massart 2013, proof of Thm 5.6. Atlas: `gaussian-concentration` (the
log-Sobolev input to `herbst`). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_lipschitz_entropy_bound`.
atlas: herbst

signature:
NLAlib.entropy_exp_mul_le_of_logSobolev_of_bounded.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure (ι → ℝ)} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {c : ℝ}
  (hLSI : NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev μ c) (f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) (L : ℝ)
  (hLip : ∀ (x y : ι → ℝ), |f x - f y| ≤ L * √(∑ i, (x i - y i) ^ 2)) (M : ℝ) (hM : ∀ (x : ι → ℝ), |f x| ≤ M) (s : ℝ) :
  ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), s * f x * Real.exp (s * f x) ∂μ -
      (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), Real.exp (s * f x) ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), Real.exp (s * f x) ∂μ) ≤
    c * s ^ 2 * L ^ 2 / 2 * ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), Real.exp (s * f x) ∂μ

doc:
A genuine LSI gives the exponential-entropy bound for a bounded smooth Lipschitz
observable, by the chain rule applied to `g=exp(s f/2)`. All three LSI integrability
requirements are proved from boundedness. Ledoux 2001, proof of Theorem 5.3;
atlas `herbst`.

signature:

`f ∈ C¹` with `δ ≤ f ≤ C` (`δ > 0`) and `|f'| ≤ C`,

Measure*, §5.1. Atlas: `gaussian-log-sobolev`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_logsobolev_bounded_below`.
atlas: gaussian-log-sobolev

proof: `x⋆ − x₀ ∈ K_ν(A, r₀)` (`sub_mem_krylovSpace_krylovGrade`), so the `A`-norm error of the

polynomial approximates every `L`-Lipschitz function with error at most `πL/(2(n+1))`.

Atlas `jackson-lipschitz` (unit-interval form).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_eval_eq_one_abs_eval_le {a c L : ℝ} (hac : a < c) (hcL : c < L) (q : ℕ) :
  ∃ p,
    p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧
      Polynomial.eval L p = 1 ∧
        ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a c,
          |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ 1 / Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((L - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_eval_eq_one_abs_eval_le
doc:
**The shifted Chebyshev amplifier.** For `a < c < L` and every `q` there is a polynomial
`p` of degree at most `q` with `p(L) = 1` and `|p| ≤ 1/T_q(1 + 2γ)` on `[a, c]`,
`γ = (L − c)/(c − a)`: namely `p(x) = T_q((2x − c − a)/(c − a))/T_q(1 + 2γ)`, the
`chebyshevAmplifier` with `α = (c − a)/2`, `γ' = 2γ`, shifted by `(c + a)/2`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1. Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle` (belongs in
`NLAlib.Polynomial.Approximation` next to `chebyshev-amplifier`).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_abs_eval_sub_inv_le {a b : ℝ} (q : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) :

doc:
Polynomial approximation of `1/x` on `[a, b]`: for `0 < a < b` there is a polynomial `p` of
degree `< q` with `|p(x) − 1/x| ≤ (2/a)((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q` on `[a, b]`. The polynomial is
`p = (1 − r)/X` for the Chebyshev residual `r = chebyshevResidual a b q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8 (the CG error bound). Atlas:
`inverse-polynomial-approx`.
atlas: inverse-polynomial-approx

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul_of_eval_zero_eq_one {p : Polynomial ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)

name: NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul_of_eval_zero_eq_one
doc:
**Residual-polynomial factorisation.** If `deg p ≤ q` and `p(0) = 1`, then `1 − p = X s` for
some `s` with `deg s < q`. This is the algebra behind every residual-polynomial Krylov argument:
`x₀ + s(A) r₀ ∈ x₀ + K_q` has error `p(A)(x₀ − x⋆)`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11
(the set `P_q^0`); Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35. Promoted from the private CG lemma
`exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul` (atlas `residual-polynomial`, helper).

name: NLAlib.exists_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_ge
doc:
**Gap-free Ritz-value bound.** Let `A` be symmetric with eigenvalues in `[0, λ₁]`,
`λ₁ = λ_{i₁}`, `0 < ε < 1`, `q ≥ 1`, `u_{i₁} ⬝ b ≠ 0`, and `Q` with orthonormal columns and
`K_q(A, b) ⊆ range Q` (e.g. the Lanczos basis). Then some Ritz value `θ_j` (eigenvalue of
`QᵀAQ`) satisfies
`λ₁ − θ_j ≤ ε λ₁ + λ₁ (2/(1 + √(2γ))^{q−1})² ‖b‖²/(u_{i₁} ⬝ b)²`, `γ = ε/(1 − ε)`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Thm 1 (single-vector, gap-free); Kuczyński–Woźniakowski
(1992) [`kw92`] for the random-start analysis. Atlas: `ritz-value-bounds`; uses
`chebyshev-amplifier`, `polynomial-spectral-bound`, `krylov-subspace`.
Label note: this is the gap-free bound (MM15); the gap-dependent bound of Saad (2011), Thm 6.4,
is `eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le` (`kaniel-paige-saad`).
atlas: ritz-value-bounds

A real positive semidefinite matrix is a Gram matrix: `A = FᵀF` for some square `F`.
Mathlib `CStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_eq_star_mul_self`. Atlas `nystrom-structural` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_finset_net_specNorm_le.{u_3, u_4} (n : Type u_3) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε)
  (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  ∃ N,
    (∀ x ∈ N, x ⬝ᵥ x = 1) ∧
      ↑N.card ≤ (1 + 2 / ε) ^ Fintype.card n ∧
        ∀ (m : Type u_4) [inst : Fintype m] [inst_1 : DecidableEq m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (M : ℝ),
          0 ≤ M → (∀ x ∈ N, √(A.mulVec x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x) ≤ M) → NLAlib.specNorm A ≤ M / (1 - ε)

doc:
**ε-net bound for the spectral norm.** For `0 < ε < 1` there is a set `N` of at most
`(1 + 2/ε)^{card n}` unit vectors of `ℝ^n` such that for every real matrix `A` with `n` columns
and every `M ≥ 0`, `‖Ax‖₂ ≤ M` on `N` implies `‖A‖₂ ≤ M/(1-ε)`.
Vershynin 2012, Lem 5.2–5.3; Vershynin 2018, Cor 4.2.13 and Ex 4.4.3; audit G1 B1.
Atlas `epsilon-net-norm`. Deviation: the atlas states `(1-2ε)⁻¹`; the standard (and stronger)
operator form `(1-ε)⁻¹` is used here, the `(1-2ε)⁻¹` forms being
`specNorm_le_div_of_net_bilinear` and `specNorm_le_div_of_net_quadForm`.
atlas: epsilon-net-norm

signature:
NLAlib.exists_finset_sphere_net.{u_3} (ι : Type u_3) [Fintype ι] {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ N,
    (∀ x ∈ N, x ⬝ᵥ x = 1) ∧
      ↑N.card ≤ (1 + 2 / ε) ^ Fintype.card ι ∧ ∀ (y : ι → ℝ), y ⬝ᵥ y = 1 → ∃ x ∈ N, (x - y) ⬝ᵥ (x - y) ≤ ε ^ 2

doc:
**Volumetric ε-net of the sphere.** For `ε > 0`, the unit sphere of `ℝ^ι` (Euclidean) has an
`ε`-net contained in the sphere with at most `(1 + 2/ε)^{card ι}` points:
`∀ y` with `yᵀy = 1`, `∃ x ∈ N`, `(x - y)ᵀ(x - y) ≤ ε²`. For an empty index type the sphere is
empty and `N = ∅`. Proof: a maximal `ε`-separated subset of the sphere is an `ε`-net, and the
volumetric packing bound caps the size of every separated subset.
Vershynin 2012, Lem 5.2; Vershynin 2018, Cor 4.2.13; audit G1 A1. Atlas `epsilon-net-norm`
(covering half). Deviation: index type any `[Fintype ι]` (audit: `Fin n`).
atlas: epsilon-net-norm

signature:

name: NLAlib.exists_iInf_sqrt_mulVec_le_of_sigmaMin_le

**Small `σ_min` forces a column close to the span of the others.** For `A : Matrix m n ℝ`
with `n` nonempty, if `σ_min(A) ≤ s` then for some column `j`,
`inf { ‖A x‖₂ : x_j = 1 } ≤ √|n| · s`; the left side is the distance from column `j` to the
span of the other columns.

"invertibility via distance" step). Atlas: `smin-small-ball`. Generalised from
`Fin N × Fin n` (with `1 ≤ n`) to arbitrary finite index types with `n` nonempty. Ported from
Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.sMin_le_imp_dist_le`.

A positive locally finite measure with nonpositive weak derivative has a
uniform integral domination bound to the right of every interior point. The
constant is finite because it is the integral of one fixed compactly supported

atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isBestRankApprox.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)

An actual Frobenius best rank-at-most-`k` approximation exists for every

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef)
  (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) : ∃ x, NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x
name: NLAlib.exists_isCGIterate
doc:
**Existence of the CG iterate.** For positive definite `A`, every `c`, `x₀` and `q`, there
is a `q`-th CG iterate. It is the Galerkin solution: the bilinear form `(y, z) ↦ zᵀ A y` on `K_q`
is nondegenerate, hence `y ↦ (z ↦ zᵀ A y)` is a bijection `K_q → K_q*`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.2 (uniqueness and existence of the minimiser).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.
atlas: cg-convergence

name: NLAlib.exists_isGMRESIterate
doc:
**Existence.** For every square `A`, right-hand side `c`, start `x₀` and `q` there is a
GMRES iterate (a least-squares problem over `A K_q`; no hypothesis on `A`).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.1; Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §2.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isGradedKrylovBasis_iff.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)

**Existence of graded bases**: a graded orthonormal Krylov basis with `q` columns exists iff
`q ≤ krylovGrade A b`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.4.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isLeast_isGreatest_complexUnitQuadFormValues.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

doc:
Every positive-dimensional complex subspace has attained minimum and
maximum real quadratic values on its Euclidean unit vectors. No Hermitian or
definiteness hypothesis is needed for this compactness statement.
Toolkit §2; Horn–Johnson Theorem 4.2.6; helper for atlas `courant-fischer`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isMoorePenroseInverse.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

doc:
Every real rectangular matrix has a Moore–Penrose inverse, with arbitrary
finite row and column types and without a rank or nonempty assumption.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature: NLAlib.exists_isSVD {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : ∃ U V, NLAlib.IsSVD A U V
name: NLAlib.exists_isSVD
doc:
**Singular value decomposition** (Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3; HMT 2011, §2.1): every real
`m × n` matrix is `A = U Σ Vᵀ` with `U`, `V` orthogonal and `Σ = rectDiag (singularValues A)`,
the singular values being nonnegative and non-increasing (`singularValues_nonneg`,
`singularValues_antitone`). Atlas `svd`.

Proof: `V` is an orthonormal eigenbasis of `AᵀA` (Mathlib's spectral theorem, sorted), the
vectors `A vⱼ / σⱼ` with `σⱼ ≠ 0` are orthonormal and are completed to an orthonormal basis of
`ℝᵐ` (atlas `orthonormal-completion`) giving `U`.
atlas: svd

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isSymm_transpose_mul_mul_eq_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {P : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hP : P.PosDef) : ∃ W, W.IsSymm ∧ W.transpose * P * W = 1

doc:
A positive definite `P` has a symmetric inverse square root: some `W = Wᵀ` with
`Wᵀ P W = I` (`W = P^{-1/2} = U diag(λ^{-1/2}) Uᵀ`). Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Thm 7.2.6.
Helper for `preconditioned-cg` (belongs in `NLAlib.Matrix`).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_card {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {s : Finset ℝ} (hs : s.card = q + 2)
  (hsab : ∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b))
  (hf' : ∀ k < q, ContinuousOn (iteratedDeriv (k + 1) f) (Set.Ioo a b)) (hz : ∀ x ∈ s, f x = 0) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b, iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ = 0
name: NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_card
doc:
**Generalised Rolle theorem**, finset form: if `f` vanishes on a set of `q + 2` points of
`[a, b]` (hypotheses as in `exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono`), then `f^{(q+1)}`
vanishes somewhere in `(a, b)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, proof of Thm 6.2. Atlas: `interpolation-remainder` (lemma).
atlas: interpolation-remainder

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {v : Fin (q + 2) → ℝ}
  (hv : StrictMono v) (hva : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 2)), v i ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b))
  (hf' : ∀ k < q, ContinuousOn (iteratedDeriv (k + 1) f) (Set.Ioo a b)) (hz : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 2)), f (v i) = 0) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b, iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ = 0
name: NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono
doc:
**Generalised Rolle theorem.** If `f` vanishes at `q + 2` points `v 0 < ⋯ < v (q+1)` of
`[a, b]`, `f` is continuous on `[a, b]` and the derivatives `f', …, f^{(q)}` are continuous on
`(a, b)`, then `f^{(q+1)}(ξ) = 0` for some `ξ ∈ (a, b)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, *An Introduction to Numerical Analysis*, proof of Thm 6.2; Atkinson,
*An Introduction to Numerical Analysis* (2nd ed.), proof of Thm 3.2.
Atlas: `interpolation-remainder` (lemma).
Deviation: stated with `q + 2` zeros and the `(q + 1)`-st derivative (so the conclusion is in the
open interval without a side condition); only continuity of `f^{(k)}`, `1 ≤ k ≤ q`, on `(a, b)`
is assumed — no differentiability, because `iteratedDeriv` is Mathlib's global derivative and
Rolle (`exists_deriv_eq_zero`) needs only continuity.
atlas: interpolation-remainder

signature:
NLAlib.exists_measurable_extension_of_antitoneOn_Ioi (ℓ : ℝ) (h : ℝ → ℝ) (hh : AntitoneOn h (Set.Ioi ℓ)) :

doc:
An antitone representative on a real half-line has a globally measurable
extension agreeing with it on that half-line. Source: operator rederivations,
Section 5, density API; atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail (helper).

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_add_sub_eq_aeval_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (x₀ : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)

  ∃ y ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q, x₀ + y - xs = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_add_sub_eq_aeval_mulVec
doc:
**Error form, converse.** If `A x⋆ = c`, every residual polynomial `p` is realised:
some `y ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` has `x₀ + y − x⋆ = p(A)(x₀ − x⋆)`. No hypothesis on `A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11. Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (partial).
atlas: residual-polynomial (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q) (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) :
  ∃ y ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q,
    c - A.mulVec (x₀ + y) = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval_mulVec
doc:
**Every residual polynomial is realised in `x₀ + K_q`.** For `deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1` there
is `y ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` with `c − A (x₀ + y) = p(A) r₀`. No hypothesis on `A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11. Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (partial: converse).
atlas: residual-polynomial (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_sub_rayleigh_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hpsd : ∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ hA.eigenvalues i) {i₁ : n}
  (htop : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ≤ hA.eigenvalues i₁) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ}
  (hq : 0 < q) (hb : (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0) :
  ∃ y ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q,
    y ≠ 0 ∧
      hA.eigenvalues i₁ * y ⬝ᵥ y - y ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec y ≤
        (ε * hA.eigenvalues i₁ +
            hA.eigenvalues i₁ * (2 / (1 + √(2 * (ε / (1 - ε)))) ^ (q - 1)) ^ 2 * b ⬝ᵥ b /
              ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ b) ^ 2) *
          y ⬝ᵥ y
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_sub_rayleigh_le
doc:
**A Krylov vector with near-maximal Rayleigh quotient (gap-free).** Let `A` be symmetric
with eigenvalues in `[0, λ₁]`, `λ₁ = λ_{i₁}`, let `0 < ε < 1`, `q ≥ 1`, and `c₁ = u_{i₁} ⬝ b ≠ 0`.
Then there is a nonzero `y ∈ K_q(A, b)` with
`λ₁ ‖y‖² − yᵀAy ≤ (ε λ₁ + λ₁ (2/(1 + √(2γ))^{q−1})² ‖b‖²/c₁²) ‖y‖²`, `γ = ε/(1 − ε)`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Lem. 4–5 and proof of Thm 1 (single-vector case).
Atlas: `ritz-value-bounds`; uses `chebyshev-amplifier`, `polynomial-spectral-bound`,
`krylov-subspace`.
atlas: ritz-value-bounds

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_tanSqAngle_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₁ : n} {a c : ℝ} (hac : a < c) (hc : c < hA.eigenvalues i₁)
  (hspec : ∀ (i : n), i ≠ i₁ → hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c) (b : n → ℝ) (hb : (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0)
  (q : ℕ) :
  ∃ x ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (q + 1),
    (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ x ≠ 0 ∧
      NLAlib.tanSqAngle (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp x ≤
        NLAlib.tanSqAngle (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp b /
          Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((hA.eigenvalues i₁ - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_tanSqAngle_le
doc:
**Angle between the top eigenvector and the Krylov space (Chebyshev bound).** Let `A` be
real symmetric, `λ₁ = λ_{i₁}`, and suppose every other eigenvalue lies in `[a, c]` with
`a < c < λ₁` (e.g. `a = λₙ`, `c = λ₂`). If `u₁ ⬝ b ≠ 0` then `K_{q+1}(A, b)` contains `x` with
`u₁ ⬝ x ≠ 0` and `tan² ∠(u₁, x) ≤ tan² ∠(u₁, b) / T_q(1 + 2γ)²`, `γ = (λ₁ − c)/(c − a)`.
The witness is `x = T_q((2A − (c + a)I)/(c − a)) b`, written through `chebyshevAmplifier`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1 (case `i = 1`); Saad (2003), §6.11.
Deviation: squared tangents; Krylov dimension `q + 1` (Saad's `m`) so that the degree is `q`;
an arbitrary enclosure `[a, c]` of the other eigenvalues instead of `[λₙ, λ₂]`.
atlas: krylov-eigenvector-angle

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_tanSqAngle_le_two_div_pow.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₁ : n} {a c : ℝ} (hac : a < c) (hc : c < hA.eigenvalues i₁)
  (hspec : ∀ (i : n), i ≠ i₁ → hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c) (b : n → ℝ) (hb : (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0)
  (q : ℕ) :
  ∃ x ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (q + 1),
    (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ x ≠ 0 ∧
      NLAlib.tanSqAngle (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp x ≤
        (2 /
              (1 + 2 * ((hA.eigenvalues i₁ - c) / (c - a)) +
                  2 * √((hA.eigenvalues i₁ - c) / (c - a) + ((hA.eigenvalues i₁ - c) / (c - a)) ^ 2)) ^
                q) ^
            2 *
          NLAlib.tanSqAngle (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp b
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_tanSqAngle_le_two_div_pow
doc:
**Eigenvector angle, explicit rate.** Under the hypotheses of
`exists_mem_krylovSpace_tanSqAngle_le`, `K_{q+1}(A, b)` contains `x` with `u₁ ⬝ x ≠ 0` and
`tan² ∠(u₁, x) ≤ (2/(1 + 2γ + 2√(γ + γ²))^q)² tan² ∠(u₁, b)`, `γ = (λ₁ − c)/(c − a)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1.
atlas: krylov-eigenvector-angle

signature:
NLAlib.exists_nonneg_primitive_of_ordered_supports (c a b : ℝ) (hca : c < a) (hab : a < b) (f g : ℝ → ℝ)

from the Prove2me solutions `Sol_GaussianMatrix_residual_law` and
`GaussianMatrix.regression_residual_indep` (the two copies merged, keeping the stronger
statement).

Label permutations act transitively on literal subsets of a fixed size.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_pos_bounds_tsupport_and_deriv (ψ : ℝ → ℝ) (hψc : HasCompactSupport ψ) (hψs : tsupport ψ ⊆ Set.Ioi 0) :

doc:
A compactly supported real function in the positive half-line and its derivative
have support in one strictly positive compact interval. No nonzero assumption is
needed; the empty-support case is included.
Source: compactness and derivative support containment;
atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail (unshifted cutoff helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_pos_mul_lt_three_bernstein_exponent_eq {t v L : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) (hv : 0 < v) (hL : 0 ≤ L) :

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sub_eq_aeval_mulVec_of_sub_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {q : ℕ}
  (hx : x - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q) :
  ∃ p, p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧ Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1 ∧ x - xs = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.exists_sub_eq_aeval_mulVec_of_sub_mem_krylovSpace
doc:
**Error form of the residual polynomial.** If `A x⋆ = c` and `x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀)`, then
`x − x⋆ = p(A)(x₀ − x⋆)` for a residual polynomial `p`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11;
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.3 (proof). Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (partial).
atlas: residual-polynomial (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sub_eval_interpolate_eq {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b x : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ} (hab : a < b)
  (hv : Function.Injective v) (hva : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 1)), v i ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hf' : ∀ k ≤ q, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) (Set.Ioo a b)) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b,
    f x - Polynomial.eval x ((Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ v) (f ∘ v)) =
      iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ / ↑(q + 1).factorial * Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.nodal Finset.univ v)
name: NLAlib.exists_sub_eval_interpolate_eq
doc:
**Interpolation remainder formula.** Let `v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ` be distinct nodes in
`[a, b]`, `f` continuous on `[a, b]` with `f, f', …, f^{(q)}` differentiable on `(a, b)`, and
`x ∈ [a, b]`. Then for the interpolating polynomial `L = Lagrange.interpolate univ v (f ∘ v)`
and the nodal polynomial `ω = ∏ (X − v i)` there is `ξ ∈ (a, b)` with
`f x − L(x) = f^{(q+1)}(ξ) / (q + 1)! · ω(x)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, *An Introduction to Numerical Analysis*, Thm 6.2; Atkinson (2nd ed.),
Thm 3.2; Cheney, *Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas:
`interpolation-remainder`.
Deviation: `ξ` is in the open interval `(a, b)` (stronger than `[a, b]`), at the cost of the
hypothesis `a < b` (used only when `x` is a node).
atlas: interpolation-remainder

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval_mulVec_of_sub_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hx : x - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q) :
  ∃ p, p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧ Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1 ∧ c - A.mulVec x = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.exists_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval_mulVec_of_sub_mem_krylovSpace
doc:
**Residual-polynomial form of an affine Krylov iterate.** If `x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀)`,
`r₀ = c − A x₀`, then `c − A x = p(A) r₀` for a residual polynomial `p` (`deg p ≤ q`,
`p(0) = 1`). No hypothesis on `A`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11; Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 35. Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (partial: forward direction).
atlas: residual-polynomial (partial)

name: NLAlib.exists_submodule_eigenvalues₀_mul_le
doc:
**Courant–Fischer, attaining subspace for the max-min half**: there is a subspace of
dimension at least `k + 1` (the span of the top `k + 1` eigenvectors) on which
`λ_k xᵀx ≤ xᵀAx`. Horn–Johnson 2013, proof of Thm 4.2.6. Audit G0 C6; atlas `courant-fischer`.
Deviation: the dimension is stated as a lower bound.
atlas: courant-fischer

signature:
NLAlib.exists_submodule_finrank_eq_isGreatest_complexUnitQuadFormValues.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℂ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (k : Fin (Fintype.card n)) :
  ∃ S, Module.finrank ℂ ↥S = Fintype.card n - ↑k ∧ IsGreatest (NLAlib.complexUnitQuadFormValues A S) (hA.eigenvalues₀ k)
name: NLAlib.exists_submodule_finrank_eq_isGreatest_complexUnitQuadFormValues
doc:
A complex spectral tail of dimension exactly `card n-k` attains its
maximum real unit-vector quadratic value at the `k`-th decreasing eigenvalue.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 4.2.6; toolkit §2; helper for atlas `courant-fischer`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_submodule_finrank_eq_isLeast_complexUnitQuadFormValues.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

name: NLAlib.exists_submodule_finrank_eq_isLeast_complexUnitQuadFormValues

A complex spectral head of dimension exactly `k+1` attains its minimum
real unit-vector quadratic value at the `k`-th decreasing eigenvalue.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 4.2.6; toolkit §2; helper for atlas `courant-fischer`.

codimension at most `k` (the span of the eigenvectors `k, k+1, …`) on which `xᵀAx ≤ λ_k xᵀx`.
Horn–Johnson 2013, proof of Thm 4.2.6. Audit G0 C6; atlas `courant-fischer`.
atlas: courant-fischer

signature:
NLAlib.exists_submodule_mulVec_dotProduct_le_sq_singularValues_mul {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  ∃ W, n ≤ Module.finrank ℝ ↥W + k ∧ ∀ x ∈ W, A.mulVec x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x ≤ NLAlib.singularValues A k ^ 2 * x ⬝ᵥ x
name: NLAlib.exists_submodule_mulVec_dotProduct_le_sq_singularValues_mul
doc:
**Attaining subspace, min-max half (singular values)**: there is a subspace of codimension
at most `k` (spanned by the right singular vectors `k, k+1, …`) on which `‖Ax‖² ≤ σ_k² ‖x‖²`.
Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3. Audit G0 B1/C6; atlas `courant-fischer`.

name: NLAlib.exists_submodule_sq_singularValues_mul_le_mulVec_dotProduct
doc:
**Attaining subspace, max-min half (singular values)**: for `k < n` there is a subspace of
dimension at least `k + 1` (spanned by the top `k + 1` right singular vectors) on which
`σ_k² ‖x‖² ≤ ‖Ax‖²`. Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3. Audit G0 B1/C6;
atlas `courant-fischer`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sum_smul_T_eq_of_degree_le {p : Polynomial ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑n) :

name: NLAlib.exists_sum_smul_T_eq_of_degree_le
doc:
Every real polynomial of degree at most `n` has a finite first-kind Chebyshev expansion.
Source: Rivlin, Chebyshev Polynomials, Chapter 1; Mathlib polynomial-sequence spanning.
This is the genuine cosine-basis construction used by sharp `jackson-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_sum_smul_U_eq_of_degree_lt {p : Polynomial ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hp : p.degree < ↑n) :

signature:
NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
  ∃ r U₁ U₂ V₁ V₂ S₂,
    A = U₁ * 1 * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose ∧
      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂ ∧
        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧
          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂ ∧ V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0 ∧ NLAlib.frobSq S₂ = NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq k A
name: NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks
doc:
Every actual real matrix has an SVD-derived right-space block split whose
tail is the genuine optimal squared rank-`k` error. The head singular values
are absorbed into `U₁=A V₁`, as permitted by HMT's structural lemma.
Only `k≤n` is needed; `k>m` is handled by the padded zero singular values.
HMT 2011, Theorem 9.1; atlas `rsvd-expected-error`, `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks_specNorm {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
  ∃ r U₁ U₂ V₁ V₂ S₂,
    A = U₁ * 1 * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose ∧
      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂ ∧
        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧
          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂ ∧
            V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0 ∧
              NLAlib.specNorm S₂ = NLAlib.singularValues A k ∧ NLAlib.frobSq S₂ = NLAlib.singularValueTailSq A k
name: NLAlib.exists_svd_right_blocks_specNorm
doc:
**SVD right blocks with spectral tail.** For `k ≤ n` every real `A` splits as
`A = U₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ` with `U₂`, `V₁`, `V₂` orthonormal, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`, `‖Σ₂‖ = σ_{k+1}` and
`‖Σ₂‖_F² = ∑_{j>k} σ_j²` (zero-indexed `singularValues A k`, `singularValueTailSq A k`). The
blocks are those of `exists_svd_right_blocks` (`U₁ = AV₁`, `U₂ = U`), with the spectral tail
identified through `IsSVD.specNorm_sub_truncatedMatrix`. HMT 2011, §2.1 and Thm 9.1.
Atlas `rsvd-spectral-expected` (helper; uses `svd`, `eckart-young`; belongs in
`Matrix/SvdBlocks.lean`).

signature:
NLAlib.exp_mul_lambdaMax_lambdaMin_le_traceExp_smul {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ)

labels. Source: Tropp 2015, equation (3.2.3); exact reindexing of the recorded comparison.

signature:
NLAlib.exp_mul_le_one_add_mul_add_sq_mul_of_le {L θ x : ℝ} (hθ : 0 < θ) (hθL : θ * L < 3) (hx : x ≤ L) :

signature:
NLAlib.exp_neg_mul_tsum_pow_div_factorial_nat_add_le {ℓ : ℝ} (hℓ : 0 ≤ ℓ) (t : ℕ) (ht : Real.exp 2 * ℓ ≤ ↑t) :

doc:

name: NLAlib.frobInner_le_frobNorm_mul_frobNorm
doc:

signature:
NLAlib.frobInner_le_sqrt_mul_frobNorm_mul_specNorm_of_rank_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {r : ℕ} (X E : Matrix m n ℝ) (hX : X.rank ≤ r) :
  NLAlib.frobInner X E ≤ √↑r * NLAlib.frobNorm X * NLAlib.specNorm E
name: NLAlib.frobInner_le_sqrt_mul_frobNorm_mul_specNorm_of_rank_le
doc:
**Rank corollary of the von Neumann trace inequality.** If `rank X ≤ r` then
`⟨X, E⟩_F ≤ √r ‖X‖_F ‖E‖₂`. Proof: with the orthogonal projector `P = X X⁺` onto `range X`,
`⟨X, E⟩_F = ⟨X, P E⟩_F ≤ ‖X‖_F ‖P E‖_F ≤ ‖X‖_F √(rank P E) ‖P E‖₂ ≤ √r ‖X‖_F ‖E‖₂`.
It follows from Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.4.1.1 (von Neumann) and Cauchy–Schwarz over the top
`r` singular values; this is the `VonNeumannRankBound` hypothesis of the Chen–Persson LRA
formalization. Audit G0 C4; atlas `von-neumann-trace` (rank corollary). Deviation: arbitrary
finite index types, no full-rank or nonemptiness condition.
atlas: von-neumann-rank-bound

signature:
NLAlib.frobInner_le_sum_singularValues_mul {m n : ℕ} (X E : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.frobInner X E ≤ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (min m n), NLAlib.singularValues X k * NLAlib.singularValues E k
name: NLAlib.frobInner_le_sum_singularValues_mul
doc:
**Von Neumann trace inequality.** For real `m × n` matrices,
`⟨X, E⟩_F = tr(XᵀE) ≤ ∑_{k < min m n} σ_k(X) σ_k(E)`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.4.1.1 (real case,
`Re tr(X E*) = frobInner X E`); Mirsky 1975. Proof: Ky Fan's maximum principle for the diagonal
of `UᵀEV` (through the weighted top-`k` inequality `sum_mul_le_sum_ite_lt_of_antitone`) and
Abel summation over `σ(X)`; no Birkhoff theorem is needed. Audit G0 A2;
atlas `von-neumann-trace`.
atlas: von-neumann-trace

doc:
Monotonicity of the residual under range inclusion (HMT 2011, Prop. 8.5, Frobenius case):
if `range Q₁ ⊆ range Q₂`, written `Q₁ = Q₂ C`, then `‖(I − Q₂Q₂ᵀ)A‖_F² ≤ ‖(I − Q₁Q₁ᵀ)A‖_F²`.
Deviation: only `Q₂` needs orthonormal columns; `Q₁` is arbitrary (with `residual` defined
by the formula `A − Q₁Q₁ᵀA`). Atlas `projection-facts`.
atlas: projection-facts

name: NLAlib.frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset
doc:
**Deterministic range-finder bound, Frobenius form** (HMT 2011, Thm 9.1, squared Frobenius
case): if `A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ`, `Ω₁ = V₁ᵀΩ` has full row rank, `Ω₂ = V₂ᵀΩ`, `QᵀQ = I` and
`range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then `‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F² ≤ ‖Σ₂‖_F² + ‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖_F²`.
Chen–Persson, Prop. `prop:hmt-struct`, second inequality (LRA `hmt_second_frob`).

Deviations from the printed statement: the SVD is a block decomposition with only the
hypotheses the proof uses (`U₂ᵀU₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₁ = I`, `V₂ᵀV₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`; no diagonality,
no conditions on `U₁`); `P_Y` is `QQᵀ` for any orthonormal `Q` with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`
(HMT take `range Q = range(AΩ)`); index types are arbitrary `Fintype`s. Atlas
`hmt-9-1-frobenius`.
atlas: hmt-9-1-frobenius

and hence `‖A − Z‖_F² = ‖Σ₂‖_F² + ‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖_F²` (HMT 2011, proof of Thm 9.1; Chen–Persson,

signature:
NLAlib.gammaRatio_le {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k) :
  2 ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) * Real.Gamma ((↑k + 1) / 2) / (Real.Gamma (↑r / 2) * Real.Gamma (↑k - ↑r + 1)) ≤
    ((↑k + ↑r) / 2) ^ ((↑k - ↑r + 1) / 2) / (2 * Real.Gamma (↑k - ↑r + 1))
name: NLAlib.gammaRatio_le
doc:
**Gamma-ratio estimate.** For `1 ≤ r ≤ k`,
`2^{(k-r-1)/2} Γ((k+1)/2) / (Γ(r/2) Γ(k-r+1)) ≤ ((k+r)/2)^{(k-r+1)/2} / (2 Γ(k-r+1))`,
i.e. the constant of the density bound (B.5) is at most the constant of (B.6).

Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.6). Atlas: `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper). Proof: iterated Gautschi
inequality (log-convexity of `Γ`, Bohr–Mollerup) and AM–GM (`prod_range_add_le_pow`). Ported
from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.tw_gamma_ratio_bound`.
atlas: wishart-lambda-min-tail

signature:
NLAlib.gamma_inverse_spectral_endpoint_le {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r < k) :
  2 ^ (-(↑k - ↑r) / 2) * Real.pi * Real.Gamma (↑k / 2) / (Real.Gamma (↑r / 2) * Real.Gamma ((↑k - ↑r + 1) / 2) ^ 2) ≤
    (Real.exp 1 ^ 2 * (↑k + ↑r - 1) / (2 * (↑k - ↑r) ^ 2)) ^ ((↑k - ↑r) / 2)
name: NLAlib.gamma_inverse_spectral_endpoint_le
doc:
The endpoint quadratic-probe constant for an `r × k` Gaussian matrix
is bounded by the strengthened inverse spectral moment constant.
Source: direct quadratic-probe proof, endpoint moment calculation; the
arithmetic-progression mean retains `k+r-1`. Atlas:
`inverse-wishart-spectral-moment` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le {r k : ℕ} (hrk : r + 4 ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) :

    ENNReal.ofReal (4 * t ^ (-((↑k - ↑r) / 2)))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le
doc:
**Tail bound for the Frobenius norm of the Gaussian pseudoinverse.** For an `r × k`
standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `r + 4 ≤ k` and `t ≥ 1`,
`P[‖G†‖_F² > 12 r t/(k-r)] ≤ 4 t^{-(k-r)/2}`, with `G† = pinvR G`.

HMT 2011, Thm A.6 (used in Prop 10.4; HMT state it as `P[‖Ω₁†‖_F ≥ √(12k/p) t] ≤ 4 t^{-p}`
with `Ω₁` of size `k × (k+p)`, the same bound after `t ↦ √t`). Atlas: `pinv-frob-tail`.
Proof: each diagonal entry of `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹` is `1/χ²_{k-r+1}`
(`gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`), whose `L^{(k-r)/2}` norm is at most
`3/(k-r+1)` (`integrable_and_integral_rpow_inv_sum_sq_gaussianReal_lt`, atlas
`chi-square-neg-moment`); Minkowski's inequality bounds `‖tr (G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖_{L^q}` and Markov's
inequality gives the tail. Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.pinv_frobenius_tail`.
atlas: pinv-frob-tail

signature:

doc:

standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `2 ≤ r ≤ k` and `t > 0`,
`P[‖G†‖ > t] ≤ (2π(k-r+1))^{-1/2} (e√k/(k-r+1))^{k-r+1} t^{-(k-r+1)}`,
with `G† = pinvR G`.

HMT 2011, Prop A.3; Chen–Dongarra 2005, Lemma 4.1. Atlas: `pinv-spectral-tail`. Proof:
`‖G†‖² = ‖(G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖ = 1/σ_min(Gᵀ)²` (`specNorm_pinvR_sq`,
`specNorm_inv_self_mul_transpose_eq`, atlas `pseudoinverse`), the `λ_min` lower tail
(`gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le`, atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail`, which uses the
proved operator bound (B.5)) and Stirling's formula. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.pinv_spectral_tail`.
atlas: pinv-spectral-tail

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self {r k : ℕ} (hrk : r ≤ k) (i : Fin r) :

matrix `G` with `r ≤ k` and any `i`, `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹ᵢᵢ` has the law of `1/χ²_{k-r+1}`, i.e. of

HMT 2011, proof of Prop A.5 / Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Lemma B.2 (each diagonal entry of an
inverse Wishart matrix is an inverse chi-square). Atlas: `pinv-frob-tail`,
`inverse-wishart-frob-moment` (helper). Proof: Schur complement
(`inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`), conditioning on the other rows, which have full rank
a.s. (`gaussianMatrix_ae_rank_eq`, atlas `gaussian-full-rank-ae`), and the residual law
(`pi_gaussianReal_map_sq_dist_rowSpace`, atlas `block-law-indep`). Ported from Prove2me
solution `GaussianMatrix.inverse_wishart_diag_law`.

`(x ⬝ᵥ x).toNNReal`; for `x = 0` both sides are the Dirac mass at `0`. Proof: the unit-vector case
`gaussianMatrix_map_mulVec_of_dotProduct_self_eq_one` and Mathlib `gaussianReal_map_const_mul`.

`Matrix.of.symm`. Ported from the Prove2me workspace, Gaussian Random Matrices series.
atlas: rotation-invariance

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_Ioc_le_of_antitone_density {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k)

  (hdens :

singular value implies the exact Edelman CDF bound. Source: operator
rederivations Section 5; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail`. All moment and
endpoint hypotheses are discharged by the operator probe; only the scalar
density representation remains as the explicit input.

NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_one_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_eq {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :

`G` (`k ≥ 1`) and `t ≥ 0`, `σ_min(Gᵀ)² = ‖G‖² ∼ χ²_k`, and
`P[σ_min(Gᵀ)² ≤ t] = ∫₀ᵗ c(1,k) x^{(k-2)/2} e^{-x/2} dx` with

duplication): the `χ²_k` CDF written in the shape of Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.5).

Gaussian vector and the substitution `y = √x`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.wishart_lambda_min_cdf_rank_one`.

`𝔼 (X_{u,t} - X_{u,s})² ≤ 𝔼 (Y_{u,t} - Y_{u,s})²` for all `u, t, s` and

  have T := (R ^ n).trace;

        ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
          (2 * (R ^ (n + 2) * (G * G.transpose)).trace +
              (R ^ (n - a + 1)).trace * (R ^ (a + 1) * (G * G.transpose)).trace +
            (R ^ (a + 1)).trace * (R ^ (n - a + 1) * (G * G.transpose)).trace)

  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {ι : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ) (X : ι → Ω → ℝ) (K : ℝ) (hK : 0 < K) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hX : ∀ (i : ι), AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hmean : ∀ (i : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X i ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hpsi : ∀ (i : ι), ∫⁻ (ω : Ω), ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp ((X i ω / K) ^ 2)) ∂μ ≤ 2) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  (μ {ω | t ≤ |(NLAlib.quadForm A fun i => X i ω) - ∫ (ω' : Ω), NLAlib.quadForm A fun i => X i ω' ∂μ|}).toReal ≤
    2 *
      Real.exp
        (-(1 / (20736 * Real.exp 1 ^ 2)) *
          min (t ^ 2 / (K ^ 4 * NLAlib.frobNorm A ^ 2)) (t / (K ^ 2 * NLAlib.specNorm A)))
name: NLAlib.hanson_wright_of_lintegral_exp_sq_le_two
doc:
**Hanson–Wright, exponential-square/ψ₂ form.** Independent centered
coordinates with nonnegative expectations `E exp((Xᵢ/K)²) ≤ 2` satisfy the
quadratic-form tail bound with explicit constant `1/(20736 exp(1)²)`.
The already-proved Orlicz-to-MGF bridge gives variance proxy `9K²`; the bound
therefore uses the common original ψ₂ scale with a conservative constant.
Vershynin 2018, Theorem 6.2.1; atlas `hanson-wright`. Deviation: the constant
`1/(20736 e²)` is explicit (Vershynin's `c` is unspecified); the index type is an arbitrary
`[Fintype ι]`.
atlas: hanson-wright

signature:

The Joukowski transform has its usual strict complex derivative away from zero.

name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_finset_sum_mul_of_iIndepFun
doc:
A finite linear combination `∑_{i ∈ s} aᵢ Xᵢ` of independent sub-Gaussian variables is
sub-Gaussian with proxy `∑_{i ∈ s} aᵢ² cᵢ`. Vershynin 2018, Prop 2.6.1; atlas `hanson-wright`
(helper). Promoted from `HansonWrightProof.hasSubgaussianMGF_finset_sum_const_mul_of_iIndepFun`.

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_id_gaussianReal (v : NNReal) :
  ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF id v (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 v)
name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_id_gaussianReal
doc:
**A centred Gaussian is sub-Gaussian with its variance as proxy**:
`E[exp(t Y)] = exp(v t²/2)` for `Y ∼ N(0, v)`, so `HasSubgaussianMGF id v (gaussianReal 0 v)`
(with equality in the mgf bound).

Vershynin 2018, §2.5, Example 2.5.8(i) (there in `ψ₂`-norm form; here the exact mgf form);
proof from Mathlib `mgf_id_gaussianReal`. Atlas: `gaussian-matrix-def` (sub-Gaussian API, audit G1 C9).
Generalises `HansonWrightProof.hasSubgaussianMGF_id_gaussianReal_zero_one` (`v = 1`).
atlas: gaussian-matrix-def

signature: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_id_rademacherMeasure : ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF id 1 NLAlib.rademacherMeasure
name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_id_rademacherMeasure
doc:
**The Rademacher law is `1`-sub-Gaussian**: `𝔼 e^{t ε} ≤ e^{t²/2}`.
Hoeffding's lemma on `[-1, 1]` (Mathlib `hasSubgaussianMGF_of_mem_Icc_of_integral_eq_zero`).
Vershynin 2018, Example 2.5.8(ii). Atlas `rademacher-khintchine` (sub-Gaussian half).

name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_mono
doc:
Monotonicity in the variance proxy: `HasSubgaussianMGF X c μ` and `c ≤ d` give
`HasSubgaussianMGF X d μ`. Atlas `hanson-wright` (helper). Promoted from
`HansonWrightProof.hasSubgaussianMGF_mono_param`.

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_mulVec_apply_gaussianMatrix {k n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin k) :
