name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_mulVec_apply_gaussianMatrix
doc:
**Coordinates of `G x` are sub-Gaussian**: for a `k × n` standard Gaussian matrix `G`, each
coordinate `(G x)ᵢ` has `HasSubgaussianMGF` with proxy `‖x‖² = x ⬝ᵥ x`.

HMT 2011, §10.1 with Vershynin 2018, §2.5. Atlas: `gaussian-matrix-mulVec-law` (corollary).
Proof: the law `gaussianMatrix_map_mulVec` and `hasSubgaussianMGF_id_gaussianReal`.
atlas: gaussian-matrix-mulvec-law

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_independent_coordinate_oscillation.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2}
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {S : ι → Type u_3} [(i : ι) → MeasurableSpace (S i)] (X : (i : ι) → Ω → S i) (hX : ∀ (i : ι), Measurable (X i))
  (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ) (f : ((i : ι) → S i) → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f) (c : ι → ℝ)
  (hc : ∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ c i)
  (hcoord : ∀ (i : ι) (x : (j : ι) → S j) (y : S i), |f (Function.update x i y) - f x| ≤ c i) :
  ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (fun ω => (f fun i => X i ω) - ∫ (ω' : Ω), f fun i => X i ω' ∂μ)
    ⟨(∑ i, c i ^ 2) / 4, ⋯⟩ μ
name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_independent_coordinate_oscillation
doc:
The centred bounded-differences MGF transports along the joint law of
independent measurable coordinates on an arbitrary probability space.
The original space and the coordinate spaces need no standard-Borel instances.
Source: the abstract-space paragraph following manuscript `cor:mcdiarmid`.
atlas: mcdiarmid (partial)

name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_isRademacher
doc:
**A Rademacher variable is `1`-sub-Gaussian**: if `μ.map r = ½ δ₁ + ½ δ₋₁` then
`𝔼 e^{t r} ≤ e^{t²/2}` for every real `t`. No measurability hypothesis is needed: the law
being a probability measure forces `r` to be a.e. measurable.
Vershynin 2018, Example 2.5.8(ii); audit G1 C5. Atlas `rademacher-khintchine`
(sub-Gaussian half).
atlas: rademacher-khintchine

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_isStandardGaussian.{u_3} {Ω : Type u_3} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  {g : Ω → ℝ} (hg : NLAlib.IsStandardGaussian μ g) : ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF g 1 μ
name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_isStandardGaussian
doc:
A standard Gaussian variable is sub-Gaussian with variance proxy `1`.
Source: Vershynin (2018), Example 2.5.8(i). Atlas: `hutchinson-tail` (helper; belongs in
`NLAlib.Concentration.Scalar.SubGaussian`).

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_lintegral_exp_sq_le_two.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Ω → ℝ} (hX : AEMeasurable X μ) (K : ℝ)
  (hK : 0 < K) (hmean : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = 0) (hpsi : ∫⁻ (ω : Ω), ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp ((X ω / K) ^ 2)) ∂μ ≤ 2) :
  ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF X ⟨9 * K ^ 2, ⋯⟩ μ
name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_lintegral_exp_sq_le_two
doc:
**Orlicz square-exponential bound implies a centered sub-Gaussian MGF.** If `K>0`,
`EX=0` and the nonnegative expectation of `exp((X/K)²)` is at most two, then every
exponential tilt is integrable and `E exp(tX) ≤ exp(9K²t²/2)`, for all real `t`.
Vershynin 2018, Proposition 2.5.2; atlas `subgaussian-def` (Orlicz-to-MGF bridge).

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_logSobolev_of_bounded.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure (ι → ℝ)} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {c : ℝ}
  (hLSI : NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev μ c) (f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) (L : ℝ)
  (hLip : ∀ (x y : ι → ℝ), |f x - f y| ≤ L * √(∑ i, (x i - y i) ^ 2)) (M : ℝ) (hM : ∀ (x : ι → ℝ), |f x| ≤ M) :
  ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (fun x => f x - ∫ (y : ι → ℝ), f y ∂μ) ⟨c * L ^ 2, ⋯⟩ μ
name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_logSobolev_of_bounded
doc:
A bounded smooth Lipschitz observable under a measure satisfying a genuine LSI has
the centered sub-Gaussian MGF with variance proxy `cL²`. Exponential integrability is
derived from boundedness. Ledoux 2001, Theorem 5.3; atlas `herbst`.

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_range_oscillation.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (g : Ω → ℝ) (hg : AEMeasurable g μ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c)
  (h : ∀ (x y : Ω), |g x - g y| ≤ c) :
  ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (fun x => g x - ∫ (y : Ω), g y ∂μ) ⟨c ^ 2 / 4, ⋯⟩ μ
name: NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_range_oscillation
doc:
A measurable scalar function of range diameter at most `c≥0` has centred
MGF proxy `c²/4`. The infimum of its range need not be attained.
Source: sharp fibre Hoeffding argument `eq:fiberhoeffding`; supports `mcdiarmid`.

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_pi_of_coordinate_oscillation.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {S : ι → Type u_2} [(i : ι) → MeasurableSpace (S i)] (μ : (i : ι) → MeasureTheory.Measure (S i))
  [∀ (i : ι), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure (μ i)] (f : ((i : ι) → S i) → ℝ) (hf : Measurable f) (c : ι → ℝ)
  (hc : ∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ c i)
  (hcoord : ∀ (i : ι) (x : (j : ι) → S j) (y : S i), |f (Function.update x i y) - f x| ≤ c i) :
  ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (fun x => f x - ∫ (y : (i : ι) → S i), f y ∂MeasureTheory.Measure.pi μ)
    ⟨(∑ i, c i ^ 2) / 4, ⋯⟩ (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi μ)

doc:
**Sharp bounded differences on a finite product.** Measurable globally
bounded coordinate oscillations give the centred MGF proxy `∑ cᵢ²/4`, with no
integrability hypotheses. All coordinate spaces may differ; no standard-Borel
assumption is used, and an empty product is included.
Source: operator manuscript `thm:mcdiarmidmgf`, coordinate averaging and sharp
fibre Hoeffding; Boucheron–Lugosi–Massart 2013, Theorem 6.2.
atlas: mcdiarmid (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.hasSubgaussianMGF_srhtNormalizedRow_dotProduct {n d : ℕ} [NeZero n] (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)

The primitive directional MGF condition for the literal one-sign SRHT row

signature:

atlas: rademacher-khintchine

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T_cos_of_open_ellipse {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ)) (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
  (θ : ℝ) :
  HasSum (fun k => NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff F k * Polynomial.eval (Real.cos θ) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑k))
    (F ↑(Real.cos θ)).re
name: NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T_cos_of_open_ellipse
doc:
The Chebyshev series on a real cosine argument reconstructs the original function's
real part from the genuine open-ellipse holomorphy and bound assumptions.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 3.1(a), 8.1 and 8.2.
Atlas `chebyshev-approx-analytic` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T_of_open_ellipse {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ)) (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
  {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  HasSum (fun k => NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff F k * Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑k)) (F ↑x).re
name: NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T_of_open_ellipse
doc:
The genuine Chebyshev series reconstructs the function on every point of `[-1,1]`.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 3.1(a), 8.1 and 8.2.
Atlas `chebyshev-approx-analytic` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_interpolate_T_of_open_ellipse {F : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ M : ℝ} (hρ : 1 < ρ)
  (hFd : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ)) (hM : ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.openBernsteinEllipse ρ, ‖F z‖ ≤ M)
  (N : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
  HasSum
    (fun k =>
      NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff F k *
        Polynomial.eval x
          ((Lagrange.interpolate (Finset.range (N + 1)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.node N)) fun j =>
            Polynomial.eval (Polynomial.Chebyshev.node N j) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑k)))
    (Polynomial.eval x (NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticInterpolant F N))
name: NLAlib.hasSum_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_interpolate_T_of_open_ellipse
doc:
The actual interpolant is obtained by interpolating the genuinely reconstructed
Chebyshev series term by term; there are only finitely many nodal values.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 3.1(a) and 4.2 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature:

  (θ : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) :

    (NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F θ)
name: NLAlib.hasSum_fourier_chebyshevCircleFunction_of_open_ellipse
doc:
The Fourier series of the circle pullback reconstructs the original function pointwise,
under the genuine open-ellipse analytic assumptions.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Theorems 8.1 and 3.1(a); Mathlib's uniform Fourier reconstruction.
Atlas `chebyshev-approx-analytic` (helper).

signature: NLAlib.hasSum_pow_div_factorial_exp (x : ℝ) : HasSum (fun i => x ^ i / ↑i.factorial) (Real.exp x)
name: NLAlib.hasSum_pow_div_factorial_exp
doc:
The scalar exponential is the sum of its factorial power series.
Mathlib's general Banach-algebra theorem, specialized to reals; used by
Sachdeva–Vishnoi, Theorem 4.1 (`exp-polynomial-approx`).

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.hermitian_bernstein.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L : ℝ)
  (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (X k)) (hHerm : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X k ω).IsHermitian)
  (hL2 : ∀ (k : Fin N), MeasureTheory.MemLp (X k) 2 μ) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.lambdaMax (X k ω) ≤ L) :
  have Y := fun ω => ∑ k, X k ω;
  have v := NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment μ Y;
  v = NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ^ 2 ∂μ) ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω) ∂μ ≤ √(2 * v * Real.log ↑d) + L * Real.log ↑d / 3 ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → (μ {ω | t ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.bernsteinTail d v L t
name: NLAlib.hermitian_bernstein
doc:
Matrix Bernstein inequality, Hermitian case: for an independent sum of centered Hermitian random
matrices with `λmax ≤ L`, `𝔼 λmax(Y) ≤ √(2 v log d) + L log d / 3` and `P{λmax(Y) ≥ t} ≤
bernsteinTail d v L t`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 6.6.1. Atlas: `matrix-bernstein`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.
atlas: matrix-bernstein

signature:
NLAlib.hermitian_gaussian_series.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (A : Fin N → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ)
  (hA : ∀ (k : Fin N), (A k).IsHermitian) (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (g k))
  (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun g μ)
  (hLaw : (∀ (k : Fin N), NLAlib.IsStandardGaussian μ (g k)) ∨ ∀ (k : Fin N), NLAlib.IsRademacher μ (g k)) :
  have Y := fun ω => ∑ k, g k ω • A k;
  have v := NLAlib.hermitianSecondMoment μ Y;
  v = NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, A k ^ 2) ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω) ∂μ ≤ √(2 * v * Real.log ↑d) ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → (μ {ω | t ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.gaussianSeriesTail d v t
name: NLAlib.hermitian_gaussian_series
doc:
Matrix Gaussian and Rademacher series, Hermitian case: for `Y = ∑ k, g k • A k` the variance is
`‖∑ A k²‖`, `𝔼 λmax(Y) ≤ √(2 v log d)`, and `P{λmax(Y) ≥ t} ≤ gaussianSeriesTail d v t`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 4.6.1. Atlas: `matrix-gaussian-series`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 4*.

Gaussian and Rademacher coefficients are covered by one statement through the disjunctive law
hypothesis.
atlas: matrix-gaussian-series

error bounded by `(1+q/(s-q-1))(1+k/(t-k-1))‖S₂‖F²`. Only `t≥k+2` and `s≥q+2` are required.

first sketches and zero-rank inputs are included via exact recovery.

whose upper tail is bounded by a nonnegative integrable `F` above `a ≥ 0` is integrable,
and `E f ≤ a + ∫ₐ^∞ F(t) dt`. Integrability is derived, rather than assumed for `f`.

Thm 10.8. The nonnegative integral version `lintegral_le_of_tail_le` also covers
infinite tail envelopes.

the tail above), e.g. HMT 2011, proof of Thm 10.8 / Vershynin 2018, Lemma 1.2.1.

  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n r k t : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ}
  {F : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A = F.transpose * F) (hkt : k + 2 ≤ t) (Ω : Ωs → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin t) ℝ)
  (hΩ : MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun ω => Matrix.of.symm (Ω ω)) μ = NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t) :
  MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => (A - NLAlib.nystrom A (Ω ω)).trace) μ ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ωs), (A - NLAlib.nystrom A (Ω ω)).trace ∂μ ≤ (1 + ↑k / (↑t - ↑k - 1)) * NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq k F
name: NLAlib.integrable_and_integral_trace_sub_nystrom_le
doc:
**Randomized Nyström, expected trace error** (Gittens–Mahoney 2016, Thm 3 / §3;
Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1 specialised to Nyström; Martinsson–Tropp 2020, §19.2): if
`A = FᵀF` and `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix with `t ≥ k + 2`, then
`tr(A − A⟨Ω⟩)` is integrable and
`E tr(A − A⟨Ω⟩) ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) · ‖F − ⟦F⟧ₖ‖_F²`.

Proof: `tr(A − A⟨Ω⟩) = ‖(I − P)F‖_F²` (`trace_sub_nystrom_eq_of_eq_transpose_mul`); a.s.
the Gaussian range frame `Q` of `FΩ` has `min(rank F, t) = rank(FΩ)` columns, so `QQᵀ = P`;
then the Gaussian RSVD bound for `F`
(`integrable_and_integral_frobSq_residual_gaussianRangeFrame_le_bestRankFrobSq`).

Deviation: the right side is `bestRankFrobSq k F`; for `A = FᵀF` this equals
`∑_{i>k} λᵢ(A) = ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_*` (the atlas form), an identification not formalized here.
Index types are `Fin` (Gaussian law convention). Atlas `nystrom-randomized` (uses
`nystrom-structural`, `rsvd-expected-error`, `leverage-scores`).
atlas: nystrom-randomized (partial)

Gaussian `n × t` matrix `Ω` (`t ≥ 1`), the sketched product `M (Ω Ωᵀ / t) Nᵀ` has mean squared
error `E ‖M (Ω Ωᵀ / t) Nᵀ − M Nᵀ‖_F² = (‖M‖_F² ‖N‖_F² + ‖M Nᵀ‖_F²) / t`, and this is at most
`(2/t) ‖M‖_F² ‖N‖_F²`.

via the Isserlis formula, e.g. Martinsson–Tropp 2020, §6.3 / Woodruff 2014, Lemma 2.2.
Atlas: `gaussian-amm`. Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.approx_multiplication`.

with `Q(s)ᵀQ(s) = I` for every `s`, and let the Hutchinson test matrix `G` be independent of `S`

bounded `A`); `S` lives in an arbitrary measurable space.

matrix `G` with `r + 4 ≤ k` and `i ≠ j`, with `N = (G Gᵀ)⁻¹`,

(`integrable_and_integral_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self_sq_gaussianMatrix`). Ported from

`c = (H Hᵀ)⁻¹ H g` the least-squares coefficients of `g` on the rows of `H`.

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, Lemma B.2 (second moments of the inverse Wishart matrix);
companion of `inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`. Atlas: `inverse-wishart-frob-moment`
(helper). Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.schur_offdiag_inv` (adjugate
computation).

satisfies `1 / 2^(q−1) ≤ M`.

`Polynomial.Chebyshev.leadingCoeff_le_of_forall_abs_le_one` applied to `p / M`;
Atlas: `chebyshev-monic-minimal`. Deviation: no hypothesis `0 < q` (for `q = 0`, `p = 1` and
the bound reads `1 ≤ M`, since `0 - 1 = 0` in `ℕ`).

NLAlib.isGMRESIterate_iff_forall_dotProduct_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} :
  NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x ↔
    x - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q ∧
      ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q, A.mulVec z ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) = 0
name: NLAlib.isGMRESIterate_iff_forall_dotProduct_eq_zero
doc:
**Petrov–Galerkin characterisation.** `x` is a GMRES iterate iff `x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` and
the residual is orthogonal to `A K_q(A, r₀)`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 5.3 and
§6.5.1; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isGMRESIterate_iff_isAffineMinimiser.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) :
  NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x ↔
    NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser (fun y => NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Polynomial.X ^ 2)) (y - xs)) x₀
      (NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q) x
name: NLAlib.isGMRESIterate_iff_isAffineMinimiser
doc:
**MINRES is the class theorem's minimiser with weight `g = X²`.** For symmetric `A` and
`A x⋆ = c`, `x` is a GMRES iterate iff it minimises `‖· − x⋆‖²_{A²} = quadForm (A²) (· − x⋆)`
over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`; so `quadForm_sub_le_of_isAffineMinimiser` with `g = X²` applies.
Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.2; KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.
Atlas: `minres-bound` (helper).

signature:

name: NLAlib.isGreatest_variational_trace
doc:
Variational formula for the trace: for positive definite `M`, `tr M` is the greatest value of `tr

signature:

    (NLAlib.traceExp (H + NLAlib.matrixLog A))

doc:

name: NLAlib.isLeast_chebyshev_minimax
doc:
The Chebyshev minimax theorem on `[a, b]`, `0 < a < b`: the least possible bound `M` for
`|p|` on `[a, b]` over polynomials `p` of degree at most `q` with `p(0) = 1` is
`1 / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`, attained by `chebyshevResidual a b q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Trefethen–Bau (1997), Thm 38.5;
Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.
atlas: chebyshev-minimax

signature:
NLAlib.isLeast_chebyshev_monic_minimax (q : ℕ) :
  IsLeast {M | ∃ p, p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = q ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M} (1 / 2 ^ (q - 1))
name: NLAlib.isLeast_chebyshev_monic_minimax
doc:
The monic Chebyshev minimax theorem: over monic real polynomials of degree `q`, the least
possible bound for `|p|` on `[−1, 1]` is `1 / 2^(q−1)`, attained by `2^(1−q) T_q`.
Source: Trefethen (2013), Thm 2.2 / Rivlin (1990), Cor. 2.1.1; Atlas: `chebyshev-monic-minimal`.
Deviation: stated for all `q`, including `q = 0` (where the value is `1`).
atlas: chebyshev-monic-minimal

signature:
NLAlib.isPCGIterate_iff_isCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A P W : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hW : W.transpose * P * W = 1) {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} :
  NLAlib.IsPCGIterate A P c x₀ q x ↔
    NLAlib.IsCGIterate (W.transpose * A * W) (W.transpose.mulVec c) (W⁻¹.mulVec x₀) q (W⁻¹.mulVec x)
name: NLAlib.isPCGIterate_iff_isCGIterate
doc:
**PCG is CG on the split-preconditioned system.** If `Wᵀ P W = I` (so `P⁻¹ = WWᵀ`), then `x`
is a PCG iterate for `(A, P, c, x₀)` iff `W⁻¹x` is a CG iterate for `WᵀAW ŷ = Wᵀc` from
`W⁻¹x₀`. With `W = P^{-1/2}` this is CG on `P^{-1/2} A P^{-1/2}`; with `W = L⁻ᵀ`, `P = LLᵀ`,
CG on `L⁻¹AL⁻ᵀ`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §9.2.1 (split preconditioning).
atlas: preconditioned-cg (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_applyRectMatrix_bounds.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ρ : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {κ : Type u_3}

two-sided Euclidean squared-norm inequality used in the sparse proof.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
Orthonormal form of a subspace embedding (Woodruff 2014 §2.1; Martinsson–Tropp 2020 §8.7):
for `U` with orthonormal columns, `S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U` iff
`(1 - ε)‖x‖² ≤ ‖SUx‖² ≤ (1 + ε)‖x‖²` for every coefficient vector `x`.

Atlas: `ose-def`.
atlas: ose-def

signature:
NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues {k m d : ℕ} {S : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin m) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin d) ℝ}

  NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε ↔
    ∀ (j : Fin d), √(1 - ε) ≤ NLAlib.singularValues (S * U) ↑j ∧ NLAlib.singularValues (S * U) ↑j ≤ √(1 + ε)
name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues
doc:
Complete singular-value OSE equivalence for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`: the sketch
preserves the subspace iff every domain singular value of `S U` lies in
`[√(1−ε), √(1+ε)]`. Atlas: `ose-def`, `svd`. Includes empty dimensions.

NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues_fintype.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3}

For `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`, every domain singular value of the normalized `S U` lies in

signature:
NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_of_forall_sqrt_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3} [Fintype k]
  [Fintype m] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] {S : Matrix k m ℝ} {U : Matrix m d ℝ} (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U)
  {ε a : ℝ} (hε : ε ≤ 1) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (haε : 3 * a ≤ ε)
  (hlo : ∀ (x : d → ℝ), (1 - a) * √(x ⬝ᵥ x) ≤ √((S * U).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ (S * U).mulVec x))
  (hhi : ∀ (x : d → ℝ), √((S * U).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ (S * U).mulVec x) ≤ (1 + a) * √(x ⬝ᵥ x)) :
  NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε
name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_of_forall_sqrt_le
doc:
**Deterministic embedding criterion.** If `U` has orthonormal columns and every
`‖SUx‖` lies between `(1 − a)‖x‖` and `(1 + a)‖x‖`, with `0 ≤ a`, `3a ≤ ε ≤ 1`, then `S` is an
`ε`-subspace embedding for `range U` (since `(1 − a)² ≥ 1 − ε` and `(1 + a)² ≤ 1 + ε`).
Woodruff 2014, proof of Thm 2.3; atlas `gaussian-ose` (helper; uses `ose-def`).
atlas: gaussian-ose

signature: NLAlib.jacobiFraction (a β : ℕ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.jacobiFraction
doc:
The finite Jacobi (Stieltjes) continued fraction with `m` levels starting at level `k`:
`jacobiFraction a β x 0 k = 0` and
`jacobiFraction a β x (m+1) k = 1 / (x − a k − β (k+1)² · jacobiFraction a β x m (k+1))`, so
`jacobiFraction a β x m 0 = 1/(x − a₀ − β₁²/(x − a₁ − ⋯ − β_{m−1}²/(x − a_{m−1})))`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3. Atlas: `jacobi-matrix-identities`.

signature:
NLAlib.jacobiFraction.eq_def (a β : ℕ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) (x✝ x✝¹ : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.jacobiFraction a β x x✝ x✝¹ =
    match x✝, x✝¹ with
    | 0, x => 0
    | m.succ, k => 1 / (x - a k - β (k + 1) ^ 2 * NLAlib.jacobiFraction a β x m (k + 1))
name: NLAlib.jacobiFraction.eq_def

signature:
NLAlib.jacobiFraction_succ (a β : ℕ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) (m k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.jacobiFraction a β x m (k + 1) = NLAlib.jacobiFraction (fun i => a (i + 1)) (fun i => β (i + 1)) x m k
name: NLAlib.jacobiFraction_succ
doc: Shifting the start level of a Jacobi fraction shifts the coefficients.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_distributional (k n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G | |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec x - x ⬝ᵥ x| > ε * x ⬝ᵥ x} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)))
name: NLAlib.jl_distributional
doc:
**Distributional Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma** for the Gaussian sketch: for
`S = k^{-1/2} G` with `G` standard Gaussian `k × n`, any fixed `x : ℝⁿ` and `0 < ε < 1`,
`P[|‖Sx‖² − ‖x‖²| > ε‖x‖²] ≤ 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Lem 2.2 (stated there for the projection of a random unit vector; the
Gaussian-sketch form is Woodruff 2014 §2.1). Atlas: `jl-distributional`; uses
`gaussian-matrix-mulVec-law`, `chi-square-upper-tail`, `chi-square-lower-tail`.

Proof: with `u = x/‖x‖`, `‖Sx‖² = (‖x‖²/k) ‖Gu‖²` and `Gu` is a standard Gaussian vector, so the
event lies in `{χ²_k ≥ (1+ε)k} ∪ {χ²_k ≤ (1−ε)k}`. The Chernoff tails and
`log(1+ε) ≤ ε − ε²/2 + ε³/3`, `log(1−ε) ≤ −ε − ε²/2` bound each part by `exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.
Degenerate cases: for `x = 0` the event is empty; for `k = 0` the bound is `2`.
atlas: jl-distributional

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (↑N ^ 2 * 2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)))
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, union-bound form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for a finite
family `p : Fin N → ℝⁿ`, the probability that the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` distorts some
pairwise squared distance `‖p i − p j‖²` by more than a factor `1 ± ε` is at most
`N² · 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Deviation: the union is taken over all `N²` ordered pairs (not the `N(N−1)/2` unordered ones),
which costs a constant factor `2` in the bound. No measurability hypothesis is needed (the union
bound holds for the outer measure).

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  ∃ S,
    ∀ (i j : Fin N),
      (1 - ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j) ≤ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ∧
        S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ≤ (1 + ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, existence form (Johnson–Lindenstrauss 1984; Dasgupta–Gupta
2003, Thm 2.1): any `N ≥ 2` points of `ℝⁿ` admit a linear map `S : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ` with
`k ≥ 48 log N / ε²` that preserves every pairwise squared distance to within `1 ± ε`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 2)
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, `O(ε⁻² log N)` form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for
`N ≥ 2` points, `0 < ε < 1` and `k ≥ 48 log N / ε²`, the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G`
distorts some pairwise squared distance by more than `1 ± ε` with probability at most `1/2`.

Deviation: the explicit constant `48` (from `(ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ ≤ 12/ε²` and
`log(4N²) ≤ 4 log N` for `N ≥ 2`) is not optimised; Dasgupta–Gupta's constant is `4·(1/2 − ε/3)⁻¹`
at failure probability `1 − 1/N`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε δ : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
  (hk : (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)⁻¹ * Real.log (2 * ↑N ^ 2 / δ) ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal δ
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma with explicit dimension (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): if
`0 < ε < 1`, `0 < δ` and `k ≥ (ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ log(2N²/δ)`, then with probability at least
`1 − δ` the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` preserves all pairwise squared distances of
`p : Fin N → ℝⁿ` to within `1 ± ε`.

Deviation: Dasgupta–Gupta take `k ≥ 4 (ε²/2 − ε³/3)⁻¹ log N`, aiming at success probability
`1/N`; we state the general-`δ` form with the constant coming from the ordered-pair union bound
in `jl_lemma`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.krylovFunApprox.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]
  (Q : Matrix n k ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox
doc:
The Krylov (Lanczos-FA) approximation of `f(A) b` from a basis matrix `Q`:
`Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b`, with `f(QᵀAQ) = cfc f (Qᵀ * A * Q)`. With the Lanczos basis, `Qᵀ b = ‖b‖ e₁`
and this is `‖b‖ Q f(T_q) e₁`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], eq. (3.2); Higham (2008)
[`higham08`], §13.2. Deviation: any `Q` (the theorems assume orthonormal columns and
`K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (definition).

signature:
NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_congr.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {k' : Type u_3} [Fintype k'] [DecidableEq k']
  {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} {Q' : Matrix n k' ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q')
  (hR : Q.mulVecLin.range = Q'.mulVecLin.range) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q A f b = NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q' A f b
name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_congr
doc:
**Lanczos-FA depends only on the range of `Q`.** If `Q` and `Q'` have orthonormal columns
and the same range, then `Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b = Q' f(Q'ᵀAQ') Q'ᵀ b` (for `Q' = QU` with `U`
orthogonal, `f(UᵀTU) = Uᵀ f(T) U`). Source: `docs/KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS.md` §3.9; Saad (1992)
[`saad92`], §3 (basis-independence of the Krylov projection).
Deviation: `A` symmetric (for nonsymmetric `A` the real `cfc` is not the matrix function).
Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper: basis independence of the approximant).

name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eq_aeval_interpolate
doc:
**Lanczos-FA is the interpolant at the Ritz values.** If `Q` has at most `q` columns, then
`krylovFunApprox Q A f b = p(A) b` for the Lagrange interpolant `p` of `f` at the distinct
eigenvalues of `QᵀAQ`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.3.
Deviation: `Q` is any orthonormal matrix with at most `q` columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q` (the
source takes the Lanczos basis, `range Q = K_q`); the Ritz values are interpolated without
multiplicity (Lagrange, not Hermite), which suffices because `f(T)` only sees `f` on `spec T`.
Atlas: proposed id `lanczos-fa-interpolation`; uses `krylov-polynomial-exactness`.
atlas: lanczos-fa-interpolation

name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eq_aeval_of_forall_eval_eq
doc:
**Lanczos-FA interpolates at the Ritz values (general form).** If `p` has `deg p < q` and
agrees with `f` at the eigenvalues of `T = QᵀAQ` (the Ritz values), then
`krylovFunApprox Q A f b = p(A) b`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.3.
Deviation: any orthonormal `Q` with `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`; Lagrange (not Hermite)
interpolation, the agreement being only required at the Ritz values.
Atlas: proposed id `lanczos-fa-interpolation`; uses `krylov-polynomial-exactness`.
atlas: lanczos-fa-interpolation

signature:
NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eval_eq_aeval.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < ↑q) :
  NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q A (fun x => Polynomial.eval x p) b = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b
name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eval_eq_aeval
doc:
**Lanczos-FA is exact on polynomials.** For symmetric `A`, `Q` with orthonormal columns and
`K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, `krylovFunApprox Q A p b = p(A) b` for every `p` with `deg p < q`.
Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Lemma 3.1.
Deviation: the matrix-function form needs `A` symmetric (so that `QᵀAQ` is self-adjoint and
`cfc` is the polynomial calculus); `mulVec_aeval_transpose_mul_mul_mulVec_eq` is the form for
any `A`.
atlas: krylov-polynomial-exactness (partial)

signature: NLAlib.krylovGrade.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) : ℕ
name: NLAlib.krylovGrade
doc:
The grade of `b` with respect to `A`: `ν(A, b) = dim span {Aⁱ b : i ∈ ℕ}`, equivalently the
degree of the monic polynomial `μ_{A,b}` of least degree with `μ_{A,b}(A) b = 0`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Def. before Prop 6.1; Liesen–Strakoš (2013) [`ls13`], §2.2.
Deviation: real scalars only (the atlas entry allows any field).
atlas: krylov-grade (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.krylovSpace_mul_mulVec_eq_map.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (W B : Matrix n n ℝ) (v : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : NLAlib.krylovSpace (W * B) (W.mulVec v) q = Submodule.map W.mulVecLin (NLAlib.krylovSpace (B * W) v q)
name: NLAlib.krylovSpace_mul_mulVec_eq_map
doc:
**Krylov spaces under a change of variables:** `K_q(WB, Wv) = W K_q(BW, v)`. With
`P⁻¹ = WWᵀ` and `B = WᵀA` this is `K_q(P⁻¹A, P⁻¹r) = W K_q(WᵀAW, Wᵀr)`, the identity behind
split preconditioning. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §9.2.1.
atlas: preconditioned-cg (partial)

name: NLAlib.krylovSpace_succ
doc:
One Krylov step adds one generator: `K_{q+1}(A,b) = K_q(A,b) ⊔ span {A^q b}`.

name: NLAlib.leverageScore
doc:
The **leverage score** of row `i` of `A`: `ℓᵢ(A) = (A A⁺)ᵢᵢ`, the `i`-th diagonal entry of
the orthogonal projector onto `range A`. Defined for every real matrix (any rank, empty
shapes). Drineas–Mahoney–Muthukrishnan–Woodruff 2012, Def. 1; Woodruff 2014, Def. 2.12.
Atlas `leverage-scores`.
atlas: leverage-scores

name: NLAlib.leverageScore_eq_sum_sq_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
**Leverage scores are squared row norms of any orthonormal basis.** If `U` has
orthonormal columns and is a basis of `range A` (`range A ⊆ range U`, written `U (Uᵀ A) = A`,
and `U` has at most `rank A` columns), then `ℓᵢ(A) = ∑ⱼ Uᵢⱼ² = ‖U_{i,:}‖²`. Since the left side
does not mention `U`, the row norms do not depend on the choice of basis.
Drineas–Mahoney–Muthukrishnan–Woodruff 2012, Def. 1 and the remark after it; Woodruff 2014,
Def. 2.12. Atlas `leverage-scores`. Deviation: "orthonormal basis of `range A`" is spelled as the
two hypotheses `hUA`, `hr` (together with orthonormality they force `range U = range A`).
atlas: leverage-scores

signature:

  [DecidableEq q] {U : Matrix m q ℝ} (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) (i : m) :
  NLAlib.leverageScore U i = ∑ j, U i j ^ 2
name: NLAlib.leverageScore_eq_sum_sq_of_self
doc:
For a matrix `U` with orthonormal columns, `ℓᵢ(U) = ∑ⱼ Uᵢⱼ²`.
Woodruff 2014, §2.4; atlas `leverage-scores`.

signature:
NLAlib.lintegral_frobSq_transpose_mul_sketch_sub_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {Ωs : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ωs]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} {k : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} [Fintype k] [Fintype n] {d₁ : Type u_4} {d₂ : Type u_5}
  [Fintype d₁] [Fintype d₂] (S : Ωs → Matrix k n ℝ) (hS : ∀ (i : k) (j : n), Measurable fun ω => S ω i j) {ε : ℝ}
  (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
  (hmom :
    ∀ (x : n → ℝ),
      ∫⁻ (ω : Ωs), ENNReal.ofReal (((S ω).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ (S ω).mulVec x - x ⬝ᵥ x) ^ 2) ∂μ ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal (ε ^ 2 * (x ⬝ᵥ x) ^ 2))
  (A : Matrix n d₁ ℝ) (B : Matrix n d₂ ℝ) :
  ∫⁻ (ω : Ωs), ENNReal.ofReal (NLAlib.frobSq (A.transpose * (S ω).transpose * S ω * B - A.transpose * B)) ∂μ ≤

name: NLAlib.lintegral_frobSq_transpose_mul_sketch_sub_le
doc:
**Approximate matrix multiplication from the JL moment property.** If the random sketch
`S` (entrywise measurable) satisfies `E (‖Sx‖² − ‖x‖²)² ≤ ε² ‖x‖⁴` for every `x`, with `ε ≥ 0`,
then for fixed `A ∈ ℝ^{n×d₁}`, `B ∈ ℝ^{n×d₂}`,
`E ‖AᵀSᵀSB − AᵀB‖_F² ≤ ε² ‖A‖_F² ‖B‖_F²`.

Woodruff 2014, Thm 2.8 (the `ℓ = 2` case of the `(ε, δ, ℓ)`-JL moment property; Kane–Nelson
2014); Sarlós 2006, Lem 6. Atlas `amm-ose`. Deviations: stated with lower Lebesgue integrals
(no integrability hypothesis); the hypothesis is the second-moment property itself, not a tail
bound; constant `1`.
atlas: amm-ose

signature:
NLAlib.lintegral_le_of_tail_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)

name: NLAlib.lintegral_le_of_tail_le
doc:
**Expectation from a general tail envelope, nonnegative integral form.** If `f ≥ 0`
a.e. on a probability space, `a ≥ 0`, and `P(f > t) ≤ F(t)` for `t > a`, then
`E f ≤ a + ∫ₐ^∞ F(t) dt`. No finiteness or measurability assumption on the envelope
is needed for this extended nonnegative integral inequality.

Standard layer-cake estimate; Vershynin 2018, Lemma 1.2.1; HMT 2011, proof of
Thm 10.8. Uses Mathlib's `lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt`.
atlas: tail-integral

signature:

Thm 2.8; Kane–Nelson 2014. Atlas `amm-ose`.

`GaussianMatrix.chi_square_neg_moment` (`cnm_gamma_lintegral`).

`a, b ≥ 0` (written with `ENNReal.ofReal`), then `∫⁻ (X − Y)² ≤ (a + b)²`. Proof: the pointwise

  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (θ : ℝ)
  (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (X k)) (hHerm : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X k ω).IsHermitian)

      ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMax (∑ k, X k ω) ∂μ ≤ Real.log (NLAlib.traceExp (NLAlib.cumulantSum μ X θ)) / θ ∧
        ∀ (t : ℝ),
          (μ {ω | t ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMax (∑ k, X k ω)}).toReal ≤
            Real.exp (-θ * t) * NLAlib.traceExp (NLAlib.cumulantSum μ X θ)) ∧

signature: NLAlib.matrixMeasurableSpace.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} : MeasurableSpace (Matrix m n ℂ)
name: NLAlib.matrixMeasurableSpace
doc:
The Borel σ-algebra on complex matrices (for the norm topology), used to state measurability of
random matrices.

This global instance is a deliberate exception to STANDARDS §3, which states measurability of
matrix-valued maps entrywise because Mathlib has no `MeasurableSpace (Matrix m n ℂ)`. The matrix
concentration development (ported from the Tropp 2015 Prove2me missions) treats random matrices as
`Measurable` maps into a normed space and integrates them as Bochner integrals in the operator
norm; every statement in `NLAlib/Concentration/Matrix/` that mentions `Measurable`, `iIndepFun` or
`Integrable` for a matrix-valued map elaborates through this instance, so removing it would mean
restating the whole development. Mathlib declares no competing instance (`Matrix` is a
non-reducible `def`, so the product σ-algebra on `m → n → ℂ` is not found), hence no diamond. It
could be made `scoped`: checked 2026-10-09, wrapping it in `namespace MatrixBorel` as a `scoped
instance` and adding `open scoped NLAlib.MatrixBorel` to the 35 modules under
`Concentration/Matrix/` that import this one (directly or not) builds cleanly, at the price of
every downstream user opening the scope to state the hypotheses of the public theorems.

signature:

  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m n N : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero n] (S : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ)
  (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (S k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun S μ)
  (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), S k ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.spectralNorm (S k ω) ≤ L) :
  have Z := fun ω => ∑ k, S k ω;
  have v := NLAlib.rectSecondMoment μ Z;
  v =
      max (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), S k ω * (S k ω).conjTranspose ∂μ))
        (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), (S k ω).conjTranspose * S k ω ∂μ)) ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω) ∂μ ≤ √(2 * v * Real.log (↑m + ↑n)) + L * Real.log (↑m + ↑n) / 3 ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → (μ {ω | t ≤ NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.bernsteinTail (m + n) v L t

n` matrices with `‖S k‖ ≤ L`, `𝔼 ‖Z‖ ≤ √(2 v log (m + n)) + L log (m + n) / 3` and `P{‖Z‖ ≥ t} ≤
bernsteinTail (m + n) v L t`.

Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.

  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L : ℝ)
  (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (X k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hHerm : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X k ω).IsHermitian)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, 0 ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMin (X k ω) ∧ NLAlib.lambdaMax (X k ω) ≤ L) :
  have Y := fun ω => ∑ k, X k ω;
  have a := NLAlib.lambdaMin (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ);
  have b := NLAlib.lambdaMax (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ);
  a = NLAlib.lambdaMin (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ) ∧
    b = NLAlib.lambdaMax (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ) ∧
      (∀ (θ : ℝ),
          0 < θ →
            (1 - Real.exp (-θ)) / θ * a - L * Real.log ↑d / θ ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMin (Y ω) ∂μ ∧
              ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω) ∂μ ≤ (Real.exp θ - 1) / θ * b + L * Real.log ↑d / θ) ∧
        (∀ (ε : ℝ),
            0 ≤ ε → ε < 1 → (μ {ω | NLAlib.lambdaMin (Y ω) ≤ (1 - ε) * a}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail d a L ε) ∧
          ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → (μ {ω | (1 + ε) * b ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail d b L ε

doc:
Matrix Chernoff inequality: for an independent sum of random positive semidefinite matrices with
`λmax ≤ L`, expectation bounds on `λmin` and `λmax` for every `θ > 0` and the lower and upper
tails `chernoffLowerTail`, `chernoffUpperTail`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 5.1.1, eqs (5.1.1–6). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`. Ported from the Prove2me mission
*An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 5*.

The expectation bounds are stated for every `θ > 0` before optimisation; degenerate `L = 0`
follows the piecewise tail definitions.

  (hLocal : ∀ (j : ℕ), NLAlib.HasLocalMatrixSecondMoment μ (↑ℱ j) (X j) (V j)) {L t v : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) (ht : 0 ≤ t)
  (hv : 0 < v) (hBound : ∀ (j : ℕ), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, X j ω ≤ (algebraMap ℝ (Matrix n n ℂ)) L) :
  (μ {ω | ∃ k, t ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMax (NLAlib.matrixIncrementSum X k ω) ∧ ‖NLAlib.matrixIncrementSum V k ω‖ ≤ v}).toReal ≤
    ↑(Fintype.card n) * Real.exp (-(t ^ 2 / (2 * (v + L * t / 3))))
name: NLAlib.matrix_freedman
doc:
The arbitrary-time upper matrix Freedman inequality on an arbitrary probability
space. Increments are adapted integrable Hermitian matrices, actually conditionally
centered, and bounded only above by `L I`. Predictable finite PSD variance increments
satisfy the genuine extended local quadratic moment identities on every predictable
set and every deterministic complex vector. Neither unconditional square integrability
nor integrability of the original variance is assumed. The bound includes `t=0` and
`L=0` and has the exact Bernstein coefficient.
Source: Tropp 2011, Theorem 1.2; supplied operator rederivations `thm:freedman` and
Part VII audit `audit:local-moment`, `audit:combined`.
atlas: matrix-freedman

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_gaussian_series.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m n N : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero n] (B : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ)
  (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (g k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun g μ)
  (hLaw : (∀ (k : Fin N), NLAlib.IsStandardGaussian μ (g k)) ∨ ∀ (k : Fin N), NLAlib.IsRademacher μ (g k)) :
  have Z := fun ω => ∑ k, g k ω • B k;
  have v := NLAlib.rectSecondMoment μ Z;
  v =
      max (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, B k * (B k).conjTranspose))
        (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, (B k).conjTranspose * B k)) ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω) ∂μ ≤ √(2 * v * Real.log (↑m + ↑n)) ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → (μ {ω | t ≤ NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.gaussianSeriesTail (m + n) v t
name: NLAlib.matrix_gaussian_series
doc:
Matrix Gaussian and Rademacher series, rectangular case: for `Z = ∑ k, g k • B k` the variance is
the maximum of the two row/column sums, `𝔼 ‖Z‖ ≤ √(2 v log (m + n))`, and `P{‖Z‖ ≥ t} ≤
gaussianSeriesTail (m + n) v t`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 4.1.1. Atlas: `matrix-gaussian-series`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 4*.

Gaussian and Rademacher coefficients are covered by one statement through the disjunctive law
hypothesis.

doc:

`rank B + d ≤ N` with `d ≥ 1`. For a standard Gaussian vector `g ∈ ℝᴺ` and `0 ≤ u ≤ d`,

basis of `(range B)ᗮ` (Bessel), which is `χ²_d` by rotation invariance; then the chi-square lower
tail. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.

`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_dist_colspace_small_ball`.

signature:
NLAlib.mem_blockKrylovSpace_iff.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype s]
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (Ω : Matrix n s ℝ) (q : ℕ) (x : n → ℝ) :
  x ∈ NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace A Ω q ↔
    ∃ p, (∀ (j : s), (p j).degree < ↑q) ∧ x = ∑ j, ((Polynomial.aeval A) (p j)).mulVec (Ω.col j)
name: NLAlib.mem_blockKrylovSpace_iff
doc:
Matrix-polynomial characterisation of the block Krylov space (valid for every `q`):
`x ∈ K_q(A, Ω) ↔ x = ∑_j p_j(A) Ω e_j` for polynomials `p_j` of degree `< q`. Equivalently
`x = ∑_{i<q} A^i Ω c_i`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3; Tropp–Webber (2023) [`tw23`], §7.
atlas: block-krylov-subspace

signature:
NLAlib.mem_krylovSpace_iff.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ}
  (hq : 0 < q) (x : n → ℝ) : x ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ↔ ∃ p, p.natDegree < q ∧ x = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b
name: NLAlib.mem_krylovSpace_iff
doc:
Polynomial characterisation of the Krylov space, `natDegree` form:
for `0 < q`, `x ∈ K_q(A,b) ↔ ∃ p, natDeg p < q ∧ x = p(A) b`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4. Atlas: `krylov-subspace`.
Deviation: needs `0 < q` (for `q = 0` no polynomial has `natDegree < 0`; use
`mem_krylovSpace_iff_degree`).
atlas: krylov-subspace

signature:
NLAlib.mem_krylovSpace_iff_degree.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) (x : n → ℝ) : x ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ↔ ∃ p, p.degree < ↑q ∧ x = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b
name: NLAlib.mem_krylovSpace_iff_degree
doc:
Polynomial characterisation of the Krylov space, degree form (valid for every `q`, including
`q = 0` where both sides are `{0}`): `x ∈ K_q(A,b) ↔ x = p(A) b` for some `p` with `deg p < q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4; Martinsson–Tropp (2020) [`mt20`], §11.7.
Atlas: `krylov-subspace`.
atlas: krylov-subspace

signature:

NLAlib.mulVec_aeval_transpose_mul_mul_mulVec_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2}

    ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b

columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, then `Q p(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b = p(A) b` for every `p` with
`deg p < q`, for any square `A`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Lemma 3.1; Trefethen–Bau
(1997) [`tb97`], Thm 34.1 (Arnoldi form).

signature:
NLAlib.mul_sq_le_min_hutchinson_exponent_of_posSemidef.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype n]

signature:
NLAlib.mul_trace_pow_mul_sq_le_trace_pow_mul_inversePowerHessianKernel.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

name: NLAlib.mul_transpose_aeval_gram_mul_mul_eq_of_blockKrylovSpace_le
doc:
A frame containing the block Krylov space reproduces every filtered sketch of degree
below the Krylov order, simultaneously. Source: manuscript `sa:filter`, its final block
Krylov specialization; Musco--Musco (2015), polynomial competitor argument.

signature:
NLAlib.mul_transpose_eq_mul_moorePenroseInverse.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq q] {Q : Matrix m q ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  {Y : Matrix m n ℝ} (hQY : Q * (Q.transpose * Y) = Y) (hr : Fintype.card q ≤ Y.rank) :
  Q * Q.transpose = Y * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse Y
name: NLAlib.mul_transpose_eq_mul_moorePenroseInverse
doc:
**Uniqueness of the orthogonal projector onto a range.** If `Q` has orthonormal columns,
`range Y ⊆ range Q` (written `Q (Qᵀ Y) = Y`) and `rank Y` is at least the number of columns of
`Q` (so the two ranges coincide), then `QQᵀ = Y Y⁺`.

Proof: `P₁ = QQᵀ` and `P₂ = YY⁺` are symmetric idempotents with `P₁P₂ = P₂ = P₂P₁`, so
`M = P₁ − P₂` is a symmetric idempotent and `‖M‖_F² = tr M = card q − rank Y ≤ 0`.
Standard (Golub–Van Loan, 4th ed., §2.5.1: the orthogonal projector onto a subspace is unique).
Atlas `leverage-scores` (basis independence), `projection-facts`. Belongs in
`Matrix/MoorePenrose.lean`.

signature:

  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q') (h : Q.mulVecLin.range = Q'.mulVecLin.range) :
  Q * Q.transpose = Q' * Q'.transpose

doc:
The orthogonal projector depends only on the range: if `Q`, `Q'` have orthonormal columns
and the same range, then `QQᵀ = Q'Q'ᵀ`. Atlas `projection-facts`.

signature:

`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (sharp limiting coefficient helper).

`b₀=1/(λmin+ε)`, with `w` the Gram eigenvalues.

signature:
NLAlib.pi_gaussianReal_map_sq_dist_rowSpace {n k : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (hH : H.rank = n) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun g => g ⬝ᵥ g - H.mulVec g ⬝ᵥ (H * H.transpose)⁻¹.mulVec (H.mulVec g))
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) =
    MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => ∑ j, x j ^ 2)
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
name: NLAlib.pi_gaussianReal_map_sq_dist_rowSpace
doc:
**Law of the residual of a Gaussian row.** Let `H` be a fixed `n × k` real matrix of rank
`n` and `g` a standard Gaussian vector in `ℝᵏ`. The squared distance from `g` to the row space of
`H`, `‖g‖² - (H g)ᵀ (H Hᵀ)⁻¹ (H g)`, has the `χ²_{k-n}` law (the law of `∑ⱼ Xⱼ²`,
`X ~ N(0, I_{k-n})`).

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, Lemma B.2 / HMT 2011, Prop A.5. Atlas: `inverse-wishart-mean`
(helper). Proof ported from the Prove2me solution `Sol_GaussianMatrix_residual_law`
(orthonormal basis of `ker H` and the block law `gaussianMatrix_map_block`, atlas
`block-law-indep`).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (g p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) =
    ∑ i,
      Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) g * Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p ^ 2 *
        ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
`(p(A)v)ᵀ g(A) (p(A)v) = ∑ᵢ g(λᵢ) p(λᵢ)² ⟨uᵢ, v⟩²` for real symmetric `A` and polynomials
`p`, `g`. Atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {g p : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)
  (hg : ∀ x ∈ S, 0 ≤ Polynomial.eval x g) (hp : ∀ x ∈ S, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) ≤
    M ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) v
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Polynomial bound, weighted form.** If every eigenvalue of the real symmetric `A` lies in
`S`, the weight polynomial `g` is nonnegative on `S` and `|p| ≤ M` on `S`, then
`(p(A)v)ᵀ g(A) (p(A)v) ≤ M² vᵀ g(A) v`, i.e. `‖p(A) v‖_{g(A)} ≤ M ‖v‖_{g(A)}`. The weights
`g = X` (energy norm, CG), `g = X²` (residual norm, MINRES) and `g = 1` (error norm) are the
cases used by Krylov methods. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1; Saad (2003),
Thm 6.29 (case `g = X`). Generalises `quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le` (KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2).
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) =
    ∑ i, hA.eigenvalues i * Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p ^ 2 * ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
`(p(A)v)ᵀ A (p(A)v) = ∑ᵢ λᵢ p(λᵢ)² ⟨uᵢ, v⟩²` for real symmetric `A`. Audit G3 C1;
atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hS : S ⊆ Set.Ici 0) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)
  (hp : ∀ x ∈ S, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) ≤ M ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A v
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Polynomial bound, energy form.** If every eigenvalue of the real symmetric `A` lies in
`S ⊆ [0, ∞)` (so `A` is positive semidefinite) and `|p| ≤ M` on `S`, then
`(p(A)v)ᵀ A (p(A)v) ≤ M² vᵀ A v`, i.e. `‖p(A) v‖_A ≤ M ‖v‖_A`. This is the form used for the
CG error (Greenbaum 1997, §3.1; Saad 2003, Thm 6.29); audit G3 C1;
atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`. The case `g = X` of `quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le`.
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_chebyshevIterate_sub_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q - xs) ≤
    (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_chebyshevIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Chebyshev iteration, `A`-norm rate.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
`0 < a < b`, and `A x⋆ = c`,
`‖x_q − x⋆‖²_A ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3; Golub–Varga (1961) [`gv61`]. Deviation: squared norms;
the iterate is defined by its residual polynomial (no recurrence).
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

name: NLAlib.quadForm_polyIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Error bound for a polynomial method, weighted norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in
`S`, a weight `g ≥ 0` on `S` and `|1 − x s(x)| ≤ M` on `S`,
`‖x − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.1;
Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1.
atlas: polynomial-method-def

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_reindex.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ) (e : ι ≃ κ)
  (z : ι → ℝ) : (NLAlib.quadForm ((Matrix.reindex e e) A) fun k => z (e.symm k)) = NLAlib.quadForm A z
name: NLAlib.quadForm_reindex
doc:
Relabelling the coordinates by an equivalence does not change the quadratic form.
Atlas `hanson-wright` (index transport).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Richardson contraction, weighted norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
step `ω ≥ 0`, `A x⋆ = c` and a weight `g ≥ 0` on `[a, b]`,
`‖x_q − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ ρ^{2q} ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}` with `ρ = max(|1 − ωa|, |1 − ωb|)`. With
`g = X` (`0 ≤ a`) this is the `A`-norm bound of the atlas, with `g = 1` the Euclidean error.
Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2.
Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`), squared norms.
atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le_of_optimal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (NLAlib.richardsonIterate (2 / (a + b)) A c x₀ q - xs) ≤
    (((b - a) / (b + a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le_of_optimal
doc:
**Richardson with the optimal step** `ω = 2/(a + b)`: for symmetric positive definite `A`
with spectrum in `[a, b]`, `0 < a ≤ b`, `‖x_q − x⋆‖²_A ≤ ((b − a)/(b + a))^{2q} ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2.1; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1.
Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`), squared norms.
atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_rowSelector.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (i : n) (z : n → ℝ) :

doc: `zᵀ (rowSelector A i) z = zᵢ (A z)ᵢ`. Atlas: `diagonal-estimator` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_sq_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (z : n → ℝ) :

doc:
Expansion `(zᵀ A z)² = ∑ᵢⱼₖₗ A_ij A_kl z_i z_j z_k z_l`. Atlas: `hutchinson-variance`
(helper).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isAffineMinimiser
doc:
**The class theorem.** Let `A` be symmetric, `A x⋆ = c`, and `g` a weight polynomial with
`g(λᵢ) ≥ 0` at every eigenvalue. If `x` minimises `‖· − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} = quadForm (g(A)) (· − x⋆)`
over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`, then for every residual polynomial `p` (`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`) with
`|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue, `‖x − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}`.
CG is `g = X` (via `cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub`), MINRES `g = X²`, the error-minimising
method `g = 1`. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1 (CG) and §3.2 (MINRES);
Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Thm 6.29; KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.
Atlas: `cg-convergence`, `minres-bound` (the shared step; tags are on the instances).
atlas: affine-krylov-minimiser

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (x - xs) ≤ (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate
doc:
**CG convergence, condition-number form.** Let `A` be symmetric with every eigenvalue in
`[a, b]`, `0 < a < b`, `A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th CG iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ (2 ((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²`; with `κ = b/a`,
`(√b − √a)/(√b + √a) = (√κ − 1)/(√κ + 1)`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.5; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8.
Atlas: `cg-convergence`; uses `chebyshev-minimax`, `polynomial-spectral-bound`,
`krylov-subspace`. Deviation: squared `A`-norms (the source states the unsquared form).
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (x - xs) ≤ (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_le
doc:
**CG convergence, condition-number form including `a = b`.** As
`quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate` but for `0 < a ≤ b`. When `a = b` (`A = aI`), CG is exact
after one step and the bound reads `0` for `q ≥ 1` and `4 ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²` for `q = 0`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.5. Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_poly
doc:
**CG error bound, polynomial form.** Let `A` be symmetric positive semidefinite,
`A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th CG iterate from `x₀`. For every polynomial `p` with `deg p ≤ q`,
`p(0) = 1` and `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue,
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²` (with `‖v‖_A² = quadForm A v`).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.3 (and the inequality (38.10)); Saad (2003),
Thm 6.29. Atlas: `cg-convergence`; uses `polynomial-spectral-bound`, `krylov-subspace`,
`residual-polynomial` (the case `g = X` of `quadForm_sub_le_of_isAffineMinimiser`).
atlas: cg-convergence

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isPCGIterate
doc:
**Preconditioned CG bound under a Loewner sandwich.** Let `P` be positive definite, `A` with
`a P ≼ A ≼ b P` for `0 < a ≤ b` (so `A` is symmetric positive definite and `κ(P⁻¹A) ≤ b/a`),
`A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th PCG iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²`.
Proof: CG on `P^{-1/2} A P^{-1/2}`, whose spectrum lies in `[a, b]`
(`isPCGIterate_iff_isCGIterate`, `quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_le`).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §9.2; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], Ch. 8.
Deviation: squared `A`-norms.
atlas: preconditioned-cg

signature:
NLAlib.rademacher_hutchinson_moments.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {g : Ω → ℝ} (hg : AEMeasurable g μ) (hlaw : NLAlib.IsRademacher μ g) :
  MeasureTheory.MemLp g 2 μ ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), g ω ∂μ = 0 ∧
      ∫ (ω : Ω), g ω ^ 2 ∂μ = 1 ∧ MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => g ω ^ 4) μ ∧ ∫ (ω : Ω), g ω ^ 4 ∂μ = 1
name: NLAlib.rademacher_hutchinson_moments

signature:
NLAlib.rademacher_matrix_mgf_cgf_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (g : Ω → ℝ) (hMeas : Measurable g) (hLaw : NLAlib.IsRademacher μ g) (θ : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.LoewnerLE (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp ((θ * g ω) • A) ∂μ) (NLAlib.matrixExp ((θ ^ 2 / 2) • A ^ 2)) ∧
    NLAlib.LoewnerLE (NLAlib.matrixLog (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp ((θ * g ω) • A) ∂μ)) ((θ ^ 2 / 2) • A ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.rademacher_matrix_mgf_cgf_le
doc:
For a Rademacher `g` and Hermitian `A`, `𝔼 matrixExp (θ g A) ≼ matrixExp (θ²/2 • A²)` and its
logarithm is `≼ θ²/2 • A²`.

Tropp 2015, Lemma 4.6.3. Atlas: `matrix-gaussian-series`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 4*.

signature:
NLAlib.rademacher_pi_coordinate_moments.{u_1} {κ : Type u_1} [Fintype κ] (i : κ) :

name: NLAlib.rank_truncatedRsvdOutput_le
doc:
Standard postprocessed RSVD has rank at most the target rank, for all
input and frame dimensions. HMT 2011, §9.2; atlas `rsvd-expected-error`.
atlas: rsvd-expected-error

name: NLAlib.rawGeneralizedNystrom
doc:
The actual raw generalized Nyström estimator, using a general
Moore–Penrose inverse. Rank-deficient sketches are included.
Source: Tropp–Webber 2023, Section 5. Atlas: `gn-expected-error`.
atlas: gn-expected-error

signature:
NLAlib.rawGeneralizedNystrom_eq_sketchedOutput.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3}
  {t : Type u_4} {s : Type u_5} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype q] [Fintype t] [Fintype s] [DecidableEq q]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (Y : Matrix m t ℝ) (Q : Matrix m q ℝ) (Ψ : Matrix m s ℝ) (hY : Q * (Q.transpose * Y) = Y)
  (hRank : Y.rank = Fintype.card q) (hΨ : IsUnit ((Ψ.transpose * Q).transpose * (Ψ.transpose * Q))) :
  NLAlib.rawGeneralizedNystrom A Y Ψ = NLAlib.sketchedOutput Q Ψ A
name: NLAlib.rawGeneralizedNystrom_eq_sketchedOutput
doc:
The raw generalized Nyström output agrees with the normalized-frame
output whenever the supplied frame has the exact sketch rank and the second
sketch is injective on that frame. No full rank of the raw first sketch is
assumed. Source: Tropp–Webber 2023, Section 5; atlas `gn-expected-error`.

name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_le_lanczosRitzValue_of_mem
doc:
Density of rational coefficients proves the true variational comparison for every
vector in the actual Krylov space. Zero polynomial vectors are included.
Source: manuscript `rt:random-start`, measurability paragraph.

signature:
NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_toEuclideanCLM_bounds.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (b : n → ℝ) :
  0 ≤ (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A).rayleighQuotient (WithLp.toLp 2 b) ∧
    (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A).rayleighQuotient (WithLp.toLp 2 b) ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A
name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_toEuclideanCLM_bounds
doc:
A PSD matrix's totalized Rayleigh quotient lies between zero and its spectral
norm, even at a zero vector. Source: the spectral theorem; manuscript `rt:power`.

signature:
NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_toEuclideanCLM_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (b : n → ℝ) : (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM A).rayleighQuotient (WithLp.toLp 2 b) = b ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec b / b ⬝ᵥ b
name: NLAlib.rayleighQuotient_toEuclideanCLM_eq
doc:
Mathlib's Rayleigh quotient of a real matrix is its ordinary quadratic quotient.
Source: Mathlib's `ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient`; manuscript `rt:power`.
The zero-vector convention is totalized division by zero.

signature: NLAlib.reTraceCLM.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] : Matrix ι ι ℂ →L[ℝ] ℝ
name: NLAlib.reTraceCLM
doc:
Real part of complex matrix trace as a continuous real-linear map.
Source: trace linearity; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature: NLAlib.reTraceCLM_apply.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (M : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : NLAlib.reTraceCLM M = M.trace.re
name: NLAlib.reTraceCLM_apply
doc:
The continuous trace map computes the usual real trace.
Source: trace linearity; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_diag_mem_Icc_of_isHermitian_of_isIdempotentElem.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (P : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hs : P.IsHermitian) (hp : IsIdempotentElem P) (j : ι) : (P j j).re ∈ Set.Icc 0 1
name: NLAlib.re_diag_mem_Icc_of_isHermitian_of_isIdempotentElem
doc:
Every diagonal capture weight of a genuine complex orthogonal projector
lies in `[0,1]`, including zero dimensions. Source: `sa:volume-theorem`.

signature: NLAlib.re_fourier_nat_coe_eq_cos (k : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) : ((fourier ↑k) ↑θ).re = Real.cos (↑k * θ)
name: NLAlib.re_fourier_nat_coe_eq_cos
doc:
The real part of a period-`2π` Fourier monomial is the usual cosine frequency.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8; used by analytic Chebyshev approximation
and sharp Jackson. Relocated unchanged from `NLAlib.Polynomial.AnalyticApproximation`.

signature: NLAlib.re_fourier_one_mem_Icc (t : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi)) : ((fourier 1) t).re ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1
name: NLAlib.re_fourier_one_mem_Icc
doc:
Every cosine-circle argument lies in the closed unit interval.
Source: unit norm of Fourier characters; helper for `jackson-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_fourier_pair_eq_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T (F : ℂ → ℂ) {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (θ : ℝ) :
  (fourierCoeff (NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F) ↑k * (fourier ↑k) ↑θ +
        fourierCoeff (NLAlib.chebyshevCircleFunction F) (-↑k) * (fourier (-↑k)) ↑θ).re =
    NLAlib.chebyshevAnalyticCoeff F k * Polynomial.eval (Real.cos θ) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑k)
name: NLAlib.re_fourier_pair_eq_chebyshevAnalyticCoeff_mul_eval_T
doc:
Pairing opposite Fourier frequencies gives the positive Chebyshev series term.
Source: Trefethen, ATAP, Chapters 3 and 8 (`chebyshev-approx-analytic`, helper).

signature:
NLAlib.re_inner_euclideanLin_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℂ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) :
  (inner ℂ x ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin A) x)).re =
    ∑ j, hA.eigenvalues₀ j * ‖(NLAlib.complexEigenvectorCoordinates hA) x j‖ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.re_inner_euclideanLin_eq_sum
doc:
The real Hermitian quadratic form is the eigenvalue-weighted sum of squared
norms of its sorted complex coordinates. No real-vector restriction is imposed.
Source: the Hermitian spectral theorem, Horn–Johnson 2013, Theorem 4.2.6;
supports `courant-fischer`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_star_dotProduct_sq_mulVec_eq_sum_sq_norm_of_isHermitian.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (u : n → ℂ) : (star u ⬝ᵥ (A ^ 2).mulVec u).re = ∑ i, ‖A.mulVec u i‖ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.re_star_dotProduct_sq_mulVec_eq_sum_sq_norm_of_isHermitian

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_sum_sq_norm.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  (A : Matrix m n ℂ) : (A.conjTranspose * A).trace.re = ∑ i, ∑ j, ‖A i j‖ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.re_trace_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_sum_sq_norm
doc:
The real trace of the actual complex Gram matrix is the sum of squared entry norms.
Source: finite Gram expansion; supports `audit:combined`, `matrix-freedman` (partial).

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_diagonal_mul_conj_diagonal.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (U : ↥(Matrix.unitaryGroup ι ℂ)) (a b : ι → ℝ) :
  ((Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(a i)) * ((↑U * Matrix.diagonal fun j => ↑(b j)) * star ↑U)).trace.re =
    ∑ i, ∑ j, ‖↑U i j‖ ^ 2 * a i * b j
name: NLAlib.re_trace_diagonal_mul_conj_diagonal
doc:
A diagonal matrix times a conjugated diagonal matrix has trace given by
the squared unitary overlap weights. Source: separate eigenbases in
manuscript `lem:traceyoung`; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_eq_rank_of_isIdempotentElem.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (P : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hP : IsIdempotentElem P) : P.trace.re = ↑P.rank
name: NLAlib.re_trace_eq_rank_of_isIdempotentElem
doc:
The real trace of any complex idempotent matrix equals its actual rank.
Source: Mathlib's projection trace theorem, `sa:volume-theorem`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_eq_zero_iff_of_complex_posSemidef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {R : Matrix n n ℂ}
  (hR : R.PosSemidef) : R.trace.re = 0 ↔ R = 0
name: NLAlib.re_trace_eq_zero_iff_of_complex_posSemidef
doc:
Zero real complex trace characterizes the zero PSD matrix.
Source: manuscript `sa:rp-one-step`, absorbing residual.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_le_card_mul_norm_of_isHermitian.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) : A.trace.re ≤ ↑(Fintype.card n) * ‖A‖
name: NLAlib.re_trace_le_card_mul_norm_of_isHermitian
doc:
The real trace of a Hermitian matrix is at most dimension times its operator norm.
Source: spectral theorem and the eigenvalue norm bound; supports `matrix-freedman`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_le_re_trace_of_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A B : Matrix n n ℂ} (h : A ≤ B) :
  A.trace.re ≤ B.trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_le_re_trace_of_le
doc:
The real trace is monotone in complex matrix Loewner order.
Source: nonnegative trace of the PSD difference; supports `matrix-freedman`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_matrixExp_mul_unitary_conj.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (U : ↥(unitary (Matrix ι ι ℂ))) (H A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) :
  (NLAlib.matrixExp (↑U * H * (↑U).conjTranspose) * (↑U * A * (↑U).conjTranspose)).trace.re =
    (NLAlib.matrixExp H * A).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_matrixExp_mul_unitary_conj
doc:
The real part of the trace pairing of a matrix exponential and another
matrix is invariant under simultaneous unitary conjugation. Source: operator
derivations §7; atlas `golden-thompson` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_mul_diagonal_pow_mul_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (C : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hC : C.IsHermitian) (ev : ι → ℝ) {m l : ℕ} (hm : Even m) (hl : l ≤ m) :
  (C * (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(ev i)) ^ l * C * (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(ev i)) ^ (m - l)).trace.re ≤
    (C ^ 2 * (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(ev i)) ^ m).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_mul_diagonal_pow_mul_le
doc:
Even mixed powers in a Hermitian diagonal basis are bounded by the endpoint
quadratic trace. Negative eigenvalues and exponent zero are included.
Source: manuscript `lem:mixed`; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_mul_diagonal_pow_mul_mul_diagonal_pow.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (C : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (hC : C.IsHermitian) (ev : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℕ) :
  (C * (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(ev i)) ^ a * C * (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(ev i)) ^ b).trace.re =
    ∑ i, ∑ j, ‖C i j‖ ^ 2 * ev j ^ a * ev i ^ b
name: NLAlib.re_trace_mul_diagonal_pow_mul_mul_diagonal_pow
doc:
Two powers of a real diagonal matrix, separated by a Hermitian matrix,
have real trace equal to a sum weighted by squared complex entry norms.
Source: the eigenbasis expansion in manuscript `lem:mixed`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_mul_pow_mul_le_trace_sq_mul_pow.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (C H : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hC : C.IsHermitian) (hH : H.IsHermitian) {m l : ℕ} (hm : Even m) (hl : l ≤ m) :
  (C * H ^ l * C * H ^ (m - l)).trace.re ≤ (C ^ 2 * H ^ m).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_mul_pow_mul_le_trace_sq_mul_pow

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_nonneg_of_complex_posSemidef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {R : Matrix n n ℂ} (hR : R.PosSemidef) :
  0 ≤ R.trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_nonneg_of_complex_posSemidef
doc:
A PSD matrix has nonnegative real complex trace.
Source: manuscript `sa:rp-one-step`; audit Part VII.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_pow_eq_sum_eigenvalues_pow.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (r : ℕ) : (A ^ r).trace.re = ∑ i, hA.eigenvalues i ^ r
name: NLAlib.re_trace_pow_eq_sum_eigenvalues_pow
doc:
Every natural Hermitian power has real trace equal to the corresponding
power sum of its real eigenvalues. Source: spectral theorem; supports the
integer trace method for `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_pow_mul_pow_eq_sum_overlap.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A B : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (r s : ℕ) :
  (A ^ r * B ^ s).trace.re =
    ∑ i,
      ∑ j, ‖↑(star hA.eigenvectorUnitary * hB.eigenvectorUnitary) i j‖ ^ 2 * hA.eigenvalues i ^ r * hB.eigenvalues j ^ s
name: NLAlib.re_trace_pow_mul_pow_eq_sum_overlap
doc:
Products of natural Hermitian powers have real trace given by the
overlap weights of their two eigenbases. Source: separate spectral
decompositions in manuscript `lem:traceyoung`; supports
`noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_pow_nonneg_of_even.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {r : ℕ} (hr : Even r) : 0 ≤ (A ^ r).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_pow_nonneg_of_even
doc:
Every even natural Hermitian trace moment is nonnegative. Source:
the real eigenvalue power sum; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_pow_nonneg_of_posSemidef.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) (r : ℕ) : 0 ≤ (A ^ r).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_pow_nonneg_of_posSemidef
doc:
Every natural PSD trace power is nonnegative. Source: its nonnegative
eigenvalues; supports `noncommutative-khintchine`.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_sub_mul_sub_pow_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (H K : Matrix ι ι ℂ)
  (hH : H.IsHermitian) (hK : K.IsHermitian) {m : ℕ} (hm : Even m) :
  ((H - K) * (H ^ (m + 1) - K ^ (m + 1))).trace.re ≤ ↑(m + 1) / 2 * ((H - K) ^ 2 * (H ^ m + K ^ m)).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_sub_mul_sub_pow_le
doc:
**Polynomial trace mean-value inequality.** At every odd power `m+1`,
where `m` is even, the Hermitian difference is bounded by the average of
the two endpoint quadratic traces. Source: manuscript `lem:meanvalue`;
supports `noncommutative-khintchine`. The matrices may fail to commute.

signature:
NLAlib.re_trace_sub_sq_mul_pow.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (H K : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (m : ℕ) :
  ((H - K) ^ 2 * H ^ m).trace.re = (H ^ (m + 2)).trace.re + (H ^ m * K ^ 2).trace.re - 2 * (H ^ (m + 1) * K).trace.re
name: NLAlib.re_trace_sub_sq_mul_pow

doc:
**Randomized SVD with a Gaussian test matrix** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD`, Algorithm
RSVD; HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case): if `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix,
`t ≥ k + 2`, and `Q ω` has a.s. orthonormal columns with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then
`E‖A − QQᵀA‖_F² ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²` (`‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F² = frobSq S₂` via the block SVD).
`rsvd_main` with its Gaussian hypotheses `hunit`, `hinv`, `hZi` discharged. The integrability
hypothesis `hXi` is also removed: when the error is not integrable its Bochner integral is `0`
and the (nonnegative) bound holds trivially. No measurability of `Q` is required.
Deviation: `n`, `k`, `r`, `r'`, `t` are `Fin` (the Gaussian law of `Ω` and the block lemmas of
`Gaussian/Conditioning.lean` live on `Fin`); the row type `m` and the column type `q` of `Q`

signature: NLAlib.singularValues {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.singularValues
doc:
The singular values `σ₀ ≥ σ₁ ≥ ⋯ ≥ 0` of a real matrix, zero-indexed, padded with zeros:
`σ k = √(λ_k(AᵀA))` for `k < n` and `σ k = 0` for `k ≥ n`. Defined as Mathlib's
`LinearMap.singularValues` of `Matrix.toEuclideanLin A`. Atlas `svd`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6; HMT 2011, §2.1). Deviation: zero-indexed, indexed by `ℕ`.
atlas: svd-def

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_add_add_le {m n : ℕ} (A B : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (i j : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues (A + B) (i + j) ≤ NLAlib.singularValues A i + NLAlib.singularValues B j
name: NLAlib.singularValues_add_add_le
doc:
**Weyl's inequality for singular values.** `σ_{i+j}(A + B) ≤ σ_i(A) + σ_j(B)` for real
`m × n` matrices (zero-indexed). Horn–Johnson 2013, §7.3 (Cor 7.3.5, label to verify); Bhatia
1997, Thm III.2.1 (Hermitian eigenvalue form). Audit G0 B2; atlas `weyl-mirsky`.
atlas: weyl-mirsky

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_add_le_add_specNorm {m n : ℕ} (A E : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues (A + E) k ≤ NLAlib.singularValues A k + NLAlib.specNorm E
name: NLAlib.singularValues_add_le_add_specNorm
doc:
**Weyl perturbation bound, upper side.** `σ_k(A + E) ≤ σ_k(A) + ‖E‖₂`. Horn–Johnson 2013,
§7.3 (Cor 7.3.5, label to verify). Audit G0 B3; atlas `weyl-mirsky`.

signature: NLAlib.singularValues_antitone {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : Antitone (NLAlib.singularValues A)
name: NLAlib.singularValues_antitone

`k < min m n`. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_le_of_forall_mem {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) (W : Submodule ℝ (Fin n → ℝ))
  (hW : n ≤ Module.finrank ℝ ↥W + k) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hAW : ∀ x ∈ W, A.mulVec x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x ≤ c ^ 2 * x ⬝ᵥ x) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k ≤ c

§7.3 (Thm 7.3.8, label to verify). Audit G0 B1; atlas `courant-fischer`. The hypothesis
`0 ≤ c` covers `k ≥ n`, where `σ_k = 0`.

signature:

signature:
NLAlib.sketch_decomp.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3} {r : Type u_4}

NLAlib.slepian_inequality.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} {Ω' : Type u_3} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  [MeasurableSpace Ω'] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {Q : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω'} (X : ι → Ω → ℝ) (Y : ι → Ω' → ℝ)
  (hX : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => X t ω) P)
  (hY : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => Y t ω) Q) (hX0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ∂P = 0)
  (hY0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y t ω ∂Q = 0) (hvar : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ^ 2 ∂P = ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y t ω ^ 2 ∂Q)
  (hinc : ∀ (s t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), (X s ω - X t ω) ^ 2 ∂P ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω'), (Y s ω - Y t ω) ^ 2 ∂Q) (τ : ℝ) :
  P {ω | τ < ⨆ t, X t ω} ≤ Q {ω | τ < ⨆ t, Y t ω}
name: NLAlib.slepian_inequality
doc:
**Slepian's inequality.** Let `X` (on `(Ω, P)`) and `Y` (on `(Ω', Q)`) be centred Gaussian
processes indexed by a finite set, with equal variances `𝔼 Xₜ² = 𝔼 Yₜ²` and dominated
increments `𝔼 (Xₛ - Xₜ)² ≤ 𝔼 (Yₛ - Yₜ)²`. Then for every `τ`,
`P(τ < maxₜ Xₜ) ≤ Q(τ < maxₜ Yₜ)`.
Source: Slepian 1962; Vershynin 2018, Thm 7.2.1. Atlas: `slepian`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.slepian_tail_comparison`.
atlas: slepian

  (hY : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω t => Y t ω) Q) (hX0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ∂P = 0)
  (hY0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y t ω ∂Q = 0) (hvar : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ^ 2 ∂P = ∫ (ω : Ω'), Y t ω ^ 2 ∂Q)
  (hinc : ∀ (s t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), (X s ω - X t ω) ^ 2 ∂P ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω'), (Y s ω - Y t ω) ^ 2 ∂Q) (τ : ℝ) :
  P {ω | τ ≤ ⨆ t, X t ω} ≤ Q {ω | τ ≤ ⨆ t, Y t ω}
name: NLAlib.slepian_inequality_ge
doc:
**Slepian's nonstrict tail comparison.** For finite centred Gaussian vectors with
equal coordinate variances and dominated increments, `P(max X ≥ τ) ≤ Q(max Y ≥ τ)`.
Degenerate Gaussian laws are included. Slepian 1962; Vershynin 2018, Theorem 7.2.1;
atlas `slepian`.
atlas: slepian

signature:

doc:
The stochastic Lanczos quadrature estimate
`(1/m) ∑ₖ (Q_kᵀ g_k)ᵀ f(Q_kᵀ A Q_k) (Q_kᵀ g_k)` with test vectors `g_k = G(·, k)` and bases

Deviation: any bases `Q_k` (the error theorems require `K_q(A, g_k) ⊆ range Q_k`).

singular both sides are `0` (Mathlib's `M⁻¹ = 0` and `1 / 0 = 0`).

HMT 2011, proof of Prop A.3; Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Lemma B.4. Atlas:
`pinv-spectral-tail`, `inverse-wishart-spectral-moment` (helper). Generalised from
`Fin r × Fin k` to arbitrary finite index types. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.specNorm_inv_gram_eq`.

`frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset`, verbatim (block decomposition with `U₂ᵀU₂ = I`,

`range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`; index types other than the rank `Fin k` are arbitrary `Fintype`s.
Atlas `hmt-9-1-spectral` (assumed → proved).

    -(2 * Real.pi)⁻¹ * ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..2 * Real.pi, NLAlib.sawtoothError n t * deriv (fun s => g (x - s)) t

doc:
